kok: Christianity wngkha Jisu Khristo ni phwrwngmungrok tei bini langmani sakao rwgwi kaisa tongthar.
en: Christianity is a religion based on the life and teachings of Jesus Christ.

kok: Khorok 2 rarwjak ni slai phano kwbangkuk maninai borokrokbai, omo hayungni kaisa kotorkuk tongtharo khobjagu.
en: It is one of the world's major religions, with over 2 billion followers.

kok: Khristanrok poito khlayo Jisu wngkha kaitorni bwsla tei boh borokno bohrok ni sumsokrokni simi mwthangna bwgwi se boh oh swngcharo phayo.
en: Christians believe that Jesus is the Son of God and that he came to earth to save people from their sins.

kok: Bohrok abobo poito khlayo, boh kwthwino mechenwi chukha sakao kasakha.
en: They also believe that he rose from the dead and ascended into heaven.

kok: Christianity'o Jisu ni bagwi hamjakma wngkha jottoni slai nangkukmani bwkhak.
en: The importance of love for Jesus is central to Christianity.

kok: Khristanrokno bohrokni bebak bwkha, mang, phola, tei phan bai Kaitorno hamjakdi hwnwi sajagu.
en: Christians are called to love God with all their heart, soul, mind, and strength.

kok: Bohrok saksakno hamjakma hai bohrokni nokarini borokno bo hamjakdi hwnwi bo sajagu.
en: They are also called to love their neighbors as themselves.

kok: Ah hamjakma haino kaisa muchungma simiya, phiya abo kaisa langmani tongwrwngse.
en: This love is not just a feeling, but a way of life.

kok: Abono khairokma, hamjakma tei nakarma bai simi se phunugwi mano.
en: It is expressed through acts of kindness, compassion, and forgiveness.

kok: Chwng Jisu no hamjakphuru, aphuru chwng bono simi chini hamjakma phunukya, phiya aphuru chwng kaitorno bo chini hamjakma phunugo.
en: When we love Jesus, we are not only showing our love for him, but we are also showing our love for God.

kok: Tamni hwnmale chini sakao kaitorni kubui hamjakmani mari wngkha Jisu.
en: This is because Jesus is the perfect expression of God's love for us.

kok: Chwng Jisu no hamjakphuru, chwng chini bwkharokni bisingtwih kaitorni hamjakma manna bwkhak chini sak-sakrok khulukmani khlayo.
en: When we love Jesus, we are opening ourselves up to receive God's love into our hearts.

kok: Jisuni hamjakma wngkha chini langmarokno swlaimanai kaisa phankuplung phan.
en: The love of Jesus is a powerful force that can transform our lives.

kok: Omo chwngno khakamung, phan, tei tongkwchang rwui manu.
en: It can give us hope, strength, and peace.

kok: Omo chwngno buino nakarnani tei sak-sakno hamjaknani chubai manu.
en: It can help us to forgive others and to love ourselves.

kok: Horhapung phatima wngkha hapharni kaisa phangwnang tei swbaikhrupmannai phan.
en: Volcanic eruptions are a powerful and destructive force of nature.

kok: Abohrok kotorma swbaisurup khlaimanu, langma sokomorwimano, tei tongkhorokno phuisarwi mano.
en: They can cause widespread devastation, loss of life, and environmental upheaval.

kok: Horhapung phatimung no urpatimung bai mamang gwdaljagu, phiya abohrok naithokmung tei uanamung baibo gwdalwimanu.
en: While volcanic eruptions are often associated with danger, they can also be a source of beauty and wonder.

kok: Horhapung phatimano naywi naikhe khaswrangrima uanamung hai, tei wngmatwi horkepek kochokma naithothok hakungmari bo swnamwi mano.
en: The sight of a erupting volcano is a awe-inspiring sight, and the resulting lava flows can create stunning landscapes.

kok: Horhapung ni phatimungrok ha bisingo belai swkwlwkmung khlaima bagwi se wngu.
en: Volcanic eruptions are caused by the build-up of pressure beneath the Earth's surface.

kok: Jephuru ah swkwlwkmung belai kotor wngwi thahngo, aphuru magma habukur gerebwi phan bai sakatwi peplai phayo.
en: When this pressure becomes too great, the magma is forced up through the crust and erupts onto the surface.

kok: Horhapung phatimung ni tormung tei phan belai phrwi manu.
en: The size and intensity of a volcanic eruption can vary greatly.

kok: Baksa phatimung belai chikon tei kwrwngsa thayo simino kwrwngjak, phiya tei kubunirokkhe kotorma tei baksa-baksa bwkhakno swbaikhrubwi phano mano.
en: Some eruptions are relatively small and localized, while others can be massive and have a devastating impact on entire regions.

kok: Jottonislai swbaikhrupmannai horhapung phatima kwrwngma thayo thapla pirsama, harpek kochokma, tei tsunami tubuimano.
en: The most destructive volcanic eruptions can cause widespread ashfall, mudflows, and tsunamis.

kok: Bohrok bangla tei ha phano kuwakrwi mano.
en: They can also trigger earthquakes and landslides.

kok: Jottonislai hamya phatimungo, horhapung phatima sai-sai borokrokni langmarok naimano tei khok rarwjak-rarwjak rangno derarwimano.
en: In the worst cases, volcanic eruptions can claim thousands of lives and cause billions of dollars in damage.

kok: Aswk deramung tongphano, horhapung phatima hayungni geological tangraidani bagwi kaisa nangkuma bokcho.
en: Despite the risks, volcanic eruptions are an important part of the Earth's geological processes.

kok: Bohrok hayungni habukurno swlaywi kwtal ha swnamthani chuba'o.
en: They help to recycle the Earth's crust and create new landforms.

kok: Bohrok dalbidal buphang-uaphang tei malmatarokni bagwi nokrokbo thumwi rwo.
en: They also provide a home for a variety of plants and animals.

kok: India ni chikonsa kamio, Ram mungwi chwrai khoroksa tongmani.
en: In a small village in India, there lived a young boy named Ram.

kok: Ram khoroksa siyangwnang tei khatungjak chwrai, tei boh bini yaksiyagra hayungni bagwi swrwngna belai hamjago.
en: Ram was a bright and curious boy, and he loved to learn about the world around him.

kok: Salsa, Ram kami twih himwi thang tongphuru, chwlarok bodol kaisano, kotorma hakorkutugo samung tangwi tongma nugo.
en: One day, Ram was walking through the village when he saw a group of men working on a large pit.

kok: "Norok tamo khlai tong?" hwnwi Ram swngkha.
en: "What are you doing?" Ram asked.

kok: "Chwng kaisa watwitwi thumjaknai twikhor swnamwi tongu," hwnwi khoroksa chwla sakha.
en: "We're building a rainwater harvesting tank," one of the men said.

kok: "Omo chwngno balsal molo watwitwi rungnani chubanai, kwran molo obono no chwng samungo phwnangwi mano."
en: "This will help us to collect rainwater during the monsoon season, so that we can use it during the dry season."

kok: Ram muani chajakma hai wngwi thangkha.
en: Ram was fascinated.

kok: Boh oboni slai swkang waisaphano watwitwi no thumwi tonnani hwnwi khwnayakhu.
en: He had never heard of rainwater harvesting before.

kok: Boh ah chwlarokno no kwbangma kokrok swngkha, tei bohrok bo aboni twywi sanani belai khatungjak.
en: He asked the men many questions, and they were happy to answer them.

kok: Ram saimankha watwitwi thummung, watwini twino rungmani tei khatiani kaisa kwlai tei sosol lama.
en: Ram learned that rainwater harvesting is a simple and effective way to collect and store rainwater.

kok: Watwini twi kaisa kotorma hakorkuthugo rwngjago, amono haino hano khurwi no swnamjago.
en: The rainwater is collected in a large pit, which is usually dug in the ground.

kok: Oh hakorkuthuk kaisa twimisimanya mwnwi bai arirwjak, aroni twino kochok thangnani simi kasonani bagwi, abo harpek eba holongbwthap bai arirwjak.
en: The pit is lined with a waterproof material, such as clay or concrete, to prevent the water from seeping out.

kok: Oh watwitwi thummung ni twikhor kamini kuwa ganao no manthogo, aroni twino kwlaikhe naharwi mannani bagwi.
en: The rainwater harvesting tank is usually located near the village well, so that the water can be easily accessed.

kok: Oh twi nwngnani, songnani, tukunani, tei maikhulrokno twi lunani bagwi samungo phwnangjagu.
en: The water can be used for drinking, cooking, bathing, and watering crops.

kok: India'o khorok 1.3 rarwjakni slai phano kwbangkuk borokrok tongu, tei abo hayungni bising jottnislai kwbangkuk borok bangthani nwi beremo kwlayu.
en: India has a population of over 1.3 billion people, and it is the second most populous country in the world.

kok: Nukhung chaplainani no twywi haphang bisi kwdwkma romwi samung khlai phai tongu, phiya tabuk phano oh jwngjal kotorni kagwimanyakhu.
en: The government has been working to promote family planning for many years, but the issue is still a major challenge.

kok: India ni kwbang achaimungni ungkulugo kwbangma kokbubak tongu.
en: There are a number of factors that contribute to the high birth rate in India.

kok: Kaisa kokbubak hwnkhe nukhung chaplanani bagwi aswk rwngswrwngmung tei kokpirmung kwrwi khu.
en: One factor is the lack of access to education and information about family planning.

kok: India ni kwbangma borokrokno contraception ni juda-juda raidarokno saimanyakhu, eba bohrok abo samungo phwnangnani phano kirijagwimanu.
en: Many people in India do not know about the different methods of contraception, or they may be afraid to use them.

kok: Tei kaisa kokbubak hwnkhe kotor nukhungrokno chajakukmungni hukumu.
en: Another factor is the cultural preference for large families.

kok: India ni baksa-baksa bwkhago, kwbangma bwsarok tongmani kaisa tongboromni mari haikhese naisikjago.
en: In some parts of India, it is seen as a status symbol to have many children.

kok: Nukhung chaplainani no tisana bagwi, haphang kwbangma tangbwtang naharkha.
en: The government has implemented a number of programs to promote family planning.

kok: Ah tangbwtangrogo magwnang eba chubachrujak contraception bakmani, nukhung chaplainani kokchana bagwi rwngswrwngmung tei kokbiti yapharmani, tei borokrokno kwlaikheno sterilized wngnanirok khobjago.
en: These programs include providing free or subsidized contraception, offering education and counseling about family planning, and making it easier for people to get sterilized.

kok: Haiphano, oh tangbwtangrok aswk bwthai tubuimanliya.
en: However, these programs have had limited success.

kok: India'o Nukhung chaplanani kokno pirnani bagwi kwbangma kasumung tongo.
en: There are a number of challenges to promoting family planning in India.

kok: Kaisa kasumung hwnkhe tangbwtangrokni belai kwbang morok.
en: One challenge is the high cost of the programs.

kok: Tei kaisa kasumung hwnkhe nukhung chaplainani phasing baksa-baksa tongthar bodolrokni simi kebengmung.
en: Another challenge is the resistance to family planning from some religious groups.

kok: Teise, oh kokrokno tisanani bagwi thwngwrwng hapharni mungsa saktharmung bo kwrwi.
en: Additionally, there is a lack of political will to address the issue.

kok: India'o bisi kwdwkma romwi no nukhung chaplainani kok kaisa kokbanglaimung ni kokhak wngwi phai tongu.
en: Family planning in India has been a topic of debate for many years.

kok: Bisi 1976'o, Barot haphang ah kokbanglaijaknai National Emergency Act Passed khlaikha, aboni twywi chwla tei bwrwirokni sakao bohrokni muchungma kwrwi twtwi bwchwlwi bwtharma tangbwtang phwnangjakha.
en: In 1976, the Indian government passed the controversial National Emergency Act, which imposed a forced sterilization program on men and women.

kok: Oh tangbwtangrok belaino sejajakha paithago abo Indian Supreme Court bai rosai naharjakha.
en: This program was met with widespread resistance and eventually overturned by the Indian Supreme Court.

kok: Laithangnai bisirokni bising, Barot haphang nukhung chaplaimani bwkhak teibo swkangnainai yaprirok naharkha.
en: In recent years, the Indian government has taken a more progressive approach to family planning.

kok: Bisi 2010'o, haphang National Family Planning tangbwtang chengkha, aboni bisingtwi jotto barot haniborokrokno magwnang suta oknangya khlaima tei bwchwlwi bwtharma sebukrok bakjakha.
en: In 2010, the government launched the National Family Planning Program, which provides free contraception and sterilization services to all Indian citizens.

kok: Ah tangbwtangni bisingtwi Barot haktorni bwsa chuwi manmungni wngmarino khaithani bwthai kahamno mankha, haiphano tabukbo obo jwngjal bai kwrangjakhu, sana thangkhe omoni twywi awaimung tei seb-sab mannani lamarok aswk kwrwi.
en: The program has been successful in reducing the fertility rate in India, but it still faces challenges, such as a lack of awareness and access to services.

kok: Baroto nukhung chaplainani no twywi jottonislai sosol kebengmungrok hwnkhe nukhung chaplaiani hamkraino twywi aswk awaimungrok kwrwikhu .
en: One of the most important challenges to family planning in India is the lack of awareness about the benefits of family planning.

kok: Barot ni kwbangma hiksainwirok poito khlayo jeswk mansak chwrai khlainani abo borokni khlaithaise hwnwi.
en: Many Indian couples believe that it is their duty to have as many children as possible.

kok: Oh poitorok hukumu tei tongtharni raidarok bai teibo rakrwjagu.
en: This belief is often reinforced by cultural and religious norms.

kok: Nukhung chaplainani thangthani tei kaisa kebengmung hwnkhe seb-sab mannani lamarok aswk kwrwi.
en: Another challenge to family planning is the lack of access to services.

kok: Kami amchairogo, nukhung chaplainani sakhamnokrok kaisa-kusu eba kwrwi swchwkno hwnwi manu.
en: In rural areas, there are often few or no family planning clinics.

kok: Obo hiksainwirokno nangwi tongmani seb-sab naharnani thani jwngjalo khiklayu.
en: This makes it difficult for couples to access the services they need.

kok: Oh jwngjalrokni bisingo bo Barot haphang barotni haniborokrokno nukhung chaplainani seb-sabrokno manthokrwnani bwkhak kwrakhe saktharjak.
en: Despite these challenges, the Indian government is committed to providing family planning services to all its citizens.

kok: Navratri ni salchuku'o, Parvati mungwi khoroksa bwrwi sikli hai hwnwi sajakha je boh khorok chwla bwsa no bahnai, ah chwla ulo khoroksa mungkotor bubagra wngnai.
en: On the ninth day of Navratri, a young woman named Parvati was told that she would give birth to a son who would become a great king.

kok: Boh belai tongthokjakha, tei boh bwsa bahna bagwi jugalina chengkha.
en: She was overjoyed, and she began to prepare for her delivery.

kok: Navratri ni salchi'o, Parvati bwsa bahmungo thangkha.
en: On the tenth day of Navratri, Parvati went into labor.

kok: Boh kwbangma dar romwi bwsa bahmungo tongkha, paithago, boh khoroksa naithok chwla kwlwibwsa no bahkha.
en: She labored for many hours, and finally, she gave birth to a beautiful baby boy.

kok: Boh bono Shiva hwnwi mung pharkha, tei boh saimano ulo boh khoroksa mungkotor bubagra wngwi bini talikha'o swijakno no supungnai.
en: She named him Shiva, and she knew that he would fulfill his destiny to become a great king.

kok: Shiva khoroksa kwrak tei kiriya chwla sikla wngwi torwi phaikha.
en: Shiva grew up to be a strong and courageous young man.

kok: Boh homnino kubuni borokrokno chubana bwkhak tiyar tongu, tei boh bini sosolmung tei khairokmung ni bagwi sinijagu.
en: He was always willing to help others, and he was known for his fairness and compassion.

kok: Boh daktino lukurokni bisingo sinijaknani chengkha, lukurokbo bini thani twidulmung tei twiphangni bagwi naichomlaikha.
en: He quickly became a popular figure among the people, and they looked to him for guidance and leadership.

kok: Salsa, Shiva bolong bisingtwi himwi thangwi tongphuru bo kaisa dagaitrokni bodolrok kami'o choprobwi tongma nukha.
en: One day, Shiva was walking through the forest when he came across a group of bandits who were attacking a village.

kok: Shiva daktino samungo bakhwlaikha, tei bo ah dagaitrok bai bulaikha.
en: Shiva quickly jumped into action, and he fought off the bandits.

kok: Kamini lukurok belai khaphurjakha Shiva bohrokno mwthangmani bagwi, tei bohrok bono swngkha bohrokni bubagra wngdi hwnwi.
en: The villagers were grateful to Shiva for saving them, and they asked him to become their king.

kok: Shiva bubagra wngna bagwi gosi naharkha, tei bo ah ha no bisi kwdwkma romwi elem tei kubuima bai naikolkha.
en: Shiva agreed to become king, and he ruled the kingdom wisely and justly for many years.

kok: Boh khoroksa khakaham tei khairokma gwnang bubagra wngkha, tei boh homnino bini borokni nangkukmarok bwskango puila tonikha.
en: He was a kind and compassionate ruler, and he always put the needs of his people first.

kok: Indira Gandhino puila tei tabukswk jora bwrwirokni bisingo baraot hani montri bokhorok chalangnai.
en: Indira Gandhi was the first and only woman to serve as Prime Minister of India.

kok: Bo 1917 bisio kaisa munggwnang thwnggwrwng nukhungo achaikha, tei bupha Jawaharlal Nehru, bono Barot hani puila Montri Bokhorok.
en: She was born in 1917 into a prominent political family, and her father, Jawaharlal Nehru, was the first Prime Minister of India.

kok: Indira Gandhi Barot tei England hao rwngswrwngkha tei bisi 1942'o Feroze Gandhi bai kaijakha.
en: Indira Gandhi was educated in India and England, and she married Feroze Gandhi in 1942.

kok: Bohrokni khoroknwi bwsa chwla wngjakha, Rajiv tei Sanjay.
en: They had two sons, Rajiv and Sanjay.

kok: Gandhi bini thwngkwrwngni langma bisi 1955 ni simi chengkha, aphuruno bo Barotni kerongchapnogo chongjago.
en: Gandhi began her political career in 1955, when she was elected to the Indian Parliament.

kok: Bini buphani haphango boh dalbidal bedego montrirokbo chalangkha, tei bisi 1966'o bini bupha thwimani yagulo boh montri bokhorok wngkha.
en: She served in various ministerial positions in the government of her father, and in 1966 she became Prime Minister after his death.

kok: Gandhi khoroksa belaikhe kok cherjaknai borok tongmani, bini tangbitirok homanino sejajago.
en: Gandhi was a controversial figure, and her policies were often criticized.

kok: Boh saksakni phanno simi phwnango tei batainairokno swkwlwgu hwnwi koksilchamung bo rwjago.
en: She was accused of being authoritarian and of suppressing dissent.

kok: Haiphano, bo khoroksa bumung gwnang ojama bo hwnjagu tei Barot hano kwtalkhe swnamnani tei oh hani borokrokni langmano hamsarwmani bagwi borombo rwjago.
en: However, she was also a popular leader, and she is credited with modernizing India and improving the lives of its people.

kok: Gandhi bisi 1984'o bini sakmwrwknairokbaino bwtharjakha.
en: Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards in 1984.

kok: Bini achukthaino bini bwsla Rajiv Gandhi naharkha .
en: She was succeeded by her son, Rajiv Gandhi.

kok: Gandhini langma tei samungbwtang belaino jwngjal tei kebengmungbai kupulwng, phiya boh bini kahamkuk ni imang yakarliya.
en: Gandhi's life and career were marked by many challenges, but she never gave up on her dream of a better India.

kok: Malgudi mungwi kaisa chikonsa aoli'o, Ramasamy mungwi khoroksa rangchakwrak Police inspector tongmani.
en: In the small town of Malgudi, there was a corrupt police inspector named Ramasamy.

kok: Boh homnino boh rommani borokrokni thani yaksak naharu, tei boh bini phan no borok rokno sikirinani tei chekeleknani bagwi bo phwnangu.
en: He would often take bribes from the people he arrested, and he would also use his power to harass and intimidate people.

kok: Salsa, Krishnan mungwi khoroksa chwla sikla no bini chayakhlaima kwrwi twtwino bono Ramamsamy romkha.
en: One day, Ramasamy arrested a young man named Krishnan for a crime he did not commit.

kok: Krishnan majra kwrwi se, haiphano Ramasamy bono khwnana se gosiliya.
en: Krishnan was innocent, but Ramasamy refused to listen to him.

kok: Boh Krishnan ni thani yakbara rwui rang sankha, Krishan jephuru bono rinani gosiliya, Ramasamy bono aphuru alongo daui rwkha.
en: He demanded a bribe from Krishnan, and when Krishnan refused to pay, Ramasamy threw him in jail.

kok: Krishnan ni bupha khoroksa bigra chuwainaisa, boh bwsla no alongnokni karinani bagwi belai muchungsukjakha.
en: Krishnan's father, a poor farmer, was desperate to get his son out of jail.

kok: Boh Ramasamy bai malainani thangkha tei bono Krishnan no phiyokdi hwnwi koikha, haiphano Ramasamy gosiliya.
en: He went to see Ramasamy and begged him to release Krishnan, but Ramasamy refused.

kok: Hwnkhe ah chuwainaisa aroni kaisa mwtainogo thangkha tei mwtai no chubajadi hwnwi surikha.
en: The farmer then went to the local temple and prayed to God for help.

kok: Teini salo, ah chuwainaisa mwtainok ni simi himwi thangphuru bo kaisa chibuk kotorma no lama laisutongmani nukha .
en: The next day, the farmer was walking home from the temple when he saw a large snake crossing the road.

kok: Ah chuwainaisa chibukno belai kirijagu, phiya boh saimano boh bini bwsla no chubana bagwi mungsaswk khaina nangnai hwnwi.
en: The farmer was afraid of snakes, but he knew that he had to do something to help his son.

kok: Boh chibukno khochakha tei police station'o twlang thangkha.
en: He picked up the snake and carried it to the police station.

kok: Jephuru Ramasamy chibukno nukha, bo kirijakha.
en: When Ramasamy saw the snake, he was terrified.

kok: Khajani [yachaksoknai ni mung], ang kha khwlayo nini kaham kwrwng jorao no o koktun sogwi khana hwnwi.
en: Dear [Recipient Name], I hope this letter finds you well.

kok: Ang nono chini khamparni simi suihoro, taklai bisi o maithai belaino kwbang mankha.
en: I am writing to you from our family farm, where the harvest has been good this year.

kok: Chwng belai khasrangjak amoswk kwbang maithai mwithai kaiwi manmani bagwi, tei bwskang bisi o amo haino khwlaiphinai hwnwi uansogo.
en: We are grateful for the bountiful crops that we have been able to grow, and we are looking forward to a successful year ahead.

kok: Ang tini nono suihorma khe clean India Campaign ni samung khwlaimano twywi sana bagwise.
en: I am writing to you today to tell you about my experience with the Clean India campaign.

kok: Nwngbo sio, Clean India Campaign khwlai mani abo India ha gwnangwi kwchwng khe tongnani tei khithairogno kwchwng khe tongnani abono twywise samung khwlai jago.
en: As you know, the Clean India campaign is a nationwide effort to promote cleanliness and sanitation in India.

kok: O pirmungo chengphuru ni simino ang kubuljak, tei chini hodao puila kaham swlaijakmung nukha.
en: I have been involved in this campaign since its inception, and I have seen firsthand the positive impact that it has had on our community.

kok: Bebakni slai hamkuk mani Clean India Campaign song samung khwlai ma khe kwchwng khe tongmani abo bwswk joratwi nang abono simung rwna naima se.
en: One of the most important things that the Clean India campaign has done is to raise awareness of the importance of cleanliness.

kok: Lukurok tabuk teibo sikha hamya manwino boro khibinai, tei bohrok sakni kamino kwchwng khwlaina bagwi bohrok teibo sakthar kha.
en: People are now more aware of the need to dispose of waste properly, and they are more willing to take action to keep their communities clean.

kok: Tei kaisa Clean India Campaign song samung khwlai ma khe bohrok manwi hamya tonijaknai bago bohrokni kamino kwchwng khwlai thanio chukthwng hwnwi.
en: Another important thing that the Clean India campaign has done is to provide resources to help people clean up their communities.

kok: Haphang song manwi hamya thumwi khibijaknai tei recycling programrokni bagwi rang bo rwi tongo, tei khithaini samung khwlaina muchungnairogno bo phwrwngjagwi tongo.
en: The government has provided funding for new garbage collection and recycling programs, and it has also provided training for people who want to become sanitation workers.

kok: Clean India Campaign khwlai mani bwthai wng kha, chini kamirok tei khithairok swkang ni slai chwngkuk kha.
en: As a result of the Clean India campaign, our community is cleaner and more sanitary than ever before.

kok: Onam Barot haktorni Kerala haste'o palaijaknai kaisa maital tisama ter.
en: Onam is a harvest festival celebrated in the Indian state of Kerala.

kok: Oh jorao nukhung kaisa tei bayapchari rokbai malaywi kaham maitalno twywi tongthoklaimani jora.
en: It is a time for family and friends to come together and celebrate the good harvest.

kok: Oh ter salchi romwi khwlaijago tei kaisa-kaisa salo dalbidal samung tei hukumu raidarok bai palaijagu.
en: The festival lasts for ten days, and each day is filled with different activities and traditions.

kok: Onamni kaisa nangkukmani hukumu wngkha Vallamkali eba chibuk rung bataimung.
en: One of the most important traditions of Onam is the Vallamkali, or snake boat race.

kok: Oh rung bataimung Pampa twimao khwlaijagu.
en: This is a boat race that takes place on the River Pampa.

kok: Oh rung belai kolok tei khochor, tei dalbidal khumbwlairokbai sajukjak.
en: The boats are long and narrow, and they are decorated with flowers and leaves.

kok: Oh rung bataimung belaino kutuk bataimung, tei naywi naikhe belai tongthothokbo wngo.
en: The race is very competitive, and it is a lot of fun to watch.

kok: Onamni tei dalsa nangkukmani hukumu wngkha Pookalam eba khumbarni dalbidal naithok swnamung.
en: Another important tradition of Onam is the Pookalam, or flower rangoli.

kok: Oh khumni rikmung belaino naithokthok wngo tei nok bwskango obo swnamjago.
en: This is a beautiful design made out of flowers that is placed in front of the house.

kok: Pookalamni bisingtwino mwtai tei mwtaijwkrokno lamsogo tei oboni bisingtwino okra-chakra roknobo borom rwjago.
en: The Pookalam is a way to welcome the gods and goddesses, and it is also a way to show respect to the elders.

kok: Onam ter phuru chalaimung tei tongthoklaimung wngo.
en: Onam is a time for feasting and celebration.

kok: Oh tero dalbidal chamung chajago romdi mai, ah tei dalokrok.
en: There are many traditional dishes that are eaten during the festival, such as rice, fish, and vegetables.

kok: Oro rwchapmung tei mwsamungbo wngo.
en: There is also a lot of singing and dancing.

kok: Ah tongkwthar kobolmungrok ah rwchapmung sakao wngkha kuar tei dalkwbang.
en: The influences of religion on music are vast and varied.

kok: Ah diyaimung rwchapma simi kwcham mwtainokrok ah birsama khorangkahamrok gospel rwchapmungrok bwkhak, rwchapmung kaisa kwdwkma tongkwtahr poitotok tei khanangjakrok swbaikhrubwi sama bwkhak.
en: From the chanting of hymns in ancient temples to the soaring melodies of gospel songs, music has long been used to express religious beliefs and emotions.

kok: Kwbangma tongkwtharrokni bising, rwchaomung kaisa ah chukhani kok bai kwrwngna bwkhka kaisa lama haikhe nukjakha.
en: In many religions, music is seen as a way to connect with the divine.

kok: Ah khorangrok tei kokyaprirok rwchapmung kaisa sinai simanwi kirima tei khlumjaknai swnam mano, tei ah khwnanai rokno kaisa kuchuk milik sichajak rwkamung bwkhak chubai mano.
en: The sounds and rhythms of music can create a sense of awe and reverence, and can help to transport the listener to a higher plane of consciousness.

kok: Phunukmari karwi, Hinduism bising, yoga wngkha kaisa sakmang bwkhak rwchapmung wansukukma wngkha.
en: For example, in Hinduism, music is considered to be a form of yoga.

kok: Ah kirtan loi khlaimung bai, eba tongkwthar rwchapmung, ah khorokno kwthar khai chubma bwkhak sajakha tei ah chukhani kok bwkhak bwkha khulukma.
en: The practice of kirtan, or devotional chanting, is said to help to purify the mind and open the heart to the divine.

kok: Buddhism bising, rwchapmung uramuram phwnangjak wngkha iko kaisa asonkhaimani tomung, ah khorokno naisikma bwkhak chubamani tei kaisa tongrem kwchang tei shanti bagwi tubumani.
en: In Buddhism, music is often used as a form of meditation, helping to focus the mind and bring about a state of calm and tranquility.

kok: Jora rwmani bising omo pholagwdaljak tangmung bwkhak, rwchapmung hodarwk tei thwngrwngrwk swimarirok nikuma bwkhak phwnangjak bo wngmano.
en: In addition to its spiritual role, music can also be used to address social and political issues.

kok: Ah luku manthai ninangrimung bising, phunukmari karwi, kaisa phangwnang tangmung rwchapmung tamjakha borokno samungo thepama bising tei bohrokno mankubuini bagwi bulaina bwkhak khasrangrwkha.
en: In the civil rights movement, for example, music played a powerful role in mobilizing people and inspiring them to fight for justice.

kok: Ah Martin Luther King Jr, Mahjalia jacksongni rwchapmungrok, tei kubunrok khorang rwma bwkhak chubakha ah khajamungrok tei African Americans ni imangrok, tei kaisa teibo haino tei makubui dopha bagwi tubuna bwkhak chubakha.
en: The songs of Martin Luther King Jr, Mahalia Jackson, and others helped to give voice to the hopes and dreams of African Americans, and helped to bring about a more just and equitable society.

kok: "Ang poito khwlaywi manya chwng tini India ni chamungrokno songnani maswrwngnai" hwnwi bisi 10 omorni Priya tongthokjagwi sakha.
en: "I can't believe we're going to be learning how to cook Indian food today," said 10-year-old Priya excitedly.

kok: Oh salno boh belaino khatungkhajakhe naisingjak bono phwrwngnai, Ms. Singh, bohrokno dalbidal hukumu bodolni chamung swrwnglainai hwnwi sakhlaimani yagulo. "Ang Indiani chamungrogrokno waisa phano chajakya kho, " hwnwi Priyani kiching, Sam sakha. "Abo bahai?"
en: She had been looking forward to this day ever since her teacher, Ms. Singh, had announced that they would be doing a unit on different cultures. "I've never had Indian food before," said Priya's friend, Sam. "What's it like?"

kok: "Abo belaino kothok, " hwnwi Priya sakha "abo belaino thogu, moso yokma bo kwbang. Tei aro kwbangma dalbidalni mii swngjaknai tongo aroni bisingo saiwi naimano."
en: "It's delicious," said Priya "It's usually very flavorful, with a lot of spices. And there are so many different dishes to choose from."

kok: Rwngremrok nokganti'o sokkha, hake Ms. Singh bo jugalnani chengkha.
en: The class arrived at the kitchen, and Ms. Singh began to set up.

kok: "Tini chwng kaisa kwlai mui dal makhani no swnamlainai, " hwnwi boh sakha.
en: "Today, we're going to be making a simple dish called dal makhani," she said.

kok: "Abo kaisa mwibwtwi haise India'o belai chajago."
en: "It's a type of lentil soup that's very popular in India."

kok: Ms. Singh class no phunukha bahaikhe manwi-khwnwirok suh'ui oh muibwtwi songnai.
en: Ms. Singh showed the class how to measure out the ingredients and cook the lentils.

kok: Swrwngnairok bohrok kiching mui helep thani tei mwitwk kollai thani chubalaikha.
en: The students helped each other chop vegetables and stir the pot.

kok: Bohrok samung khwlai twtwi, bohrokni thokjakukmani chamungrogno twywi tei India ni chamungno bo chanai nayano hwnwi salaikha.
en: As they worked, they chatted about their favorite foods and what they were looking forward to trying in India.

kok: Dal makhani song baikha hwnkhe, bohrok chalaina bagwi achuklaikha.
en: When the dal makhani was finished, the students sat down to eat.

kok: Manthaini khatimung wngkha belai raida kaham aboni naharmung wngkha laibuma rwgwi swkwlwkjagwi phainai dopharokno kuchugo tisanani.
en: Reservation in India is a system of positive discrimination that aims to provide opportunities to historically disadvantaged groups.

kok: Omo kaisa uansokmungni sakao je oh dopharok agi phuru swkwlwkjagwi phaima bagwi, bui bai baksa bohrokno tisana bagwi juda chubamung nango.
en: It is based on the idea that these groups have been discriminated against in the past, and that they need special help in order to achieve equality.

kok: Kwbangma thayono manthaini khatimung khwlaijago, aro swrwngmungo, haba tangthanio, tei haphango bo abo khobjago.
en: Reservations are used in a number of areas, including education, employment, and government.

kok: Bohrokni manthaini sinimung bwlai nauimanno, aro kaisa bodolni borokrok simino manwi mano, bohrokni bodolno simino judakhe chongwi naharjago.
en: They can take the form of quotas, which set aside a certain number of places for members of a particular group, or of preferences, which give members of a particular group an advantage in selection.

kok: Manthai khatimungrokno twywi belai kokbanglaimung tongu, abono twywi kwbangma kaham tei hamya kwbangma kokrok sajaklayu.
en: Reservations are controversial, and there are a number of arguments for and against them.

kok: Baksa borok kheba sao abono teisa swnamna nangphinai hwnwi, tei manthaino manyarokni bagwi jora kaham rwna nangnai hakhese bohrok kuchugo kauimanai hwnwi sajago.
en: Some people argue that they are necessary to correct the effects of past discrimination, and that they provide an important opportunity for members of disadvantaged groups to improve their lives.

kok: Baksa ba sao manthaino khatimani abo kubun bodolrokni bagwi chaya hwnwi, tei bohrok manthaino manwi mangse tongna muichungo hwnwi.
en: Others argue that reservations are unfair to other groups, and that they create a sense of entitlement among the beneficiaries.

kok: Manthai khatimungno twywi kokbanglai mani abo phainai bisirogo bo banglaiwi no thangnai.
en: The debate over reservations is likely to continue for many years to come.

kok: Abobaino, bangrwrwk wngmabai manthaini khatimung nangsogo India o bebakno baksa khwlaina bagwi.
en: However, there is a growing consensus that reservations are an important tool for achieving equality in India.

kok: India ni tongraida bebak borokno no tongbaksa khwlayo, bohrokni dopha, tongk'thar, eba sir no naiya.
en: The Indian Constitution guarantees the right to equality for all citizens, regardless of their caste, religion, or gender.

kok: Chwla sikla wngwi, ang homni no kothomarok bai muani kwlaima je ani nanan ano sama hai.
en: As a young man, I was always fascinated by the stories that my grandmother used to tell me.

kok: Bo kothomasawui uanamasingsa rwmung kwlayo, tei bini khothoma homnino kubuni swngcharo ano rwkai twlango.
en: She had a wonderful gift for storytelling, and her tales always seemed to transport me to another world.

kok: Ani kaisa chajakmani kothoma hwnkhe khoroksa Srinivasa mungwi, bo kotorkuar swrwngnai tei nukuansuksinai.
en: One of my favorite stories was about a man named Srinivasa, who was a great scholar and philosopher.

kok: Srinivasa belai sijak je bono swngmung rwjakmani bo abono kokphirokwi mano.
en: Srinivasa was so wise that he could answer any question that was put to him.

kok: Salsa, bubagra Srinivasa ni ro phaikha tei bono mohai swngmung swngkha je tak sak jora kebo Kokphirok manyakhu: "langma ni kokmung tamo" Srivasa swrapsa wansukgrakha, tei bo sakha, "langma ni kokmung wng nini rwmungno naituknani.
en: One day, a king came to Srinivasa and asked him a question that no one had ever been able to answer: "What is the meaning of life" Srinivasa thought for a moment, and then he said, "The meaning of life is to find your gift.

kok: Langma ni naimung hwnkhe bagwi rohornani" bubagra Srinivasa ni kokphirokma no aswk khe chajakha je bo bono kotorma yakpai rwkha.
en: The purpose of life is to give it away" The king was so impressed with Srinivasa's answer that he gave him a large reward.

kok: Phiya Srinivasa yakpai no nana soiliya, bo sakha je bo agino elem bai belai yakpaijak je bo buino chubachu khai mankha hwnwi.
en: But Srinivasa refused the reward, saying that he had already been rewarded enough by the knowledge that he had helped someone else.

kok: Oh kothoma ano phwrwngkha je oh langma ni belai nangkukma manwi hwnkhe manwi-khwnwi sasokmani naitukma simiya, phiya nini rwmung naitukna se tei kubun bai baknani.
en: This story taught me that the most important thing in life is not to seek material possessions, but to find your gift and share it with others.

kok: Ang salsa Mysoreni lamtwi himwi thang phuru jephuru ang chwrai khoroksano noktharni lamani theken o achukjak nukphu.
en: I was once walking through the streets of Mysore when I saw a young boy sitting on the steps of a temple.

kok: Bo kabui tongo swlwgwi, tei ang bono jephuru tamo wngkha hwnwi swngkha, bo bini lama koro kha hwnwi ano sakha.
en: He was crying bitterly, and when I asked him what was wrong, he told me that he had lost his way.

kok: Ang bono Khairok kha tei bono chubakha bini nokni lama naitukthani.
en: I took pity on him and offered to help him find his way home.

kok: Chwng baksa khe swrapsani bagwi himkha, tei ang bono bini langmani twi swngkha.
en: We walked together for a while, and I asked him about his life.

kok: Bo ano sakha bo bini buma-bupha tei dagisong bai mysore ni phataro chikonsa kamio tongo hwnwi.
en: He told me that he lived with his parents and siblings in a small village outside of Mysore.

kok: Bo cricket thwngna hamjago hwnwi sakha tei bini imang khe salsa kaham cricket thwngkwrwng wngnani.
en: He said that he loved to play cricket and that he dreamed of one day becoming a professional cricketer.

kok: Ang bono sakha bo bini imangno mannai tumung bo samung kwrak tei yakarya'ui khlai tongkhe.
en: I told him that I was sure he would achieve his dream if he worked hard and never gave up.

kok: Chwng ulokhe bini nok mankha, tei ang tongthok kha bini buma-bupha songno bono nugui khakchangma manmano nugwi.
en: We eventually found his way home, and I was glad to see that his parents were so relieved to see him.

kok: Ambedkar Jayanti wngkha mohai sal India o terkhlaima tei kubun hakotorrokni hayung yaksiyagra Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar ni mukumu no borom rwi, khoroksa hodarwk swnamnai, raidakwrwng, tei thwngrwngrwk ojama je Indian ni yohkmung ninangrimung ni kaisa lekhathaih berepkong tei Inda ni raidabwchcap tangrwbai.
en: Ambedkar Jayanti is a day of celebration in India and other countries around the world to honor the memory of Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar, a social reformer, jurist, and political leader who was a key figure in the Indian independence movement and the architect of the Constitution of India.

kok: Ambedkar kaisa Dalit ni nukhungo achayo, kaisa borok bodol je tangwimanya hwnwi wansukjago India ni khil lam bai.
en: Ambedkar was born into a Dalit family, a group of people who were considered to be untouchables in the caste system of India.

kok: Bo phermung malaikha tei bini langma o kwrwngwi bo belai biyal manjakha, phiya bo bini imang no jesaphano wngthwng yakaliya je Indians no homan khainani.
en: He faced discrimination and hardship throughout his life, but he never gave up on his dream of equality for all Indians.

kok: Ambedkar wngkha bomtomgwnang rwngswrwngnai tei bo United States o thangwi Kerong doctrate ajikha Colombia University o.
en: Ambedkar was a brilliant student and went on to earn a doctorate in law from Columbia University in the United States.

kok: Bo London rangthong rwngnogo porijak tei khoroksa barrister bo wngkha.
en: He also studied at the London School of Economics and became a barrister.

kok: India o phirokma olo, Ambedkar khoroksa lekhathaih dagimung wngkha Indian yokmung ninangrimung thayo.
en: After returning to India, Ambedkar became a leading figure in the Indian independence movement.

kok: Bo khoroksa Indian National Congress ni adong wngjak, phiya paithago bodol bai kagwi thangpaikha tei bini sakni thwngrwngrwk motha swnamkha, Scheduled Castes Federation.
en: He was a member of the Indian National Congress, but he eventually broke away from the party and formed his own political organization, the Scheduled Castes Federation.

kok: Ambedkar wngkha khoroksa berepkhong lekhathaih India ni raidabwchap koksongsagramung khai thani.
en: Ambedkar was also a key figure in the drafting of the Constitution of India.

kok: Khil wngkha kaisa hodarwk lam India bising boro borokrok kwrak hodarwk rwngremrok bising bakjakha, khilrok hwnwi ringjakha.
en: Casteism is a social system in India in which people are divided into rigid social classes, called castes.

kok: Ah khil lam yapahang wngkha poitoni sakao je borok kaisa khatharjak khil bising achaikha tei je bohrokni khil kahthonmarok borokni hodarwk tongborom, occupation, tei khailaimung naiphunukmungrok.
en: The caste system is based on the belief that people are born into a certain caste and that their caste determines their social status, occupation, and marriage prospects.

kok: Khil bisirarok karwi Indian dophani kaisa bokcho wngkha tei kaisa kuthukuk sekrupma tongo Indian hukumu tei dopha sakao.
en: Casteism has been a part of Indian society for centuries and has had a profound impact on Indian culture and society.

kok: Ah khil lam tola khilrok kwthaiya khakjakmani bwkhak twlangkha, je rwng bwkhak sogwima, samungrok, tei kubun seprok gosiya wngkha.
en: The caste system has led to discrimination against lower castes, who have been denied access to education, jobs, and other opportunities.

kok: Laithangjak bisirok bising, ah khil lam sokomorna bwkhak chaitokmarok aro wngkha, phiya amo kaisa India bising kubui kebengmung torwkma.
en: In recent years, there have been efforts to abolish the caste system, but it remains a serious problem in India.

kok: 2018 bising, ah hodapharwk tangsitra tongmarirok haphangtang saimarikha je aro 40,000 sakao dorbkamung khil-yaphang bulaimamung wngkha Indiani bising.
en: In 2018, the National Crime Records Bureau reported that there were over 40,000 cases of caste-based violence in India.

kok: Khil wngkha kaisa kutuk tei jadrepodjak ongkhorma.
en: Casteism is a complex and multifaceted issue.

kok: Aro ah kebengmung bwkhak mungsa solution kwrwi, phiya omo wngkha nangkukma bwkhak choyai oh ongkhorma sirwmarok kasama bwkhak tei ganarwk samung khil khajakmani normani.
en: There is no easy solution to the problem, but it is important to continue to raise awareness of the issue and work towards eliminating caste discrimination.

kok: Obo nokgantini simi phaiui tongo, haini bagwi ang naitukphinani bachakha.
en: It’s coming from the kitchen, so I get up to investigate.

kok: Ang khotol kotoro twrwk twrwk makhwganw, hojak tongdi mungsa khorang khwlaiyatwi
en: I creep down the hallway, careful not to make a sound.

kok: Kechemeche khorang teibo torrwk
en: The clacking is getting louder.

kok: Ang nokgantini bwsup ganatwi naison naikha tei nukha ama sink ganao bwchaui phataro naisik tongo.
en: I peer around the corner into the kitchen and see Mum standing at the sink, staring out the window.

kok: Boh saktwi kajak tei kwlwijak. "Ama?" Ang swngkha.
en: She looks pale and shaken. “Mum?” I ask.

kok: Boh yaksi yagra uphilya wng tongkha.
en: She doesn’t turn around.

kok: “Ama, tamo wngkha?” Boh hama kolok uaisa nasakha tei ani mwkhang phasing uphilkha.
en: “Mum, what’s wrong?” She takes a deep breath and turns to face me.

kok: Bini mokol kotor kotor tei kirima gwnang wngjak.
en: Her eyes are wide and filled with fear.

kok: “Phataro mungsaswk tongo, ” boh sao. “mungsaswk kotor.”
en: “There’s something outside,” she says. “Something big.”

kok: Ang tailam phataro bini naisikmano rwgwi naisik naikha.
en: I follow her gaze out the window.

kok: Puilao, Ang mwgnsa nugwi manya wngmani.
en: At first, I don’t see anything.

kok: Phiya ulo, ang sampili kaisa lorimano nukha.
en: But then, I notice a movement in the shadows.

kok: Obo kaisa kotor, kosom mang tei obo nok phaising agogui tongo.
en: It’s a large, dark shape, and it’s moving towards the house.

kok: “Obo tamo?” Ang swngkha. Ama sao “Ang saimanya, ”. “Phaia obo kichinghai hwnwi ang khakaya.”
en: “What is it?” I ask. “I don’t know,” Mum says. “But I don’t think it’s friendly.”

kok: O mal manwi ganao sokphayo.
en: The creature gets closer.

kok: Obo kuchuk tei keram, yakung kolok, kwsagwnang.
en: It’s tall and slender, with long, spindly legs.

kok: Bini bwsak buikhumu kosombai kupulung, tei bini khorok kepher, ball kitinghai
en: Its body is covered in black fur, and its head is a smooth, round ball.

kok: Oboni mokol kwrwi, phiya ang kotor, kwplap khunji kainwi nugwi tongo.
en: It has no eyes, but I can see two large, pointed ears.

kok: “Chwng tamo khwlainani naiui tong?” Ang swngkha.
en: “What are we going to do?” I ask.

kok: “Chwng oroni nokhornani nangnai, ” ama sao. “Tabuk”
en: “We need to get out of here,” Mum says. “Now.”

kok: Chwng nokgantini kharwi achukjaknai khotolo phaiui paikha.
en: We run out of the kitchen and into the living room.

kok: “Ama! Apha!” ang kabo, “phataro mungsa tongo!”
en: “Mum! Dad!” I cry. “There’s something outside!”

kok: Apha TV ni simi nasikhoro. “Obo tamo?” Boh swngkha.
en: Dad looks up from the TV. “What is it?” he asks.

kok: “Ang saimanya, ” ama sao. “Phiya obo kotor tei yango phaiui tongo.
en: “I don’t know,” Mum says. “But it’s big and it’s coming this way.”

kok: Apha sofani simi bwchakha.
en: Dad gets up from the couch.

kok: “Chwng oroni nokhorwi thangnani nangnai, ” boh sao.
en: “We need to get out of here,” he says.

kok: Chwng jottono bwskangni dogar phasing khachiklaikha.
en: We all run for the front door.

kok: Ama doga phiyogwi rwkha tei chwng phatar phaising dolaikha.
en: Mum unlocks it and we rush outside.

kok: Oh mal manwi chinisai kisa ukologo
en: The creature is right behind us.

kok: Obo aswkkhe ganao je ang ani gwdwna ukologo bini hama kutungno chongwimanw.
en: It’s so close I can feel its hot breath on the back of my neck.

kok: Chwng malkhung phaising kharlaikha tei bisingo haplaikha.
en: We run to the car and get in.

kok: Apha engine chengkha tei chwng lahartwi nokhorwi phaikha.
en: Dad starts the engine and we peel out of the driveway.

kok: Oh mal manwi chini ukolok rwktharo, phiya chwng belai dojak.
en: The creature chases after us, but we’re too fast.

kok: Omo tamni hinba bohrok thwi nwngya.
en: This is because they do not feed on blood.

kok: Boni slai, bohrok khumrokni simi twikwtwi nwngo.
en: Instead, they feed on nectar from flowers.

kok: Bwrwi thampuirok, tei kubun digi, bohrok thwi nwngo.
en: Female mosquitoes, on the other hand, do feed on blood.

kok: Bwtwirok twihna bagwi bohrok thwi nango.
en: They need blood in order to produce eggs.

kok: Chwla thampurirok pohor bwkhak sotonjak wngkha, aswkno bohrok uramuramwi tailamrok tei duklamrok gana mano.
en: Male mosquitoes are attracted to light, so they are often found near windows and doors.

kok: Bohrok kolomtwi bahai tei C02 bwkhak khasotonma bo wngkha.
en: They are also attracted to the smell of sweat and CO2.

kok: Bwrwi thampuirok wngkha ah sollai manwirok bwkhak khasotonjakha, phiya bohrok borok thwi bising khatharjak sapulswnamjakrok bahai bwkhak bo sotonjakha.
en: Female mosquitoes are attracted to the same things, but they are also attracted to the smell of certain chemicals in human blood.

kok: Jephuru khoroska borokno kaisa bwrwi thampui uaro, bo ah bukur bising khuktwi sitogo.
en: When a female mosquito bites a human, she injects saliva into the skin.

kok: Oh khuktwi anticoagulants tonio, bomo ah thwi buthupmani simi kasogra khayo.
en: This saliva contains anticoagulants, which prevent the blood from clotting.

kok: Ah thampui hwnkhe ah thwi kusupbo.
en: The mosquito then sucks up the blood.

kok: Thampui warna motokmani tei torrwmani pher mano.
en: Mosquito bites can cause itching and swelling.

kok: Baksa tanghalokrok bisingm borok kaisa allergic wngmani pher bo mano.
en: In some cases, they can also cause an allergic reaction.

kok: Ah jottoni slai manthok allergic wngmani sapokthaih thampui uarmarok bwkhak wngkha bothrairok wngo.
en: The most common type of allergic reaction to mosquito bites is hives.

kok: Ah bothrairok wngkha kwchak, tisajak thaihmarok je ah bukur sakao peplao.
en: Hives are red, raised bumps that appear on the skin.

kok: Bohrok motokma eba belai sah'ui mano.
en: They can be itchy or painful.

kok: Manthokya tonghalok bising, thampui uarmarok teibo uansukrak kebengmungrok pher mano.
en: In rare cases, mosquito bites can cause more serious problems.

kok: Phunukmari kari, baksa borok kaisa bemar tubumani hamkrai mano ah uarma thayo.
en: For example, some people can develop an infection at the site of the bite.

kok: Baksa tonghalokrok bising, thampui uarma thwimung bwkhak haino dagi mano.
en: In some cases, mosquito bites can even lead to death.

kok: Ah kaham lama thampui uarmarok katina bwkhak wngkha kolok yaktwkrok tei pants jephuru nwng phataro thangkhe.
en: The best way to avoid mosquito bites is to wear long sleeves and pants when you are outdoors.

kok: Nwng yong kosorwma bo phwnangna nango.
en: You should also use insect repellent.

kok: Tumungno nwng thampui bai uarjakha, nwng uarma thayo kaisa kwchang sinna thepai mano ah motokmani tei torrwmani holirwi mano.
en: If you do get bitten by a mosquito, you can apply a cold compress to the bite to relieve the itching and swelling.

kok: Nwng kaisa kaisa allergic wngmani nukswkangmari holirwm bakhak kaisa ah-counter-sakao antihistamine bo nai mano.
en: You can also take an over-the-counter antihistamine to relieve the symptoms of an allergic reaction.

kok: Thampuirok wngkha bemar twinai nangkukma wngkha.
en: Mosquitoes are important carriers of disease.

kok: Bohrok kaisa dalbidal bermarok, malaria khobmani, dengue kulum, tei kormo kulum rohor mano.
en: They can transmit a variety of diseases, including malaria, dengue fever, and yellow fever.

kok: Ah chirasairok borok bisi thwgwi thwimungrok bagwi thampuirok bokjak wngkha.
en: Mosquitoes are responsible for the deaths of millions of people each year.

kok: Aro kwbangma manwirok tongo je ah thampui bangmanirok mwthakmung bwkhak khlaijak mano.
en: There are a number of things that can be done to control mosquito populations.

kok: Kaisa lama wngkha ah lombor thairok khairwnani boro thampuirok achai mano.
en: One way is to reduce the number of places where mosquitoes can breed.

kok: Omo twi bathajakmani sokornani tei mwikhwtwng phang sapsutra hakchalo khaimani bai khlaijak mano.
en: This can be done by draining standing water and clearing away vegetation.

kok: Tei kaisa lama thaimpui bangmani mwthakmung wngkha yongkuk thwithirok phwnangma.
en: Another way to control mosquito populations is to use insecticides.

kok: Yongkuk thwithirok thampui bwtharna bwkhak phwnangjak mano kanwi nokbisingrok tei patharok bai.
en: Insecticides can be used to kill mosquitoes both indoors and outdoors.

kok: Thampuirok wngkha kaisa kotor luku sakduk kebengmung.
en: Mosquitoes are a major public health problem.

kok: Haiphano, aro wngkha kwbangma manwirok je thampui bangmanirok mwkthakmung bwkhak khlaijak mano tei ah thampui- achaijak bemarok khairwi mano.
en: However, there are a number of things that can be done to control mosquito populations and reduce the risk of mosquito-borne diseases.

kok: Jephuru sakhan dukhu manjak wngkhak, ah sak phiyokjak lam thwi kuphur khotolste homarok ah ari bwkhak.
en: When tissue is injured, the body’s immune system sends white blood cells to the area.

kok: Oh khotolsterok sapulswnamjakrok yakaro je thwi twkrok pher phuarma bwkhka tei teibo hapmanjak wngkha.
en: These cells release chemicals that cause blood vessels to dilate and become more permeable.

kok: Omo bwtwi tei thwi kuphur khotolste bwkhak kwpla ongkhorma ah thwi twkrok tei ah sakhan dukhu manjak bisingo wngo.
en: This allows fluid and white blood cells to leak out of the blood vessels and into the injured tissue.

kok: Ah bwtwi sakmangrok kaisa sraisrai, twima torrwmani edema hwnwi ringjago.
en: The fluid forms a clear, watery swelling called edema.

kok: Ah thwi kuphur khotolsterok solomani bulaima bwkhak chubao tei bo sakhan piyakjak ongkhorma bwkhak.
en: The white blood cells help to fight infection and to remove damaged tissue.

kok: Bohrok sapulswnamjak bo yakarkha je ah kwtal sakhan torrwma jolirwma bai.
en: They also release chemicals that stimulate the growth of new tissue.

kok: Oh kwcham marirok chiring robomsamung chaksama, kutung, torrwmani, tei kiyorma wngkha
en: The classic signs of acute inflammation are redness, heat, swelling, and pain.

kok: Oh marirok thwi kochokma bangma bai pherjak tongo tei ah sakhan dukhu manjak bising sapulswnamjak yakarma tongo.
en: These signs are caused by the increased blood flow and the release of chemicals in the injured tissue.

kok: Chaksamarok ah thwi twkrok phuarma bai pherjak wngkha.
en: Redness is caused by the dilation of blood vessels.

kok: Tungma wngkha thwi kochokma bangma bai tei ah robomsama sapulswnamjakrok yakarma bai wngo.
en: Heat is caused by the increased blood flow and the release of inflammatory chemicals.

kok: Torrwmani wngkha ah bwtwi kwpla thwi twkrok ah sakhan dukhu manma simi pherjak wngkha.
en: Swelling is caused by the leakage of fluid from blood vessels into the injured tissue.

kok: Kiyorma wngkha pherjak ah yakarma bai robomsama sapulswnamjakrok tei ah torrwmani sepmung.
en: Pain is caused by the release of inflammatory chemicals and the pressure of the swelling.

kok: Chiring robomsamung wngkha kaisa kosong bokcho ah hammani tangsep.
en: Acute inflammation is a normal part of the healing process.

kok: Haiphano, tumungno omo kwrak eba kokphang, omo sakdukma sakhan paiyakmung mano.
en: However, if it is severe or prolonged, it can damage healthy tissue.

kok: Baksa tonghalokrok bising, chiring robomsamung kwdwk bemar bwkhak dagi mano, bomo kaisa kolok-joraari tonghalok je kiyorma, manjuya, tei haino thwimung pher mano.
en: In some cases, acute inflammation can lead to chronic inflammation, which is a long-term condition that can cause pain, disability, and even death.

kok: Aro kwbangma manwirok tongo je chiring robomsamung, solomani khobmani, dukhu manma, tei sakphiyokjak beramrok pher mano.
en: There are a number of things that can cause acute inflammation, including infection, injury, and autoimmune diseases.

kok: Solomanirok bacteria, solobermarok, eba fungi bai pherjak mano.
en: Infections are caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi.

kok: Jephuru oh malmatarok sak oh habo, boro kaisa phiyokjak khophirokmarok lorki je robomsamung bwkhak dagimarok mano.
en: When these organisms enter the body, they can trigger an immune response that leads to inflammation.

kok: Dukhumanmarok robomsamung pher bo mano.
en: Injuries can also cause inflammation.

kok: Jephuru sakhan paiyakmung wngkha, omo sapulswnamjakrok yakarmarok je thwi kuphur khotolsterok tei kubun phiyokjak khotolsterok ah ari bwkhak khasotonma mano.
en: When tissue is damaged, it releases chemicals that attract white blood cells and other immune cells to the area.

kok: Oh khotolsterok sapulswnamjakrok yakaro je pher robomsamung bai.
en: These cells release chemicals that cause inflammation.

kok: Sakphiyojka bemar wngkha ah sak phiyokjak lam choprobmani sakni sakhanrok bai pherjak wngkha.
en: Autoimmune diseases are caused by the body’s immune system attacking its own tissues.

kok: Omo ah sago kwlaijak sakhan bising robomsamung bwkhak dagi mano.
en: This can lead to inflammation in the affected tissues.

kok: Chiring robomsamung wngkha nangnungya kiyor holirwmarok bai saknaijak, ahaino ibuprofen eba acetaminophen.
en: Acute inflammation is usually treated with pain relievers, such as ibuprofen or acetaminophen.

kok: Baksa tonghalokrok bising, corticosteriods robomsamung khaina bwkhak bo phwnangjak mano.
en: In some cases, corticosteroids may be used to reduce inflammation.

kok: Tumungno robomsamung kaisa solomani, antibiotics bithini-kok sama bai pherjak mano.
en: If the inflammation is caused by an infection, antibiotics may be prescribed.

kok: Kwdwk bemar robomsamung wngkha kaisa kolok- joraaro tonghalok je kiyorma, manjuya, tei ahaino thwimung.
en: Chronic inflammation is a long-term condition that can cause pain, disability, and even death.

kok: Omo uramuram sakphiyokjak bemarok bai pherjak wngkha, ahaino rheumatoid arthristis tei kwdwk bemarrok.
en: It is often caused by autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and Crohn’s disease.

kok: Kwdwk bemar khammani kuphungm hoku nwngmani, tei nokbar sitramung bai bo pherjak mano.
en: Chronic inflammation can also be caused by obesity, smoking, and air pollution.

kok: Aro mungsa hammung kwrwi kwdwk bemar robomsamung bagwi, phiya amo bithi rwmani, tongdal swlaimarok tei sakno twywi haya naimung methepjak wngmano.
en: There is no cure for chronic inflammation, but it can be managed with medication, lifestyle changes, and physical therapy.

kok: Omo haino nwng tamo kanmani bagwiya, phiya nwng omo bahaikhe kanma.
en: It's not just about what you wear, but how you wear it.

kok: Tumungno nwng homnino didakmidak wngo tei nini richumrok kodrokjak wngkha, omo phunugo je nwng ninisaksani bagwi naikani khaiya.
en: If you're always slouching and your clothes are rumpled, it shows that you don't care about yourself.

kok: Borok nono naisiknai tei bohrok nini bagwi khakamarok swnamnai.
en: People will notice and they'll make assumptions about you.

kok: Bohrok wansuk mano je nwng seler eba sitrama.
en: They might think that you're lazy or unkempt.

kok: Bohrok haino wansuk mano je nwng khoroksa borok kahamya.
en: They might even think that you're not a good person.

kok: Aow, aro jorarok wngkha jephuru chwng jotto soroi richumrok kankha.
en: Of course, there are times when we all wear shabby clothes.

kok: Chwng haino kharmani phimungrok wngwi mano eba chwng ah nokni yaksiyagra samungrok khai tongo.
en: Maybe we're just running errands or we're doing chores around the house.

kok: Phiya tumungno nwng ninisaksakno soroi richumrok kanmani mankha jotto ah jora, omo ninisaksakno naisik nama bwkhak jora wngkha.
en: But if you find yourself wearing shabby clothes all the time, it's time to take a look at yourself.

kok: Nwng kubuida tongthokjak nwng je nukjakma bai?
en: Are you really happy with the way you look?

kok: Tumungno ehe, hwnkhe omo kaisa swlaina bwkha swnamna jora wngkha.
en: If not, then it's time to make a change.

kok: Nini sakbaithang tongdalni bagwi wansukna bwkhak kisa jora namani bai chengdi.
en: Start by taking some time to think about your personal style.

kok: Nwng bomtwihai richumrok bising kaham hwnwi wansuk?
en: What kind of clothes do you feel good in?

kok: Nwng bomtwihai richumrok bai sakno poito wansukma swnam?
en: What kind of clothes make you feel confident?

kok: Waisa nwng saimankha nwng tamo chajak, richumrok painani bagwi chengdi je nini saksuarno khropsa wngo.
en: Once you know what you like, start shopping for clothes that fit your personality.

kok: Omo bo nangkukma wngkubui swnamma je nini richumrok kwchwng tei kaham-khropsa wngkha.
en: It's also important to make sure that your clothes are clean and well-fitting.

kok: Tumungno bohrok kodrojak eba khain nangma wngkha, omo nono aswkno hayasuk swnamnai.
en: If they're rumpled or stained, it will only make you look worse.

kok: Jora nadi nini richumrokno istaree khaina bwkhak tei kahamkhe swnamdi bohrok kahamkhai khropsa wngo.
en: Take the time to iron your clothes and make sure they fit properly.

kok: Paithago, takiridi amjokmung bai juda juda tongdalrok bwkhak.
en: Finally, don't be afraid to experiment with different styles.

kok: Nwng uanamasingsa wngwi mano nwng tamo manam bai.
en: You might be surprised at what you find.

kok: Aro aswkno kwbangma juda juda lamarok tongo richumma bwkhak, haini bagwi takiridi kwtal manwirok chaitokmung bwkhak.
en: There are so many different ways to dress, so don't be afraid to try new things.

kok: Nwng teibo amjokmung khayo, kaisa tongdal naitukna bwkha nwng je hamjakma nwng ahaino teibo wngkha.
en: The more you experiment, the more likely you are to find a style that you love.

kok: Jephuru nwng kahamkhe richummo, omo phunugo je nwng ninisaksakno bising saktormung nadi.
en: When you dress well, it shows that you take pride in yourself.

kok: Omo bo nono teibo sakno poito wansukma bo swnammo.
en: It also makes you feel more confident.

kok: Tumungno nwng kaisa lama nini sakpuito sakhlaima bwkhak naitongmani wngkha, nini khutruk naina namani bai chengdi.
en: So if you're looking for a way to boost your self-confidence, start by taking a look at your wardrobe.

kok: Kisa kwtal richumrok kaisa kotor pherlaimung swnam mano.
en: A few new clothes can make a big difference.

kok: Nini swihni yasku rama wngkha naikani khwlaimungni kaisa nangmani babai, phiya obo kisaswk malmata rinai nokphangrokni bagwi kaisa samung kwrak wngmanw.
en: Trimming your dog's nails is a necessary part of grooming, but it can be a daunting task for some pet owners.

kok: Tumung nwng nini swihni yasku bahaikhe ranani siswkya hinkhe, tauanadi obo nini uansukmani saibo kwlai.
en: If you're not sure how to trim your dog's nails, don't worry - it's easier than you think.

kok: Puilani yapri wngkha nini manwi khwnuirok thumsa khwlaidi.
en: The first step is to gather your supplies.

kok: Nini thani kenchi kubuk josa eba yasku rajaknai kaisa, styptic powder thaisa eba pencil tei tuali kangsa nanganw.
en: You'll need a pair of sharp scissors or a nail clipper, a styptic powder or pencil, and a towel.

kok: Oboni ulo, nwng kaisa thai kahamno nini swihni yaskuno rauimano.
en: Next, you'll need to clip your dog's nails in a comfortable place.

kok: Tumung nini swih kirijakha hinkhe, bohrok tailamtwi phataro nukya abohai siring siring khotol khungsao yasku ranani chaitokdi.
en: If your dog is nervous, try clipping their nails in a quiet room where they can't see out the window.

kok: Nwng nini swihno romwi tonina bagwi keboni chubachu sanwimanw.
en: You may also want to have someone help you hold your dog still.

kok: Nini swihni yasku rana bagwi, bohrokni yathek yakno kahamkhe romwi chengdi.
en: To trim your dog's nails, start by gently grasping their paw.

kok: Aboni ulo, yasku buchuk bara rwna bagwi kenchi eba yasku rajaknaino samungo phwnangdi.
en: Then, use your scissors or clippers to clip the tip of the nail.

kok: Hojak tongdi belai barakhe rajakyatwi, tamoni hinkhe sajagwimanw tei thwi phaimanw.
en: Be careful not to cut too short, as this can cause pain and bleeding.

kok: Tumung nwng nini swihni yasku belai rauipaikha hinkhe thwi mwthakna bagwi styptic powder eba pencil phuldi.
en: If you do cut your dog's nail too short, apply a styptic powder or pencil to stop the bleeding.

kok: Kwbangkuk rwjaknai malmatani phalnogo styptic powder tei penchil manthogw.
en: Styptic powders and pencils are available at most pet stores.

kok: Uaisa nwng nini swihni jotto yasku rabai paikha hinkhe, bohrokno treat riui yakpai rwnani tapokdi.
en: Once you've trimmed all of your dog's nails, be sure to reward them with a treat.

kok: Kisaswk swihni bagwi yasku rajakma kaisa poja hilikno saimanma hai wnganw, haini bagwi obono kaisa kaham saimanma khwlainani nangkugo.
en: Trimming nails can be a stressful experience for some dogs, so it's important to make it a positive experience.

kok: Loi kisa swrwngmani bisingtwi, nwng khoroksa kwrwng haikhe nini swihni yasku raui mananw.
en: With a little practice, you'll be able to trim your dog's nails like a pro.

kok: Tei nini swihbo bohrokni yasku rajakthani tongthokjaganw!
en: And your dog will be happy to have their nails trimmed, too!

kok: Nini swihni yasku rana bagwi oro kisaswk yakbara kokbiti tongo:
en: Here are a few additional tips for trimming your dog's nails:

kok: * Nini swini bwskango yakungni yasku raui chengdi.
en: * Start by trimming the nails on your dog's front paws.

kok: Obono chengsana bagwi jottonisai kwlaikuk thai.
en: This is usually the easiest place to start.

kok: * Tumung nini swih kirijakha hinkhe uaisabaino bohrokni yasku ranani chaitokdi.
en: * If your dog is nervous, try trimming their nails one at a time.

kok: * Yaskuno milkhai ranani tapokdi.
en: * Be sure to trim the nails evenly.

kok: Nwng, yasku kaisa kubun-roknisai bara wngnano naigwlak.
en: You don't want one nail to be shorter than the others.

kok: * Tumung nwng nini swihni yasku bahaikhe ranani siswkya hinkhe, nini malmata saknai kwrwng eba khoroksa naikani khwlainaino swngdi.
en: * If you're not sure how to trim your dog's nails, ask your veterinarian or a groomer for help.

kok: Kisisa naikani tei kha rwmabai, nwng nini swihno yasku rajak tei kahamkhe toniuimanw.
en: With a little care and attention, you can keep your dog's nails trimmed and healthy.

kok: Ang saimano nwng miya tamo khaikha.
en: I know what you did yesterday.

kok: Nwng a saksak no ah kwkhrang rikichik kanwi hodarwk pinlam wo kaisa mangpili achukrem rikmani.
en: You posted a picture of yourself wearing that green rag on social media.

kok: Ang saimano nwng wansukha amo mwmwikothok hwnwi, phiya abo amtwiya.
en: I know you thought it was funny, but it wasn’t.

kok: Abo nini ama no borom rwya khaima se, tei bini chongphango dukhu rwma kwlayo.
en: It was disrespectful to your mother, and it hurt her feelings.

kok: Ang nono nakar sandi hwnwi samaniya tamni hinba ang nono jolio tongo.
en: I’m not asking you to apologize because I’m mad at you.

kok: Ang nono nakar sandi hwnwi sao tamni hinba omo no sosol samung.
en: I’m asking you to apologize because it’s the right thing to do.

kok: Nini ama nini hamajago, tei bo nini borom manthai nango.
en: Your mother loves you, and she deserves your respect.

kok: Khapurwi bono tini call khaidi tei bono sadi nono nakardi hwnwi.
en: Please call her today and tell her you’re sorry.

kok: Bono sadi nwng ichha khai bini chongphano duku rwya hwnwi, tei swmai tangdi nwng tei jesaphuru phano ah kwkhrang rikichik kanya hwnwi.
en: Tell her that you didn’t mean to hurt her feelings, and that you promise to never wear that green rag again.

kok: Ang saimano nwng belai borok kaham, tei ang saimano nwng nini ama no hamjago.
en: I know you’re a good person, and I know you love your mother.

kok: Haini bagwi khapurwi, sosol samung khaidi tei nakar sandi.
en: So please, do the right thing and apologize.

kok: Nini ama no nakar sanma olo, ang muchung je nwng ah kwkhrang rikichik no sogwi khibidi hwnwi
en: After you apologize to your mother, I want you to burn that green rag.

kok: Omo nini kaisa borom rwyani mari se, tei no thangna nango.
en: It’s a symbol of your disrespect, and it needs to be gone.

kok: Ang saimano ah rikichikno yakar honani belai kutuk, haiphano omo belai nangkuma.
en: I know it might be hard to let go of that rag, but it’s important.

kok: Omo nini lai thangjak ni mari, tei omo jora wngkha bwskang aguknani.
en: It’s a symbol of your past, and it’s time to move on.

kok: Nwng tabuk kwtal borok.
en: You’re a new person now.

kok: Nwng khoroksa kahamkuk borok.
en: You’re a better person.

kok: Tei nwng sakno ari khamwui ah rikichik no tei samung nangliya.
en: And you don’t need that rag to define you anymore.

kok: Haini bagwi khapurwi, sokdi.
en: So please, burn it.

kok: Sokdi tei yakar hodi.
en: Burn it and let it go.

kok: Tei thangwi nini ama no kwbangwidi tei sadi nwng bono hamjago hwnwi
en: And then go hug your mother and tell her you love her.

kok: Bobo nono hamjago.
en: She loves you too.

kok: Omo kutung, songmani, tei katirimani bwgwi phwnangjak tongkha, tei omo kaisa ah hakung mari swnammani bising.
en: It has been used for warmth, cooking, and protection, and it has also played a role in shaping the landscape.

kok: Laithangma bisirokni bising, haiphano, ah runghalokma borok tei horni kwcharo kutuk bangrwi tongkha.
en: In recent years, however, the relationship between humans and fire has become increasingly complex.

kok: Nokbartwibar swlaima horrok swnammani wngkha teibo wngjak tei teibo kwbangkuk, tei omo kaisa bolongrok, nokrok, tei langmarokni sakao sekhurpma swkamamani tongmani wngkha.
en: Climate change is making fires more frequent and more intense, and this is having a devastating impact on forests, homes, and lives.

kok: Baksa borok tokra rwkha je ah kahamkuk lama oh kengengmungbai lenden wngkha jotto horrokno mothokma bwkhak.
en: Some people argue that the best way to deal with this problem is to suppress all fires.

kok: Oh gana thangma bisirarok bagwi phwnangjak phayo, phiya omo homnino sago lwklaiya.
en: This approach has been used for centuries, but it is not always effective.

kok: Kubuio, , omo baksajorarogo hamyaswk manwirok swnam mano.
en: In fact, it can sometimes make things worse.

kok: Jephuru horrok mothokjak wngkha, bohrok supungma saka tiama tei hainoi kaisa kotor pher, swbaijakma hor bwkhak wngwi mano.
en: When fires are suppressed, they build up fuel and become more likely to cause a large, destructive fire.

kok: Tei kaisa gana thangma wngkha horrokno habar khamrimarok dagima wngkha.
en: Another approach is to let fires burn naturally.

kok: Oh gana thangma baksa tonghalokrok bising sago kwlaijak wngwi mano, phiya omo homnino katijak eba tangbaithang wngya.
en: This approach can be effective in some cases, but it is not always safe or practical.

kok: Kwbangma tonghalorok bising, omo kwcharo wngma bwkhak wngkha borok mwthangma tei manwiphan bwkhak.
en: In many cases, it is necessary to intervene to protect people and property.

kok: Ah kahamkuk lama hor bai lenden wngkha kaisa ojon manma wngkha haba khammani tei mothokmani kwcharo.
en: The best way to deal with fire is to find a balance between suppression and natural burning.

kok: Oh gana thangma chaplaimani tei logichalukma nangma wngkha, phiya omo jottoni slai sago kwlaijak lama wngkha ah bolonghorrok khapharmunng khairina bwkhak wngkha.
en: This approach requires planning and cooperation, but it is the most effective way to reduce the risk of wildfires.

kok: Tikinani tei naharmung oh gana thangma bwkhak berepkhong wngkha.
en: Resilience and adaptation are key to this approach.

kok: Tikinani wngkha ah khlaimanmung kasoma tei kaisa kebengmung simi kiphil manma bwkhak, jephuru naharmung wngkha khapima bwkhak khlaimanma wngkha kaisa habar swlaimani bwkhak.
en: Resilience is the ability to withstand and recover from a disturbance, while adaptation is the ability to adjust to a changing environment.

kok: Kainwi tikinani tei naharmung wngkha borokrokni bagwi tei habarlamrokni bagwi nangkukma wngkha.
en: Both resilience and adaptation are important for humans and for ecosystems.

kok: Borokrok hor bwkhak tikinani tisai mano yaprirok namani bai ah bolonghorok khapharmung khaina bwkhak, ahaino jabra sraisraimani tei horswbaimarok swnamani.
en: Humans can build resilience to fire by taking steps to reduce the risk of wildfires, such as clearing brush and creating firebreaks.

kok: Bohrok hor bwkhak naharmung bo mano swrwngmani bai bahaikhe hor-kongjak arirok bising tongma bwkhak.
en: They can also adapt to fire by learning how to live in fire-prone areas.

kok: Habarlamrok hor bwkhak tikiwui bo mano.
en: Ecosystems can also be resilient to fire.

kok: Hor wngkha kaisa habar bokcho kwbangma habarlamrokni, tei omo kubuino sadukma bolongrok kaham tonima bwkhak chubai mano.
en: Fire is a natural part of many ecosystems, and it can actually help to maintain healthy forests.

kok: Jephuru horrok mothokma wngkha, borok ah habar saikel hor tei bolong torrwma sachokma khai mano.
en: When fires are suppressed, they can disrupt the natural cycle of fire and forest growth.

kok: Thansa samung tangmani bai, borokrok tei habarlamrok hor bwkhak tikimani tisai mano.
en: By working together, humans and ecosystems can build resilience to fire.

kok: Omo ah bolonghorrok khapharmaung tei langmarok kaitina tei manwiphan khaina bwkhak chubai mano.
en: This will help to reduce the risk of wildfires and protect lives and property.

kok: Morokmung wngkha manwi morokmani tei kwlai wngma no sao.
en: Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.

kok: Abo consumer price index (CPI)o swlai jakuk o, nangkuk mani manwi tei samung khwlaijakmarok no bwswk morokna nang abono boksa o.
en: It is often measured as a change in the consumer price index (CPI), which tracks the prices of a basket of goods and services that are commonly purchased by households.

kok: Kwbangma ni bisingtwi no morokmung swlaijagwi mano, rang kwbang khe pirjak mano khobwi, manwi kahamno khe teibo nangjak bayo, tei supply khwlaimani kwmaswngcha wngo.
en: Inflation can be caused by a number of factors, including increases in the money supply, higher demand for goods and services, and supply shocks.

kok: Rang ni morokmung bang khe, pai-phal wng thani kuchuk ka'ui mano tei manwi morok rwi bo painairok kharwi thangya.
en: When the economy is growing rapidly, businesses may be able to raise prices without losing customers.

kok: Abo wngkha manwi morokmungno kuchugo tisa mani.
en: This can lead to a rise in inflation.

kok: Abo hai wngwibo, manwino morokjakugwi bo gosewi naiman drople wngo rangni lama no tisa na bagwi.
en: However, there are also factors that can help to offset the inflationary effects of faster economic growth.

kok: Phunukmario, labor hati khathorjagwi tong khe, salsa ni habani morokmung kwlwgwi thangnai rang ni slai, abo hai khe manwi morok mano naikol wi manthok o.
en: For example, if the labor market is tight, wages may rise more slowly than prices, which can help to keep inflation in check.

kok: Bebagwi, rang ni kuchuk kamung bai manwi morok mani halogo belai kutuk.
en: Overall, the relationship between economic growth and inflation is complex.

kok: Bahai khe rang kuchugo ka kha tei manwi bahai khe morogwi thang kebo sarwgwi manya tei aboni mungsa raida bo kwrwi.
en: There is no simple rule that can predict how faster economic growth will affect inflation.

kok: Phiya ba, belai hus bo wngna nango manwi morogma baise rangbo kuchuk ka o.
en: However, it is important to be aware of the potential for inflation when the economy is growing rapidly.

kok: Saka o je wngmanirogno khobwi sajak mani, abono karwi bo tei kwbangma ni bisingtwi manwi morogwi mano.
en: In addition to the factors mentioned above, there are a number of other factors that can affect inflation.

kok: Exchange rate, interest rate, tei haphangrokni raida bo khobjago.
en: These include the exchange rate, interest rates, and government policies.

kok: Exchange rate wngmani abo manwi phano morogwi mano eba laiwi phano mano.
en: The exchange rate can affect inflation by making imported goods more or less expensive.

kok: Phunukmari, dollars ni morokmung kwrai khe, phatarni naharjakma manwi teibo moroknai, hakhe teibo manwi morogwi mano.
en: For example, if the value of the dollar falls, imported goods will become more expensive, which can lead to higher inflation.

kok: Interest rate bai bo manwi morogwi mano eba laiwi mano.
en: Interest rates can also affect inflation.

kok: Interest rate morok phuru khe, pai-phal wngnairok tei painairok rang solok na thani kisakuk wngwi mano.
en: When interest rates are high, businesses and consumers are less likely to borrow money, which can slow economic growth and reduce inflation.

kok: Haphang wngnairokni raida bomani bo manwi morogwi mano.
en: Government policies can also affect inflation.

kok: Phunukmari, haphang rang swbaimani bisingtwi bo manwi morogwi mano, omo hai kheno manwi morogmung kuchugo ka wi mano.
en: For example, government spending can increase demand for goods and services, which can lead to higher prices.

kok: Haphang wngnairok ni raida boma baibo manwi morogwi mano.
en: Government regulations can also affect the price of goods and services.

kok: Rangni kuchuk kamung bai manwi morok mani halog belai kutuk tei kwbangma ni bisingtwi bo morogwi mano.
en: The relationship between economic growth and inflation is complex and depends on a number of factors.

kok: Bahai khe rang kuchugo ka kha tei bahai khe manwi morogwi thang kha abo kebo sirwkya tei aboni mungsa raida bo kwrwi.
en: There is no simple rule that can predict how faster economic growth will affect inflation.

kok: Phiya ba belai hus bo wngna nango manwi morogwi se rangbo kuchuk o ka o.
en: However, it is important to be aware of the potential for inflation when the economy is growing rapidly.

kok: Khumrok bisirarwgwi manjukma koktunrok phwnangjagwi phayo, tei khumni rwbai thepamani lama hwnkhe naithotok khe swnamnani tei kokmunggwnang rikmung samungrok.
en: Flowers have been used for centuries to communicate messages, and the art of flower arranging is a way to create beautiful and meaningful works of art.

kok: Aro kwbangma judajuda rwngnokrok uansukphan khum thepamani tongo, phiya jotto kaisa chwrokni along: kaisa ojon tei chajakmani thumsa khlaimani.
en: There are many different schools of thought on flower arranging, but all share a common goal: to create a balanced and pleasing composition.

kok: Kaisa nangkumanai bokhrwirok kharwsukma hwnkhe jephuru khumrokno thepamani banokma, pali, tei taknai.
en: The most important elements to consider when arranging flowers are shape, color, and texture.

kok: Banokma swnamjakha bohroknisaksakni khumrokni thepajakma bai.
en: Shape is created by the arrangement of the flowers themselves.

kok: Khumrok kaisa solai molai eba solo maolaiya naidal thepjak wngmano, tei bohrok thansa bodolkhai buthuprok saksaknikhai mano.
en: The flowers can be arranged in a symmetrical or asymmetrical pattern, and they can be grouped together in clusters or placed individually.

kok: Pali hwnkhe teikaisa nangkumani bokhrwi khum halok thepamani.
en: Color is another important element of flower arranging.

kok: Palirok sinai simanwi halok kwthamung eba ulophima swnam thani phwnangjak mano, tei bohrok evoke sukhrupbwi khatanjakrok phwnangwi mano.
en: Colors can be used to create a sense of harmony or contrast, and they can also be used to evoke specific emotions.

kok: Taknai hwnkhe khum thepamani thamrem bokhrwi.
en: Texture is the third element of flower arranging.

kok: Taknai khumrokbai bai judajuda sapokthaih bai halok bubarlaih, bwlairok, tei bosongrok swnamjak mano.
en: Texture can be created by using flowers with different types of petals, leaves, and stems.

kok: Jephuru khumrok thepjago, omo belai nanagkumani jottomiliwui amjokthai bwkhak wansukukma, je nwng swnamna nang jakmani.
en: When arranging flowers, it is important to consider the overall effect that you want to create.

kok: Nwng raidatwi eba raidayatwi thepajakma nang?
en: Do you want a formal or informal arrangement?

kok: Kaisa wansuk khapang eba kwtal thepjakma nang?
en: A romantic or modern arrangement?

kok: Waisa jodi nwng saimankha je nwng tamo nang, nwg saina chengwi manoo khumrok tei bohrokno thepama lamago je nwng muchungmarok amjokthai manwi mano.
en: Once you know what you want, you can start to choose the flowers and arrange them in a way that will achieve your desired effect.

kok: Khum thepamani hwnkhe kaisa swnamjakma rikmung sakmang, je jotto omorni borok tongthotogwi mano.
en: Flower arranging is a creative art form that can be enjoyed by people of all ages.

kok: Omo kaisa kotorkuar lama nini swnammarok sraisrai khai sama tei nini nogo bisingo naithotok khe tubuimano.
en: It is a great way to express your creativity and to bring beauty into your home.

kok: Jora rwmung bwkhak bohrokni aethetic koima, khumrokno kokkwrwnglaima koktungrogo phwnangwi mano.
en: In addition to their aesthetic appeal, flowers can also be used to communicate messages.

kok: Phunukmari karwi, kwchak khutlairok wngkha hamjakmano sraisrai khai sama uramuram bwkhak rijago, jephuru kuphur kongcharirok khe khairokmung sraisrai khai sama uramuram bwkhak rijago.
en: For example, red roses are often given to express love, while white lilies are often given to express sympathy.

kok: Khumrokni kokmung dalbidal khlaima sakbokmani hukumu tei jeba swkangnikok bising bohrok rijago.
en: The meaning of flowers can vary depending on the culture and the context in which they are given.

kok: Phunukmari karwi, baksa hukumurogo, pali phantok gap bugrasong bai gwdaljak, tei kubuni hukumurok, amo khe dukhu nangmani bai gwdaljak.
en: For example, in some cultures, the color purple is associated with royalty, while in other cultures, it is associated with mourning.

kok: Nwng jodi kaisa chongjak khum kokmung tamo wngkubui hwnwi siya khai, omo homnino kaham bwkhak je borok nono rinai no swngwi mano.
en: If you are not sure what the meaning of a particular flower is, it is always best to ask the person who gave it to you.

kok: Khum thepamani wngkha kaisa naithokma tei kokmungkuplung rikmung sakmang je jotto omorni borok tongthokjak mano.
en: Flower arranging is a beautiful and meaningful art form that can be enjoyed by people of all ages.

kok: Omo kaisa kotorkuar lama bwkhak nini swnamjakma srai srai khai sama tei nini no bisingo naithok bwwkhak tubunani.
