en: If you're not prepared for it, living in a big city can be a real culture shock.

kok: Phiya nwng tumungno omo kwbak mano, kaisa doyung kotor mlangchama saktwikarjak wngwi mano.
en: But if you can embrace it, life in a big city can be an amazing adventure.

kok: Aro kwbangma naijaknai tei khaijaknai tongo, tei nwng jesakhe phano akaijakgwlak.
en: There's so much to see and do, and you'll never be bored.

kok: Nwng jotto hayung sakani jotto khasrangjak dal borok bai malayanw, tei nwng juda juda hukumurok tei langma ni lamarokni bagwi swrwng mano.
en: You'll meet all sorts of interesting people from all over the world, and you'll learn about different cultures and ways of life.

kok: Nwng torma bwkhak sep bo manwi ano tei nwng salbrum no kwtal manwi swrwng mano.
en: You'll also have the opportunity to grow and learn new things every day.

kok: Aow, aro bataimung tongo kortorma doyung bising tongmani.
en: Of course, there are challenges to living in a big city.

kok: Ah tongmani mwswk belai kuchuk wngwi mano, tei nokrok naimanma naituk thani 3 wngwi mano.
en: The cost of living can be high, and it can be difficult to find affordable housing.

kok: Ah tangsitra swk chikonsa aolirok eba doyungrokni slai kuchukma wngwi mano.
en: The crime rate can also be higher than in smaller towns or cities.

kok: Phiya tumungno nwng omo manwi mankhe tei nwng kisa khapharmungrok nama gosikhe, kotor doyungo tongmani nini langma-swlaimani saimanjak wngwi mano.
en: But if you can afford it and you're willing to take some risks, living in a big city can be a life-changing experience.

kok: Kwrwngsao swrwngmung wngkha rwngnok khungsaono chwla tei bwrwirokno thansakhe phwrwngmungni tangloi.
en: Co-education is the practice of educating boys and girls together in the same school.

kok: Obo wngkha bisi ra-ni kwbang jora romwi choliui phainai kaisa tangloi, phiyaba obono twywi tabukbo koktanlaiui tongkhu.
en: It is a practice that has been around for centuries, but it is still being debated today.

kok: Kisaswk borok poito khwlayo je kwrwngsao swrwngmung, chwrairokno phwrwngmungni jottonisai kaham lama, taisa kubunrok poito khwlayo je chwla tei bwrwirokno juda khwlaima chakugo.
en: Some people believe that co-education is the best way to educate children, while others believe that it is better to separate boys and girls.

kok: Oro chama eba chayani phirokmung kwrwi, tei chongjak chwraini bagwi kahamkuk kokchap bohrokni saksakni Nangmani sakao bogwi naharwimanw.
en: There is no right or wrong answer, and the best decision for a particular child may depend on their individual needs.

kok: Kwrwngsao swrwngmungni kwbangma manmari tongo.
en: There are many benefits to co-education.

kok: Manmari kaisa wngkha je obo sir rwgwi khajak tongmani raidano swbaithani chubauimanw.
en: One benefit is that it can help to break down gender stereotypes.

kok: Jephuru chwla tei bwrwirok thansakhe phwrwngjago, aphuru bohrok khoroksa tei khoroksabai teibo kubui lamtwi kwrwngnani swrwngo.
en: When boys and girls are educated together, they learn to interact with each other in a more positive way.

kok: Bohrok khoroksa tei khoroksano borom rwnanibo swrwngo.
en: They also learn to respect each other's differences.

kok: Kwrwngsao swngmungni taikaisa manmari wngkha je, obo rwngni ajimungrokno chasarwthani chubauimanw.
en: Another benefit of co-education is that it can help to improve academic achievement.

kok: Amjok naitukmao saimankha, jerok kwrwngsao swrwngmungni rwngnogo swrwngkha, bohrok sir dalsani rwngnogo swrwngnai-roknisai rwngni remtwi kaham khwlayo.
en: Studies have shown that students who attend co-educational schools tend to do better academically than students who attend single-sex schools.

kok: Sana thangkhe, kwrwngsao swrwngmungobo kisaswk kebengmungrok tongo.
en: Of course, there are also some challenges to co-education.

kok: Kaisa kebengmung wngkha je kwrwngsao swrwngmungni rwngkhotol naikolmung teibo kutuk wngmanw.
en: One challenge is that it can be more difficult to manage a co-educational classroom.

kok: Chwla tei bwrwirokni swrwngmungi dal juda wngmanw tei bodolnwini nangmano supungmung kutuk wngmanw.
en: Boys and girls can have different learning styles, and it can be difficult to cater to the needs of both groups.

kok: Tei kaisa kebengmung wngkha kwrwngsao swrwngmung uaisa uisu damrokmung tei cheklekmung phaising twlagwimanw.
en: Another challenge is that co-education can sometimes lead to bullying and harassment.

kok: Chwrai tangnai wngkha kaisa uansukrak kebengmung kwbangma hakotorok ah hayung yaksiyagra bising.
en: Child labour is a serious problem in many countries around the world.

kok: Chwrayok uramuram akocho tei sakdukmaya tonghalorok bising samung bwkhak sakphan wngkha, tei bohrok uramuram kaisa banik tangrang rwjakya.
en: Children are often forced to work in dangerous and unhealthy conditions, and they are often not paid a fair wage.

kok: Omo kaisa swbaimani sekrupma bohrokni sakno twywi tei khapang sakduk sakao tongwi mano, tei omo bohrokno kaisa rwng manmani simi kasogra bo mano.
en: This can have a devastating impact on their physical and mental health, and it can also prevent them from getting an education.

kok: Kaisa hakotor bising, khoroksa bwrwi sikli Esther mungwi kaisa swnamnok bising samung bwkha sakphan wngkha.
en: In one country, a young girl named Esther was forced to work in a factory.

kok: Bo kwdwkma damrok samung khaikha, tei bo uramuram bini sebukrinai bai bujakha.
en: She worked long hours, and she was often beaten by her employers.

kok: Bo rwngnok bwkhak thangna bagwi rwjakya, tei bo bini bayaprokbai thwngnani bo jora kwrwi.
en: She was not allowed to go to school, and she did not have time to play with her friends.

kok: Esther belai tonghtokya wngkha, tei bo ah swnamnok simi salsa yoknani imang nukha.
en: Esther was very unhappy, and she dreamed of one day escaping from the factory.

kok: Salsa, Esther's sujuk phaikha.
en: One day, Esther's chance came.

kok: Bo swnamnok bising samung khai tongo jephuru aro kaisa hor kham tongo.
en: She was working in the factory when there was a fire.

kok: Esther yokma bwkhak mankhaa, phiya bini kwbangma bayaprok thwikha.
en: Esther was able to escape, but many of her friends were killed.

kok: Esther belai bwkha hamya wngkha, phiya bo saimano je bo kaisa lama naitukna nangnai kubun chwrairokno chubana bwkhak je swnamrokni bising samung bwkhak sakphan wngjak.
en: Esther was very sad, but she knew that she had to find a way to help other children who were being forced to work in factories.

kok: Esther chwrai tangnaini bagwi saimarima tisama bwkhak kaisa chobsong chengkha.
en: Esther started a campaign to raise awareness about child labour.

kok: Bo jotto ah hayung sakai borok bai kok sakha, tei bo bohrokno sakha ah chwrai tangnai kirimarok bagwi.
en: She spoke to people all over the country, and she told them about the horrors of child labour.

kok: Estherni chobasong belai khlaimanmung wngkha, tei omo bini hakotor bising ridarok swlaina bwkhak chubakha.
en: Esther's campaign was very successful, and it helped to change the laws in her country.

kok: Ah khapungmung kaisa chukjak tangma wngkha mungswk je Aida waisaphano swkang saimanyakhu.
en: The satisfaction of a perfect touch was something that Aida had never experienced before.

kok: Bo kwbangma chwla bai tongwi phaijak, phiya bohrok khoroksaphano bono mohai tongthok rwi manya je bo chajakma haikhe.
en: She had been with many men, but none of them had ever been able to give her the kind of pleasure that she craved.

kok: Abo uramuramwi wanajak tumungno bo khakeplengwi belai sanmani, eba tumungno bo haino saichung tongnani kokmang hwnkhe.
en: She had often wondered if she was simply too demanding, or if she was just meant to be alone.

kok: Phiya hwnkhe bo Hakim bai malaikha.
en: But then she met Hakim.

kok: Hakim jesa chwla rokni simi juda bo swkango waisaphano malai phaimanai.
en: Hakim was different from any man she had ever met before.

kok: Boh khakaham, tongkaham, tei boh jekhe buji'o mohai khe bono khoroksa phano agiphuru bujimanyakhu.
en: He was kind, gentle, and he seemed to understand her in a way that no one else ever had.

kok: Bo bini jora nakha bo bai, bini sakno naitukberaimani bai kaisa kwlwijak je bono golirikha.
en: He took his time with her, exploring her body with a tenderness that made her melt.

kok: Tei jephuru bo paithago bo bono mahmlai lama khai bono tangkha, bo kaisa bini tongthok twidu sujakma hai wansukha je omo mohaimanwi kahaiya bo swkango waisaphano wansukjakya khu.
en: And when he finally touched her in that special way, she felt a wave of pleasure wash over her that was unlike anything she had ever felt before.

kok: Omo haino bini sak hai hwnwi bini jotto swkangkologwi bini tangmano naisingwi tongmani.
en: It was as if her body had been waiting for his touch all along.

kok: Bo paijak hwnwi wansukha, jotto, tei bini langmani puila jora, bo saimankha kubuiyo khapungjak wngnani tamo hwnwi.
en: She felt complete, whole, and for the first time in her life, she knew what it was to be truly satisfied.

kok: Hakim bono choya karwi tangwi tongkha, bo saksak no mwthakmung kwmajagwi wansukkha.
en: As Hakim continued to touch her, she felt herself losing control.

kok: Bini sago hor chwngwi tongkha, tei bo bini bisingo tungphlamung tisamani wansuk tongkha.
en: Her body was on fire, and she could feel the tension building inside of her.

kok: Bo saimano je bo phaina nai tongkha hwnwi, tei bo jesamanwi slai teibo omo nangjago je bo swkango waisa phano nangjak hai.
en: She knew that she was about to come, and she wanted it more than anything she had ever wanted before.

kok: Kwdwkma jora romwi, aro chwla khoroksa Ahmed mungwi tongo bo Fatima hwnwi bwrwi khoroksa bai kaijakha.
en: Once upon a time, there was a man named Ahmed who was married to a woman named Fatima.

kok: Bohrok bisi kwdwkma romwi kaijajak, phiya bohrok kwthalai tongya.
en: They had been married for many years, but they were not happy together.

kok: Ahmed wngkha belai kwrak chwla, tei bo homnino bini moteh khe khaina muchungjago.
en: Ahmed was a very strict man, and he always wanted things to be done his way.

kok: Fatima hwnkhe kaham tei kwchang bwrwi, phiya bo Ahmed's ni lagatia sanmani logi tongna 3 chajakha.
en: Fatima was a kind and gentle woman, but she found it difficult to live with Ahmed's constant demands.

kok: Salsa, Ahmed tei Fatima kaklaina hwnwi chabwi nakha.
en: One day, Ahmed and Fatima decided to get a divorce.

kok: Bohrok kaklainani koksanai ni thani malaina thangkha, je bohrokno buchinani chubachu khaikha nangma law tei kerem khamani.
en: They went to see a divorce consultant, who helped them to understand the relevant laws and regulations.

kok: Koksanai bohrok ni gosithayo sogwithani chubachu khaikha bahaikhe borok ni rangmairok bakjaknai tei bohrokni bwsarokno naikolnani bakthani.
en: The consultant also helped them to reach an agreement on how to divide their assets and share custody of their children.

kok: Paithago kaklaikha, tei Ahmed bai Fatima bohrokni jani-jani langma thangkha.
en: The divorce was finalized, and Ahmed and Fatima went their separate ways.

kok: Ahmed kailabari ni yogwi kisa khakchangkha, phiya Fatima bini nukhung baimano twi mokjak.
en: Ahmed was relieved to be free from the marriage, but Fatima was sad to see her family break up.

kok: Bo saimano je bo bini 3 bwsarokno saichungno pusinai bini bisi 3 nanganw, phiya bo omo khaithani khathonwi bini yangtwi jura rwkha.
en: She knew that it would be difficult for her to raise her children on her own, but she was determined to make the best of it.

kok: Fatima samung mankha tei bini langmano tisa chengsakha.
en: Fatima found a job and started to rebuild her life.

kok: Bo bini bwsarokno rwngnogo sitokrikha tei bohrokni thani je nangmani manwi da tong kwrwi hwnwi khel khai.
en: She enrolled her children in school and made sure that they had everything they needed.

kok: Bo hamya nainai bai malaina bo chengkha, je bono bini kaklaima yakolo khanangwi kiyorwi pairinani chubachu khaikha.
en: She also started to see a therapist, who helped her to deal with the emotional pain of the divorce.

kok: Bisi kolokma romwi buphang bokocho twisa o kochokjak, tei aboni laibuma kwbangma tongo.
en: The log had been floating in the river for many years, and it had seen a lot of history.

kok: Rung kwbangma phayo thango wngmani nukjagwi tongo, tei twisa bo jora ni jora swlaijagwi no tong.
en: It had seen the coming and going of many boats, and it had seen the river change over time.

kok: Phiya ba nukhung kaisa ni malmatarogno salsa aro thangma hai khe waisa phano thangmani nukya kho.
en: But it had never seen anything like the family of animals that moved into it one day.

kok: O malmatarok wng kha mwkhwra ni bodol, tei bohrok masa siyan gwnang mwkhwra bai twiduljak layo bumung Hanuman.
en: The animals were a group of monkeys, and they were led by a wise old monkey named Hanuman.

kok: O buphang bokocho no twywi Honuman khwnajak, tei bo saimano aro boni nukhung ni bagwi chasok nai hwnwi.
en: Hanuman had heard about the log from a friend, and he knew that it would be a perfect home for his family.

kok: O buphang belai kotor tei kwrak, tei abo bohrokno satung watwi ni kate rw nai.
en: The log was large and sturdy, and it would provide them with shelter from the rain and the sun.

kok: O Mwkhwrarok a buphang bokocho o thanglai kha tei daktino bohrokni nok swnam kha.
en: The monkeys moved into the log and quickly made themselves at home.

kok: Bohrok bedekrogo nok swnam laikha, tei bohrok a buphang bokocho ni bugrung no khe mayanok swnam lai kha.
en: They built nests in the branches, and they used the hollow inside of the log as a storage space.

kok: Bohrok belai tongthok laijak bohrokni nok kwtal bai, tei bohrok sai mano bohrok aro bebak jwngjal ni yogwi manai.
en: They were very happy with their new home, and they knew that they would be safe there.

kok: Salsa, mwichomnai bodolrok twisa o phailai kha.
en: One day, a group of hunters came to the river.

kok: Borok malmata no bwthar na bagwi naituk lai jak, tei bohrok belai tongthok jak kha a mwkhwrarok no buphang bokocho o nugwi.
en: They were looking for animals to kill, and they were very excited when they saw the monkeys in the log.

kok: Bohrok bohrokni dono tisalai kha tei kogna bagwi tiyar wnglaiwi tongo.
en: They raised their bows and prepared to shoot.

kok: Phiya bohrok kogya swkangno, Hanuman buphang bokochoni bakhwlai kha tei mwichomnairokni bwskang o bacha'ui kha.
en: But before they could fire, Hanuman jumped out of the log and stood in front of the hunters.

kok: CHini khetoni puila maital tisamani ang tabukbo muitu togkho.
en: I remember the day I collected the first harvest of our family farm.

kok: Aphuru tungblang jora, satung tungmani panthoro samung tangmani rampra sukha.
en: It was a hot summer day, and the sun was beating down on us as we worked in the fields.

kok: Phiyaba chini bwkha bathakya chwng chini kolomtwi yorwi samung tangmani bwthaino mannani naisingjak.
en: But we didn't mind, because we were excited to see the fruits of our labor.

kok: Chwng mol kupulwng samung kwrak tangwi phaimani, tei tabukno o bwthaino chapnani jora.
en: We had been working hard all season, and it was finally time to reap the rewards.

kok: Chwng phantok mwkhwi tei moso kitingjat rokno khaklaikha tei chwng kahamkhe oborokno manwi rwkanai malkhungo dalaikha.
en: We picked the ripe tomatoes and peppers, and we carefully loaded them into the back of the truck.

kok: Ulo chwng bono kheto o twlangphikha je thayo chwng oborokno suo tei sayo.
en: Then we drove them back to the farm, where we washed and sorted them.

kok: Chwng mwikwthwng subaimani yak ulo, chwng bono hokango khachiui rwo.
en: After we had finished cleaning the vegetables, we put them in the smoker.

kok: Buphang chilibai hoku swnamwi mwikwthwng hango tei abo belaikhe kothok bahai motom rwo.
en: The smoke from the wood fire slowly permeated the vegetables, giving them a delicious flavor.

kok: Chwng dam kolok romwi aborokno hokango tongkha kahamkhe munyasak.
en: We smoked them for several hours, until they were perfectly cooked.

kok: Chwng samung tangwi jottono khatwtwng wngjakha, tei chwng nukhung tei kiching songbai bagwi chalaina bagwi naisingwi tongwi manlaya.
en: We were all so proud of our work, and we couldn't wait to share the delicious vegetables with our family and friends.

kok: Ah horo, kaisa chamung kotor songchalaikha, tei chwng jottono chini bwkhabai chalaikha nwnglaikha.
en: That night, we had a big feast, and we all ate and drank to our hearts' content.

kok: Obo kubui kubuino kaisa muitu marwkma sal wngkha, tei mungsa salo phano pogwi manglak.
en: It was a truly memorable day, and one that I will never forget.

kok: Ah kwcham buphang rung ah rukhung sakao achukjak, omo dolma chokmarok tei omo bukubuk nobarhalok ah sal tei ah watwi bai.
en: The old wooden boat sat on the shore, its sails furled and its hull weathered by the sun and the rain.

kok: Omo kwbangma bisirok rwgwi sebuk nukjakha, omo bini nokphangrokno twihmani twi beraimungrok hachal ha bwkhak.
en: It had seen many years of service, carrying its owners on voyages to far-off lands.

kok: Phiya tabuk, omo kiphilkha, omoni chokmani salrok paikha.
en: But now, it was retired, its days of sailing over.

kok: Salsa, khoroksa omorkisa chwrai mung Thomas mungwi ah twirwkong bwkhak paikha.
en: One day, a young boy named Thomas came to the beach.

kok: Bo ah kwcham rung bagwi kothomarok khwnakha, tei bo amo binisasakni bagwi naina bwkhak muchungjak wngkha.
en: He had heard stories about the old boat, and he was eager to see it for himself.

kok: Jephuru bo ah rungno nukha, bo omoni torma tei omoni naithokma bai uanajak wngkha.
en: When he saw the boat, he was amazed by its size and its beauty.

kok: Bo ah kotor twijlang bising saktwikarjakrok sakao hachalo chokmani binisaksakno wansukmankha.
en: He could imagine himself sailing off on adventures in the vast ocean.

kok: Thomas ah nokphang no swngkha ah rung tungmung bo kaisa ganarwk naima naida mano.
en: Thomas asked the owner of the boat if he could take a closer look.

kok: Ah nokphang mwnwikha tei sakha, "aow nwnng mano. Kasai phaidi!"
en: The owner smiled and said, "Of course you can. Come aboard!"

kok: Thomas ah rung bising kasakha tei ah Captain's achukphang bising achukkha.
en: Thomas climbed into the boat and sat down in the captain's chair.

kok: Bo phatar naikha ah twi sakao tei saksak chokamani thangma wansukha kaisa hachal thangma ha bwkhak.
en: He looked out over the water and imagined himself sailing away to a faraway land.

kok: Ah rungni nokphang Thomas mukphliksa ni bagwi Thomas no naikha, hwnkhe sakha, "nwng swrwngna da muchung bahaikhe choknai?"
en: The owner of the boat watched Thomas for a moment, then said, "Do you want to learn how to sail?"

kok: Thomas's mokol torkha "In'" bo sakha.
en: Thomas' eyes widened "Yes" he said.

kok: Ah rungni nokphang tei waisa mwnwikha.
en: The owner of the boat smiled again.

kok: "Hwnkhe ang nono phwrwngnai, " bo sakha.
en: "Then I'll teach you," he said.

kok: Sakmang paiphalnai: kaisa erwi tongmani kebengmung sakmang paiphalnai wngkha kaisa kubui kebengmung je borok ni yaksiyagra hayungno nangrwo.
en: Organ Trafficking: A Growing Problem Organ trafficking is a serious problem that affects people around the world.

kok: Jotto bisio, borok sairok, daga chopro, eba khokjakmani twi bohrokni sakmungrok riwui ma rio.
en: Every year, thousands of people are tricked, coerced, or kidnapped into giving up their organs.

kok: Oh sakmangrok hwnkhe rang-rigwnang borok rokno simi phaljago je bohrokno rwi mannai no simi.
en: These organs are then sold to wealthy people who can afford to pay for them.

kok: Sakmang phalnairok wngkha kaisa manmari bepar.
en: Organ trafficking is a lucrative business.

kok: Oh kosom hatio kaisa sakmang ni rangmari \$100, 000 simi \$1 chirasai o sogwi mano.
en: The black market price for a single organ can range from \$100,000 to \$1 million.

kok: Omo kiasa tangsitra rokni bagwi kaisa belai sotonmani saimung swnamo je dakti rang ajina naitongnai rokni bagwi.
en: This makes it a very attractive option for criminals who are looking to make a quick buck.

kok: Sakmang paiphalnairok ahaino tanghamya motha bodol rokbai kariwui twijago.
en: Organ trafficking is often carried out by organized crime groups.

kok: Oh bodolrok kaisa dalbidal khlaimungrok phwnango sakthar rokno borti khayo, jur khai khobmani, phemlokmung tei seplemung.
en: These groups use a variety of methods to recruit victims, including force, fraud, and deception.

kok: Sakthar rok wngkha unramuram hakotor digi khamuchungrwmung bai samung rina hwnwi swmai tangwi eba langma kaham rinai hwnwi tubujago.
en: Victims are often lured into the country with promises of a job or a better life.

kok: Waisa bohrok oro phaikheno, bohrok chopjagwi tonijago tei bohrokni sakmangrokno jurkhai rwi ma rio.
en: Once they are here, they are held captive and forced to give up their organs.

kok: Sakmang paiphalanai sakthar rokno swbainai wngmung tongwi mano.
en: Organ trafficking can have devastating consequences for victims.

kok: Omo simi ya bohrok mang tei bwkhabasilam trauma bo soywimano, phiya bohrok hanramung khaiphuru thwi mano.
en: Not only do they suffer physical and psychological trauma, but they may also die from the surgery.

kok: Jora riwui, sakmang paiphalnai bemarok auaima khai mano ahinao HIV bai hepatitis.
en: In addition, organ trafficking can spread diseases such as HIV and hepatitis.

kok: Sakmang paiphalanai kebengwi bulainani kaisa kutuk.
en: The fight against organ trafficking is a complex one.

kok: Aro mungsa kaisa gwdalamung hwnwi kwrwi je jotto tanghalogo samung khaiyanw.
en: There is no single solution that will work in every case.

kok: Kentha ni tungmung nini sago hab mano si di, tei nini bahanrok bo lenglagra thwng.
en: Feel the warmth of the blanket seeping into your body, and let your muscles relax.

kok: Mokol mukum di tei hama kolok na di.
en: Close your eyes and take a deep breath.

kok: Nini bukung twi hama sosa di tei bukhuk twi hama rohor di.
en: Inhale through your nose and exhale through your mouth.

kok: Omo hai khwlaimangno tong di, nini uanskmarogno kwchwng khwlai di tei bwsak no thir khwlai di.
en: Repeat this several times, letting your mind clear and your body become still.

kok: Nwng lengla kha ba, kaisa naithothok tongthai no uansok di.
en: As you relax, imagine yourself in a beautiful place.

kok: Abo twima rukung phano wngwi mano, bolong phano wngwi mano, eba khe Hathai kuchuk no phano uansogwi mano.
en: It could be a beach, a forest, or a mountaintop.

kok: Nwng jesa thai no sai na'ui bo, nwng tongthogwi manai tei khakchangwi manai abotwi tongthai swnam di.
en: Whatever place you choose, make it a place where you feel happy and at peace.

kok: Kitingwi naidi, khorang khwna di, tei nwng saiwi namani tongthaini bahai no motom su di.
en: See the sights, hear the sounds, and smell the smells of your chosen place.

kok: Nini bukur o saltung nangmano si di tei nini khwnai o boyar nangmano bo.
en: Feel the sun on your skin and the breeze in your hair.

kok: A tongthai o nwng je muchungsak no lengla di.
en: Let yourself relax in this place for as long as you like.

kok: Nwng mwkthango phirokna tiyar wngphuru khe, hama kolok khe sosa di tei mokol phiyok di.
en: When you're ready to return to the present, take a few deep breaths and open your eyes.

kok: Nini sakno swrwng swrwng hai wngjaknai tei phan bo manai, o salno haino hai chengphina phan man phinai.
en: You'll feel refreshed and rejuvenated, ready to take on the day.

kok: Obo kaisa ahaino lenglajaknai kaida ni phunukmari se abobai nini sakni bebak ruwaima tei bebakni wngwi sago kaham tongnai.
en: This is just one example of a relaxation technique that you can use to relieve stress and improve your overall well-being.

kok: Tei kubun lenglajaknai kaidarok bo kwbangma no tongo, aboni bagwi kaisa kaidano no khwlai di je nini samungo chugo tei abono no loi khwlai di.
en: There are many other relaxation techniques available, so find one that works for you and make it a part of your daily routine.

kok: Kisisa swrwng ma baino, nwng nang phuru, dage kheno lengla'ui man nai.
en: With a little practice, you'll be able to relax on command, whenever you need to.

kok: Obo tamni hinba ah cholidrop omor wngkha ah bwrwimani puila tangwimanya jora 12 bisirok wngkha, tei ah cholidrop tangmanya bathakma omor wngkha 45 bisirok.
en: This is because the average age of a woman's first menstrual period is 12 years old, and the average age of menopause is 45 years old.

kok: Obo kokmarok je ah bwrwima thani prai 33 omorok tongo chwrai bana bwkhak.
en: This means that a woman has approximately 33 years to bear children.

kok: Haiphano, khroksa bwrwimani kwchar-thamchirok bising bwsa baimanma lonma bwkhak chengmarok, tei jora bai bo 40 ugkha, bini oknangmani habar sujukrok nangkuma khaikha.
en: However, fertility begins to decline in a woman's mid-thirties, and by the time she is 40, her chances of conceiving naturally are significantly reduced.

kok: Aro wngkha kwbangma kusungchwlwirok je khoroksa bwrwimani baimanma lonmani bwkhak rwma mano, omor khobmani, hoku nwngmani, kuphungm tei baksa sakham tonghalokrok.
en: There are a number of factors that can contribute to a woman's declining fertility, including age, smoking, obesity, and certain medical conditions.

kok: Khoroksa bwrwima omorok wngkhe, bini bwtwirok sakdukma kisa tei teibo ahaino chromosomal adamwlangrok tongo.
en: As a woman ages, her eggs become less healthy and more likely to have chromosomal abnormalities.

kok: Oh ah bwsakwraima akocho, kwthwi achaima tei achaima chayarok bari mano.
en: This can increase the risk of miscarriage, stillbirth, and birth defects.

kok: Hoku nwngmani bo kaisa bwrwima baimanma ah bwsakhok tei rwbamrok bwkhak thwi kochokna lonmani bai hamya khlaimano.
en: Smoking can also damage a woman's fertility by reducing blood flow to the uterus and ovaries.

kok: Kuphung horomonal thitiyarok bwkhak dagi mano je rwbammani bai kebengma wngmano.
en: Obesity can lead to hormonal imbalances that can interfere with ovulation.

kok: Tei baksa sakham tonghalorokrok, ahaino polycystics ovary syndrome (PCOS) tei endometriosis, khoroksa bwrwimani bagwi oknangma bwkhak omo bo 3 swnam mano.
en: And certain medical conditions, such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and endometriosis, can also make it difficult for a woman to conceive.

kok: Tumungno nwng khoroksa bwrwima wngkha je 30 sakao wngkha tei chwrairok khainanai bagwi wansugwi tongkha, nwng nini saknainai bai kok sama bwkhak omo nangkukma wngkha nini baimanma bagwi.
en: If you are a woman who is over 30 and are thinking about having children, it is important to talk to your doctor about your fertility.

kok: Aro wngkha kwbangma manwirok je nwng nini oknangmani sujukrok charwma bwkhak khlaimano, hilikmung seplemani khobmani bai tumungno nwng belaihilikmung eba kuphung wngkha, hoku nwngmani yakarmani, tei sabrumbrum sakswnamma manmani.
en: There are a number of things that you can do to improve your chances of conceiving, including losing weight if you are overweight or obese, quitting smoking, and getting regular exercise.

kok: Nini saknainai baimanma bithirok bitirimung eba kubun saknaimungrok bo wngmano nono oknangma bwkhak chubao.
en: Your doctor may also recommend fertility medications or other treatments to help you conceive.

kok: Omo muito narakma bwkhak nangkukma wngkha je aro kwbangma kubun lamarok tongo kaisa nukhung tongna bwkhak, ahaino tumungno nwng oknangma habar bwkhka chukya wngkha.
en: It is also important to remember that there are many other ways to have a family, even if you are unable to conceive naturally.

kok: Sandaima tei kubunni ok wngkha kainwi saimungrok je nwng nwng gosima bwkhak muchung mano.
en: Adoption and surrogacy are two options that you may want to consider.

kok: Ah kwtal bithini chubamung bai, aro kwbangma lamarok tongo kaisa nukhung tongma bwkhak, nini omor eba baimanma jesaphano wngthwng.
en: With the help of modern medicine, there are many ways to have a family, no matter what your age or fertility.

kok: Bo phwrwngkha je jotto mangrok guriui romjago achaima, thwima, tei ayang masing, tei oh gurimani swngcharni manwi bai chini manjumabai wngsugo.
en: He taught that all beings are caught in a cycle of birth, death, and rebirth, and that this cycle is perpetuated by our attachments to things in the world.

kok: Oh manjuma jesphano wngmano, manwi-khwnwi sasokmani simi khakama bai poito khaima jora.
en: These attachments can be to anything, from material possessions to ideas and beliefs.

kok: Chwng jephuru mungsaswk bai manjugo, chwng sasokma bai kasokmahai wngthango, tei jephuru kwmama eba chwng je nangma manwi manyakhe aphuru chwnwg jwngjalo kwlaiyo.
en: When we are attached to something, we become possessive and controlling, and we suffer when we lose or cannot have what we want.

kok: Buddha chwngno phwrwngo jwngjalno mwthakna hwnkhe chwng jotto manjuma rokno rwi hona nango.
en: The Buddha taught that the way to end suffering is to let go of our attachments.

kok: Amtwiya 1, phiya dhiyan khaima bai tei pholagwdaljak loi khwlaikhe abo gerebjak wngmano.
en: This is not easy, but it is possible through meditation and other spiritual practices.

kok: Chwng jephuru chini manjukma rwi howo, chwng aphuru gurima thani phiyokjago halok achaima, thwima, tei ayang maising, tei chwng kubui kwchangtotok tei tongthtok sijak wngmano.
en: When we let go of our attachments, we become free from the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth, and we can experience true peace and happiness.

kok: Chini thani kaisa jottoni swlai muito naraknani nangkukmani manwi hwnkhe jephuru chini manjumano rwi hona chaitokphuru chwng je chini saksomani no ya.
en: One of the most important things to remember when trying to let go of our attachments is that we are not our possessions.

kok: Chwng chini khakamung eba poito no ya.
en: We are not our ideas or beliefs.

kok: Chwng mohai khakeplengjak kwthang je chini sinai simanwi twi swngcharno sijagwi khai tongo.
en: We are simply beings who are experiencing the world through our senses.

kok: Jephuru chwngno chwng omo haikhe nugo, aphuru manwi rwi honani belai kwlai wngthango chwng wansugo je chwng tongthokna nango hwnwi.
en: When we can see ourselves in this way, it becomes easier to let go of the things that we think we need to be happy.

kok: Chini manjuma rokno rwi horphano omo haiya je chwng chini jotto yakar rinai.
en: Letting go of our attachments does not mean that we have to give up everything.

kok: Omoni suja kokbwrwng hwnkhe je chwng chini manwi no rwi hona nango jephuru jora phaikhe.
en: It simply means that we need to be able to let go of things when it is time.

kok: Chwng mohai manwi rwi honani chukna nango je chwngno tei chubai manliya, tei chwng mohai manwino rwi howui chukha je chini naimwthang eba chini kirima bai manjuwi tongmano.
en: We need to be able to let go of the things that are no longer serving us, and we need to be able to let go of the things that we are attached to out of fear or insecurity.

kok: Chwng jephuru chini manjuma rwi howo, chwng aphuru kwtal swngchar halok wngmarokno chwngno khulugo.
en: When we can let go of our attachments, we open ourselves up to a new world of possibilities.

kok: Chwng chini langmano mohaikhe tongwi thangnani hwnwi yokjak wngthango je omo chini bagwi kubui, tei chwng sijakna bagwi yogwi thango khaswrang tei thongthokma abo chini manthai.
en: We become free to live our lives in a way that is true to ourselves, and we become free to experience the joy and happiness that is our birthright.

kok: Jephuru omo kaisa bebak loi hai khakama wngmano, omo kubuino wakni bagwi belai manmarijak.
en: While this may seem like a gross habit, it is actually quite beneficial to the pig.

kok: Ah harpek wakno kwchang tei kwchwng khai chubao, tei omo haino kaisa habar satungriso bo manthokrio.
en: The mud helps to keep the pig cool and clean, and it also provides a natural sunscreen.

kok: Jora rwmung bising, ah harpek wakni bukur no parasites tei bacteria thani katina chubao.
en: In addition, the mud helps to protect the pig’s skin from parasites and bacteria.

kok: Baksa borok poito khayo je wakrok wngkha letra patra tamni hinba bohrok khibijaknai manwi chao.
en: Some people believe that pigs are dirty because they eat garbage.

kok: Haiphanom wakrok wngkha kubuino belai kwchwng malmatarok.
en: However, pigs are actually very clean animals.

kok: Bohrok abo chao je bohrokno bohrokni habar bising mano, tei borok mungsaphano chagwlak je sokjak eba bermajak.
en: They only eat what they find in their environment, and they will not eat anything that is rotten or diseased.

kok: Kubui hwnkhe, wakrok wngkha uramuram bwkhak khibijaknai khipma hakorrok kwchwng khaima tamni hinmakhe bohrok wngkha aswk kaham erengmanwi chamani.
en: In fact, pigs are often used to clean up garbage dumps because they are so good at eating trash.

kok: Wakrok wngkha belai siyankwrwng malmatarok.
en: Pigs are also very intelligent animals.

kok: Bohrok kebengmungrokno solve khaimano tei kwtal manwirok daktino swrwng mano.
en: They are able to solve problems and learn new things quickly.

kok: Wakrok kolrokno phwnangna bwkhak sini jago, tei bohrokno phemloknarok khaina bagwi haino phwrwng mano.
en: Pigs have been known to use tools, and they can even be trained to do tricks.

kok: Bohrokni munggnang phano, wakrok wngkha kubuino belai kwchang tei hodarwk malamatarok.
en: Despite their reputation, pigs are actually very gentle and social animals.

kok: Bohrok bohrokni bugrarok bai belaino hamjakjak, tei bohrok borokni yaksiyagra tong tongthokjago.
en: They are very affectionate with their owners, and they enjoy being around people.

kok: Wakrok wngkha haino belai simuchung malmatarok, tei bohrok bohrokni khopmani naitukberaima bwkha hamjago.
en: Pigs are also very curious animals, and they love to explore their surroundings.

kok: Tumungno nwng kaisa hamjakmani tei uansukphan rwjak malmata naitongkhe, kaisa wak nini chasukjak malmata wngwi mano.
en: If you are looking for a loving and intelligent pet, a pig may be the perfect animal for you.

kok: Wakrok wngkha 1 bwkhak naikani bagwi, tei bohrok kotorkuar logisongjak swnamo.
en: Pigs are easy to care for, and they make great companions.

kok: Bohrok khatijak tei twichuruma habar yapharo boro swkangni tongnairokno phiyokjagwi tongnani tei haya wngphimung katima swrwng mano.
en: They provide a safe and supportive environment where former inmates can learn to live independently and avoid relapse.

kok: Kwchangtotok tongjaknai nokrok hainohai podrepod samungrok yapharo, ahaino kokchapmani, samung swrwngmani, tei loiungmani bodolrok twichuruma bai.
en: Sober living homes typically offer a variety of services, such as counseling, job training, and addiction support groups.

kok: Bohrok hoda sinai simanwi tei twichuruma bago, je borokrokni bagwi marokjakya wngmano je jora bokjakl chobwi rwjak mani olo teiwaisa hodao habphimani.
en: They also provide a sense of community and support, which can be invaluable for people who are reentering society after a period of incarceration.

kok: Aro kwbangma manmari tongo kwchangtotok tongjaknai nok tongkhe.
en: There are many benefits to living in a sober living home.

kok: Masa ni bagwi, obo habar nokrakrok bagjago boro swkangni tongnairok phiyojak khai tongna swrwngmano.
en: For one, it provides a structured environment where former inmates can learn to live independently.

kok: Bohrok raida thepama tei kerem khamungno je bohrokno kaham tongraida tei tangremrok hamkrai bwkhak chubai mano.
en: They are expected to follow a set of rules and regulations, which can help them to develop good habits and routines.

kok: Jora rwmungo, kwchangatotok tongjaknai nokrok podrepod samungrok yapharo je swkngnai tongnairokno bohrokni yethego teiwaisa bachana bagwi.
en: Additionally, sober living homes offer a variety of services that can help former inmates to get back on their feet.

kok: Oh samungarok kokchapmani khobwi mano, samung swrwngmani, tei loiungmani bodolrokno twichuruma bai.
en: These services may include counseling, job training, and addiction support groups.

kok: Oh hoda sinai simanwi tei twichuruma je kwchangthotok tongjaknai nokrok belai chubanai mankha.
en: The sense of community and support that is found in sober living homes can also be very beneficial.

kok: Swkangni tongwi thangnairok uramuram chongo junda khai tongma tei saichung wngo along eba along ni phiyokjakma olo.
en: Former inmates often feel isolated and alone after being released from prison or jail.

kok: Kwchangtotok tongjaknai nogo tongmnai bohrokno tei kubuni bai kwrwngmano je mohai solai molai saimanjak gerebwi thangwi tongmani.
en: Living in a sober living home can help them to connect with others who are going through a similar experience.

kok: Bohrok tangsong tei kubn tongnairokni thani twichuruma manwi mano, je bohrokno yaprimari tongnani bohrokno phiroktubuna bagwi.
en: They can also receive support from staff and other residents, which can help them to stay on track with their recovery.

kok: Nwng jodi tabukno yoknai tongnai hwnkhe, kwchangtotok tongjaknai nogo tongmani obo kotorkuar lama bwkhak twi mung hoda phiroknani.
en: If you are a recently released inmate, living in a sober living home can be a great way to transition back into society.

kok: Omo nono twichuruma tei swnamari bagwi mano je nwng tangmanma wngna nangnai.
en: It can provide you with the support and structure that you need to succeed.

kok: Aro kwbangma kwchangtotok tongjaknai nokrok manthogo, je nwngbo kaisa naituk mano, je nini nangmarok tei rangchongmungo malaimarok.
en: There are many sober living homes available, so you can find one that meets your needs and budget.

kok: Nwng samung tangnani tiyar de tong abono sraisrai khwlaina bagwi loi phwrwngmungni nangmarokno rwksaui tongnani nango.
en: It is important to comply with the training requirements in order to ensure that you are properly prepared for the job.

kok: Oboni bisingo tongo jotto loi phwrwngmung pandao manjakma, jotto samung chongjakno paihma, tei jotto dagimarokno rwksama.
en: This includes attending all training sessions, completing all assignments, and following all instructions.

kok: Nini loi phwrwngnai tei supervisorni thani chama chaya phirokmung tei kokbiti nahanabo nangkugo.
en: It is also important to be receptive to feedback and suggestions from your trainers and supervisors.

kok: Obo nono nini rwbai tei elem hamrwthani chubauano, tei obo nono samung kahamni uansukmung chasarwthanibo chubauano.
en: This will help you to improve your skills and knowledge, and it will also help you to develop a positive work ethic.

kok: Jephuru nwng chama chaya phirokmung eba sejamung mano, abono tongraida kahambai yachaknani nangkugo.
en: When you receive feedback or criticism, it is important to take it in a positive manner.

kok: Oboni kokmang nono jesa sajakmani jotto kokno soinani nangnai abohaiya, phiyaba oboni kokmang wngkha obohaise je dalbidal naharmungtwi khwnana bagwi tiyar tongnani nanganw.
en: This does not mean that you have to agree with everything that is said, but it does mean that you should be open to hearing different perspectives.

kok: Je borok nini chama chayano phirogmung rwui tongo bohno borom rwnabo nangkugo.
en: It is also important to be respectful of the person giving you feedback.

kok: Muitu narwkdi, bohrok nono chubanani chaitogwi tongo, haini bagwi bohrokni sajakthai tongmano khwnani nangkugo.
en: Remember, they are trying to help you, so it is important to listen to what they have to say.

kok: Nwng chama chayani phirokmung uaisa manpaikha hinkhe obono twywi uansukna bagwi kisaswk jora nanani nangkugo.
en: Once you have received feedback, it is important to take some time to think about it.

kok: Uansugwi naidi tamo sajakha tei bahaikhe nwng obono nini samungo thepauiman.
en: Consider what was said, and how you can apply it to your work.

kok: Nini mungsaswk swngmung tongkhe, nini loi phwrwngnai eba supervisorno swngnani takwmamdi.
en: If you have any questions, do not hesitate to ask your trainer or supervisor.

kok: Nini samungni loi eba tangraidao swlaimung tubuna bagwi khulokjak tongnabo nangkugo.
en: It is also important to be open to making changes to your work habits or procedures.

kok: Tumung nwng swlainani muchungjakya hinkhe nwng chasaui mangwlak.
en: If you are not willing to change, then you will not be able to improve.

kok: Loi swrwngmungrokni raida rwksai tongmani bisingtwi tei jesa kokbiti eba sejamano tongraida kahambai yachagwi, nwng nini kwrwng tei elemno chasarwi manano tei nwng kaisa samung kahamni tangraidani hamkwrai khwlai manano.
en: By complying with the training requirements and responding in a positive manner to any suggestion or criticism, you will be able to improve your skills and knowledge, and you will also be able to develop a positive work ethic.

kok: Obo nono jesa bodolni bagwi kaisa mulaja gwnang rwbai khwlai tisauano tei obo nono nini tangmungni naharmung ajithani chubauano.
en: This will make you a valuable asset to any team, and it will help you to achieve your career goals.

kok: Nwng oh salni bagwi naising tongmani tamo kaisa molbrumbrum kahai wansukmarok bagwi, tei tabuk omo paithago oro wngkha.
en: You have been waiting for this day for what feels like an eternity, and now it is finally here.

kok: Nwng nini kwtal langma thansa nukhung haikhe chengma bwkak naising mangwlak.
en: You can't wait to start your new life together as a family.

kok: Ah sandaima tansep kolok tei kwrak wngmano, phiya omo wngkha jotto swk ah paithakni bising omo.
en: The adoption process can be long and arduous, but it is all worth it in the end.

kok: Jephuru nwng paithago nini chwraino romkha nino yaktwkrok bising tei sakha, "ang nini ama/baba tabuk, " nwng saimannai je omo wngkha jotto swk.
en: When you finally hold your child in your arms and say, "I'm your mom/dad now," you will know that it was all worth it.

kok: Sandaima wngkha naithokma manwi.
en: Adoption is a beautiful thing.

kok: Omo wngkha khroksa chwraino hamanai nok kaisa rwmung rwmani tei saka torna bwkhak sep kaisa katijak tei kwrak habar bising.
en: It is the gift of giving a child a loving home and the opportunity to grow up in a safe and stable environment.

kok: Omo bo ah mapharokni bwkhak kaisa rwmung je ah sujug rwjak tongo ah maphawngjak tongthokrok simari bawkhak.
en: It is also a gift to the parents, who are given the chance to experience the joys of parenthood.

kok: Tumungno nwng sandaima wansugwi tongkha, ang nono khatungrimung khaidi hino nini rutukrwk tei kaisa borom gwnang sandaima adong naitukna bagwi.
en: If you are considering adoption, I encourage you to do your research and find a reputable adoption agency.

kok: Aro kwbangma juda juda sandaima adong sakpokthaihrok tongo, aswkno omo kaisa naitukna bwkhak nangkukma je nini bagwi kaisa kaham chukjak.
en: There are many different types of adoption agencies, so it is important to find one that is a good fit for you.

kok: Ah sandaima tangsep kutuk wngwi mano, aswkno omo wngkha nangkukma thaini bising kaisa kaham nangmani lam bwkhak tongo.
en: The adoption process can be complex, so it is important to have a good support system in place.

kok: Sandaima wngkha kaisa langma-swlaimani simari.
en: Adoption is a life-changing experience.

kok: Omo wngkha kaisa beraima je hamjakma, mwnwima, tei mwktwrwi bai supungjak.
en: It is a journey that is filled with love, laughter, and tears.

kok: Phiya omo wngkha kaisa beraima je swk namani wngkha.
en: But it is a journey that is worth taking.

kok: Tumungno nwng sandaima wansugwi tongkha, ang nono ah barma bwkhak khatungrimung khayo.
en: If you are considering adoption, I encourage you to take the leap.

kok: Nwng omo dukhu mangwlak.
en: You will not regret it.

kok: Kwdwkma jora romwi, aro khoroksa bwrwi sikli Alice mungwi tong je belaino seler.
en: Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Alice who was very lazy.

kok: Bo bini samungrok jesaphuru phano khaiya, tei bo homnino bini rwngnok karo.
en: She would never do her chores, and she would always skip school.

kok: Bini maphasong bini bagwi belai wanajak, tei jotto manwi chaitok naikha bohrok khaimatwi bini lamarok swlaida mano hwnwi.
en: Her parents were very worried about her, and they tried everything they could to get her to change her ways.

kok: Phiya mungsaphano samung khailiya.
en: But nothing worked.

kok: Salsa, Alice's ni maphasong chongkha bono kaisa hamya nainai ni oro bono twlangna hwnwi.
en: One day, Alice's parents decided to take her to see a therapist.

kok: Ah hamya nainai Alice bai kok sakha ah nangkukma tongchapjak ni bagwi, tei bo bono sakha je tumungno nwng bini langmao tangmanjak wngna muchungkhe, bo tongchapjak swrwngna nango.
en: The therapist talked to Alice about the importance of discipline, and she told her that if she wanted to be successful in life, she would need to learn to be disciplined.

kok: Alice omo khwnai tongthok jakliya, phiya bo saimano je bini maphasosng chao hwnwi.
en: Alice was not happy to hear this, but she knew that her parents were right.

kok: Bo swlaina hwnwi chongwi nakha, tei bo bini samungrok khwlaina chengjakha tei sal thwigwi rwngnok bwkhak thangkha.
en: She decided to make a change, and she started to do her chores and go to school every day.

kok: Omo puilao 1 wngmaya, phiya bo omo bai kwchajak, tei phaithago bo abono bwthaihrok nukna chengkha.
en: It was not easy at first, but she stuck with it, and eventually, she started to see results.

kok: Bo rwngnok bising kaham remrok manna chengkha, tei bo kwtal bayaprok swnamakha.
en: She started to get better grades in school, and she made new friends.

kok: Boh ahaino tongthokjak wngkha bo swkang wngmani slai.
en: She was even happier than she had been before.

kok: Alice swrwngkha je tongchapjak wngkha nangkukma langma khlaimanmung bagwi.
en: Alice learned that discipline is important for success in life.

kok: Omo homnino 1 tongchapjak wngma simiya, phiya omo morojak wngkha.
en: It is not always easy to be disciplined, but it is worth it.

kok: Nwng jephuru tongchapjak wngkha, nwng jesamanwi manwi mano nwng nini khorogo khaihmani.
en: When you are disciplined, you can achieve anything you set your mind to.

kok: Awa toke.
en: The end.

kok: Adi nobar o, khoroksa sikli khungsa bwsate kami o tong jao bwmung Anna.
en: Once upon a time, there was a young woman named Anna who lived in a small village.

kok: Bo belai maya gwnang tei bwkha kaham, phiya bo belai bwkha bo tongthok jak ya.
en: She was a kind and gentle soul, but she was also very unhappy.

kok: Bo yoksamung bahai sina muchungo, phiya bo saimano bo boni kami no yakarwi thangmaya hwnwi.
en: She longed for freedom, but she knew that she would never be able to leave her village.

kok: Salsa, Anna bolongtwi himwi tong phuru khoroksa siniya chwla bai malai kha.
en: One day, Anna was walking in the forest when she came across a strange man.

kok: Bo kolok tei chwla naithok, boni khwnai bo kolok tei naichomung gwnang mokol.
en: He was tall and handsome, with long black hair and piercing blue eyes.

kok: Bo sakno Luka hwnwi sinimung rw kha, tei Anna no bo sakha bo khoroksa hakchalma ni phainai hwnwi.
en: He introduced himself as Luka, and he told Anna that he was a traveler from a faraway land.

kok: Anna bai Luka daktino hamjak lai kha, tei bohrok kwnwi kharlai na bagwi kok chablai kha.
en: Anna and Luka quickly fell in love, and they decided to run away together.

kok: Bohrok sal kwdwkma romwi himlaijak, tei bohrok belai naithok naithok manwirok nuklaikha.
en: They traveled for many days, and they saw many amazing things.

kok: Bohrok borok kaham baibo malaikha tei borok hamya baibo malaikha.
en: They met kind people and cruel people, and they learned a lot about the world.

kok: Paithago, Anna bai Luka twijwlango sogwi laikha.
en: Finally, Anna and Luka reached the sea.

kok: Bohrok rung swnamlaikha tei chogwi thanglaikha, tei bohrok ungkuluk phirogwi bo naharliya.
en: They boarded a ship and sailed away, and they never looked back.

kok: Bohrok kwchalma hao kwtal tonthai manlaikha, tei aro bohrok tongthogwi tonglaikha.
en: They found a new home in a faraway land, and they lived happily ever after.

kok: Anna bai Luka ni kothoma wngkha kaisa muito rwmani se yoksama bwswkse kaham hwnwi.
en: Anna and Luka's story is a reminder that freedom is a precious thing.

kok: Abono chwng tongphlainai hwnwi bo uansogwi manya.
en: It is something that we should never take for granted.

kok: Chwng bebakno yoksajakkhe tongnani masaktharnai, tei chwng chini naharmungno yakarthai kwrwi.
en: We should all strive to be free, and we should never give up on our dreams.

kok: Chakra borok bai twiyung.
en: The Old Man and the Sea

kok: Santiago, khoroksa chakra Cuban ni ah romnai, bo charchi-bwrwi salromwi kaisa phano ah rommwi manyawui thangkha.
en: Santiago, an old Cuban fisherman, has gone eighty-four days without catching a fish.

kok: Boh kamini jottonislai chakra borok, tei chwraikuk, Manolin, bobai tak tei ah romna muchungjakliya tamni hinmale chakra borok belai talikha hamya.
en: He is the oldest man in the village, and the youngest, Manolin, no longer wants to fish with him because the old man is unlucky.

kok: Salsa, Santiago bini skiff twi ongkhor thangkha tei kaisa kotorma marlin no bosoi karkha.
en: One day, Santiago sets out in his skiff and hooks a giant marlin.

kok: Ah marlin aswkhe kotorma je abo skiff no hakchalo sotonwi twiyung bwkhak twlangkha.
en: The marlin is so big that it pulls the skiff far out to sea.

kok: Santaigo salnwi tei hornwi jora marlin bai bulaikha, phiya bo amono tubui manliya.
en: Santiago fights the marlin for two days and nights, but he cannot bring it in.

kok: Ah marlin belai hilik, tei ah chakra borok belai lengjakha.
en: The marlin is too heavy, and the old man is too tired.

kok: Paithago, ah marlin lengna chengkha.
en: Finally, the marlin begins to tire.

kok: Santiago marlin no ahyung suhrma bwkhak mankha, tei bo omono bwtharkha.
en: Santiago is able to get a harpoon into the marlin, and he kills it.

kok: Phiya ah marlin aswkhe kotor je Santiago omono rungo tubui manliya.
en: But the marlin is so big that Santiago cannot bring it into the boat.

kok: Bo ah marlin no rungni kuna khaka tei rukungo chogwi phirokna chengkha.
en: He ties the marlin to the side of the boat and begins to row back to shore.

kok: Sharkrokni bodol kaisa rungno rwtharkha, tei bohrok marlin no chana chengkha.
en: A school of sharks follows the boat, and they begin to eat the marlin.

kok: Santiago Sharkrokbai bulaikha, phiya bo bohrokno mwthak manliya.
en: Santiago fights the sharks off, but he cannot stop them all.

kok: Bo rukungo sogwima jora, marlin ni khorok tei khitung amswk simino torok sio.
en: By the time he reaches shore, only the head and the tail of the marlin are left.

kok: Kokthuna yokmung wngkha manjumung tei muchung samung yokmung kwrwnglamrok twih sapokjak pinlam tei ah internet no khobwi.
en: Freedom of the press is the freedom of communication and expression through mediums including printed media and the internet.

kok: Omo kaisa nangthai borokni manthai 19 kerongbwkhak bai sinijakma ah hayungkhobwi sakhlaimani borokni manthairok tei gosi chongmani 19 kerongbwkhak hayung rwkjak kokchaplaimung luku tei thwngrwngrwk manthairok.
en: It is a fundamental human right recognized by Article 19 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and reaffirmed in Article 19 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.

kok: Ah manthai yokmung bwkhak muchung samung sinijakma ahaino kaisa nangmani swkang tonghalok ah tongthokmani bagwi jotto kubun borokni manthairok.
en: The right to freedom of expression is recognized as a necessary precondition for the enjoyment of all other human rights.

kok: Kokthumnai yokmung wngkha kaisa sakdukma lukuchongraida bagwi nangnai.
en: Freedom of the press is essential for a healthy democracy.

kok: Omo habarokno kwbang kokthumjakmani gosimarok tei bohrokni hapang thikemung bwkhak romchrepmani.
en: It allows citizens to access information and to hold their government accountable.

kok: Omo khasrai khwlaima bwkhak bo chubao je jotto khorangrok khwnajak thwng, tei je ah lukurok nangkukma ongkhormarok kokthumjak thwng.
en: It also helps to ensure that all voices are heard, and that the public is informed about important issues.

kok: Laithangjak bisirokni bising, aro kwbangma sikrimungrok torwi tongo kokthumnai yokmung ah hayung yaksiyagra bwkhak.
en: In recent years, there have been growing threats to freedom of the press around the world.

kok: Haphangrok kerongrok phwnangwi tongo ah pinlam kasona bagwi, tei kokholnairok cheklekjagwi tei choprobjagwi tongo.
en: Governments have been using laws to restrict the media, and journalists have been harassed and attacked.

kok: Oh sikrimarok wngkha kaisa uansukrak uanama, tei bohrok tongthai bumungrok khaina nango.
en: These threats are a serious concern, and they need to be addressed.

kok: Chwng haino jotto bachana nangnai kokthumnai yokmungni bagwi.
en: We must all stand up for freedom of the press.

kok: Chwng ah kokhoknairokno saksoma bwkhak ah kokrikma koktunmarok kiriyawui sejana nangnai.
en: We must defend the right of journalists to report the news without fear of reprisal.

kok: Chwng yohkjak pinlam ongkhorlam rokno twichuruma makhainai tei chwng borokrokno porina bagwi khatorwma nangnai tei koktunmarok bakma simi kaisa dalbidal yaphangrok.
en: We must also support independent media outlets, and we must encourage people to read and share news from a variety of sources.

kok: Kokthumnai yokmung wngkha hamkukjak manthai.
en: Freedom of the press is a precious right.

kok: Chwng jotto yangtwi bokcho khaina nangno omono katirina bwkhak.
en: We must all do our part to protect it.

kok: Sal thangna chengkheno, chwrai omor kisa Raman mungwi rwngnok simi bini nok lama thangkha.
en: As the sun began to set, a young boy named Raman made his way home from school.

kok: Bo himwi thangphuru, bo khel khaikha lamakorokjak swi bono rwtharwitongo hwnwi.
en: As he walked, he noticed a stray dog following him.

kok: Ah swi leta-pata tei keram, phiya bini bayap wngna mwkhang tongo.
en: The dog was dirty and skinny, but it had a friendly face.

kok: Raman oh swino khairokjakha, haini bagwi bo bono bini nogo twlangna hwnwi chongwinakha.
en: Raman felt sorry for the dog, so he decided to take it home with him.

kok: Jephuru Raman nogo thangwi sogwikha, bo bini ma-phano swini bagwi sakha.
en: When Raman got home, he told his parents about the dog.

kok: Bohrok puila'o sakphorkha, phiya bohrok paithago swirokno tonina hwnwi gosi'ui nakha.
en: They were hesitant at first, but they eventually agreed to let him keep the dog.

kok: Raman swino Buddy hwnwi mung rwkha, tei bohrok dakti kiching kaham wnglaikha.
en: Raman named the dog Buddy, and they quickly became best friends.

kok: Buddy Ramanni bagwi homnino tongo, jesaphano wngthwng.
en: Buddy was always there for Raman, no matter what.

kok: Boh bono lamsukna bagwi duklam bwskango tongo jephuru bo nogo rwngnokni kiphilwi phaiphuru, tei bo khasrangna bagwi bini logi tongo jephuru bo tola uansukphan wngphuru.
en: He was there to greet him at the door when he came home from school, and he was there to comfort him when he was feeling down.

kok: Salsa, Raman berailwngo thwngwi tongphuru boh kwlainai bini yasku kukkha.
en: One day, Raman was playing in the park when he fell and scraped his knee.

kok: Boh kabna chengkha, tei Buddy bini gana khaprumwi phai bini kwsano swlakha.
en: He started to cry, and Buddy came running over to lick his wound.

kok: Swini kwchang bwslai Raman no samani simi holirwna chubakha, tei bo daktino bini kukma pogwi thangkha.
en: The dog's gentle tongue helped to soothe Raman's pain, and he soon forgot all about his injury.

kok: Raman bai Buddy thansakhe kwbangma bisi romwi tongthoktokkhe tonglaikha.
en: Raman and Buddy shared many happy years together.

kok: Bohrok himna thangkha, berailwngo khitarmung thwnglaikha, tei thuyamo thansa khe kwbaklai tonglaikha.
en: They went on walks, played fetch in the park, and cuddled up on the couch together.

kok: Agi phuru, khoroksa sikla tongo bwmung Rajiv bo kaisa kami bwsatete'o tongjao.
en: Once upon a time, there was a young man named Rajiv who lived in a small village.

kok: Boh bigra borokja, tei bo bai bini buma okhui'ui mangno matonglaijao.
en: He was a poor man, and he and his mother often went hungry.

kok: Salsa, Rajiv chamung rutukna bagwi bolongo thangnai hwnwi khao chabkha.
en: One day, Rajiv decided to go into the forest to find some food.

kok: Boh bolong bising twi himwi tong phuru, Rajiv phangsa siniya-nukya buphangno nukha.
en: As he was walking through the forest, Rajiv came across a strange tree.

kok: Oh buphang rangchak ni apples bai kupulwng, tei omo twi buphangrokno waisa phano Rajiv nukya kho.
en: The tree was covered in golden apples, and Rajiv had never seen anything like it before.

kok: Boh apple khosana bagwi aro sogwi kha, phiya boh abono tangkheno, ah buphang bono kok sakha.
en: He reached up to pick an apple, but as soon as he touched it, the tree spoke to him.

kok: "Ani apple no tatang di" hwnwi a buphang sakha. "Aborok nini bagwya."
en: "Do not touch my apples," the tree said. "They are not for you."

kok: Phiya Rajiv belai kheno okhuijak, tei boh ah buphangni kokno khwnaliya.
en: But Rajiv was hungry, and he didn't listen to the tree.

kok: Boh ah apple no khosa'ui wakhakha.
en: He picked an apple and took a bite.

kok: Boh abo hai khlaikheno, boh bini sago swlaijakma hai matongkha.
en: As soon as he did, he felt a strange change come over him.

kok: Boh bini sago belai phan kwrak phaijakmahai wngjakkha, tei saimankha bo mungsaswkle chaya khwlai kha hwnwi.
en: He felt stronger and more powerful, and he knew that he had done something wrong.

kok: "Ang wngkha Rangchakni Apple Buphang, " hwnwi ah buphang sakha. "Tei tabok nwng ani apple chamani, nwng swraimung mansinai."
en: "I am the Golden Apple Tree," the tree said. "And now that you have eaten my apple, you will be cursed.

kok: Je nini tongma bai nwng tei kha suksogwi mangwlak, tei nwng teibo manna bagwi rutukphwlai mangno matongnai."
en: You will never be satisfied with what you have, and you will always be searching for more."

kok: Aboni bagwino tabuk omo hai mangno wngwi matongkha.
en: And so it was.

kok: Khoroksa chwraisa bwrwi lama baichingo bachajak, kwchangmani ba kwlwibrajak.
en: The little girl stood on the street corner, shivering in the cold.

kok: Bo salni simino horkotra phalnani chaitokjak, phiya keba paiya.
en: She had been trying to sell matches all day, but no one had bought any.

kok: Bo khoroksa chwla phaima nuhurwi yakarnase nai tongkha.
en: She was about to give up when she saw a man approaching.

kok: Bo belai dojak, phiya bo chwraisa bwrwino nugwi bathak kha.
en: He looked like he was in a hurry, but he stopped when he saw the little girl.

kok: " Nwng oro saichung khe tamo khwlai?" bo swngkha.
en: "What are you doing out here all alone?" he asked.

kok: " ang horkotra phalnai nayo, " a chwraisa bwrwi sakha. " Phiya kebo abono paina se naiya."
en: "I'm trying to sell matches," the little girl said. "But no one will buy them."

kok: "Do, ang kaisa paisi wano, " a chwla sakha"phiya nwng ano gulap rwna nangnai aboni bodla."
en: "Well, I'll buy one," the man said "But you have to give me a rose in exchange."

kok: A chwraisa bwrwi wanajakha, phiya bo gosi kha.
en: The little girl was surprised, but she agreed.

kok: Bo nogo kharwi thang kha hakhe gulap naithokno kholwi tubukha.
en: She ran home and picked a beautiful rose.

kok: Hakhe bo a borokni aro phirogwi thang kha hakhe bono horkotra bai gulap yapharwi rwi kha.
en: Then she went back to the man and gave him the match and the rose.

kok: " Hambai, " a borok sakha "nwng belai maya gwnang bwrwi." bo horkotra na'ui mwchwng kha.
en: "Thank you," the man said "You're a kind girl." He took the match and lit it.

kok: Horjwlai torwi phaima bai, a bwrwi abono soidomni horkotra khe nukha.
en: As the flame grew, the little girl saw that it was a magic match.

kok: Abo kaisa naithok khe gulap bubarni motha se wngwi thangsio.
en: It turned into a beautiful bouquet of roses.

kok: A chwraisa bwrwi belai tongthok jakha.
en: The little girl was so happy.

kok: Relmalkhungrok kaisa mal bokcho bisirarok karwi rwkajakamnai tongkha.
en: Trains have been a vital part of transportation for centuries.

kok: Bohrok kaisa katijak, pharinai, tei poitognang himla kolok chalmarok beraina bwkhak tongo.
en: They are a safe, efficient, and reliable way to travel long distances.

kok: Haiphano, ah rellama swnammung sabrumbrum updates nango yapri tonma bwkhak ah kaiberainai nangmarok swlaimani bai.
en: However, the railroad industry requires regular updates to keep pace with the changing needs of passengers.

kok: Kaisa ah jottoni slai nangkukma updates ah relmalkhung nangma wngkha ah kwtal katijakma mwkhangrok thepamani.
en: One of the most important updates that trains need is the installation of new safety features.

kok: Tabukni bisirok bising, aro kisa kuchuk-profile relmalkhung akabikarok tongkha, bomo ha phunukjakma tongo ah kaham katijakma sumarokni bagwi nangma.
en: In recent years, there have been a number of high-profile train accidents, which have highlighted the need for better safety measures.

kok: Kwtal katijakma mwkhangrok ahaino sosol relmalkhung kasomung (PTC) relmalkhung bathakmani saksak khaimanma akabikarok kasogra chubai manai je belal doui beraimani wngkha eba je kubun relmalkhung bai thutaima bagwi tongo.
en: New safety features such as positive train control (PTC) can help prevent accidents by automatically stopping trains that are traveling too fast or that are about to collide with another train.

kok: Teikaisa nangkukma update je relmalkhung nangma wngkha ah kwtal tangsep thepamani.
en: Another important update that trains need is the installation of new technology.

kok: Ah wngthang bisingm relmalkhungrok phap kolrok bai cholijakha.
en: In the past, trains were powered by steam engines.

kok: Haiphano, phap kolrok wngkha pharimanya tei ah habar sitra rwkha.
en: However, steam engines are inefficient and pollute the environment.

kok: Tini, jottoni slai relmalkhungrok wngkha diesel kolrok eba pherang loriwnai kolkrok bai chalukjakha.
en: Today, most trains are powered by diesel engines or electric motors.

kok: Oh kolrok wngkha teibo pharinai tei habarma bayapma.
en: These engines are more efficient and environmentally friendly.

kok: Jora rwmani bising katijakma tei tansep updates bwkhak, relmalkungrok bo updated wngna bwkhak nango ah kaiberainairokni nangmarok gothokrima bwkhak.
en: In addition to safety and technology updates, trains also need to be updated to accommodate the needs of passengers.

kok: Tabukni bisirok bising, aro kaisa bangrwma tongkha ah lombor kaiberainairok je relmakhung bai berainai.
en: In recent years, there has been an increase in the number of passengers who travel by train.

kok: Omo railmalkhung sakao bwlai bohrokbangmani bwkhak dagi tongo, bomo kaisa kisa tongthotok tei tongthokma simari bagwi swnam mano.
en: This has led to overcrowding on trains, which can make for a less comfortable and enjoyable experience.

kok: Ani khapangni sajwkma, ang saimano nwng uanamansingsa wngjak ah habar pohor tei mwnakni bagwi.
en: My dear daughter, I know you've been wondering about the nature of light and darkness.

kok: Omo wngkha kotor swngmungrok, tei kaisa soisikwrwngrok bisirarok kwrwi kokphirokna bwkhak chaitongmani tongkha.
en: It's a big question, and one that scientists have been trying to answer for centuries.

kok: Phiya ani wansukmung ang nono kaisa khakepleng swbaisukrupmani rwi mano je nono buchina chubai mano kaisa kisa kaham bai.
en: But I think I can give you a simple explanation that will help you understand it a little better.

kok: Pohor wngkha kaisa phan prakar je twidurok bising beraimarok.
en: Light is a kind of energy that travels in waves.

kok: Chwng pohor nugwi mano tamni hinma omo chini mokolrogo habu tei ah retinano jolirwo, bomo wngkha kaisa pohor-bormanjak sakhanm ah mokolni ungkulugo.
en: We can see light because it enters our eyes and stimulates the retina, which is a light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye.

kok: Ah retina chini botomrok bwkhak phunukmari howu, bomo bohrokno mangpilirok haikhe kokswlaima wngo.
en: The retina sends signals to our brain, which interprets them as images.

kok: Mwnakma ah kwrwisani pohor wngkha.
en: Darkness is the absence of light.

kok: Jephuru aro pohor kwrwi, chwng mungsaphano nukya.
en: When there is no light, we can't see anything.

kok: Pohor tei mwnakma wngkha kainwi judarok, phiya bohrok bo kainwi digirokni ah puisa ni solai wngo.
en: Light and darkness are two opposites, but they're also two sides of the same coin.

kok: Chwngno phunuknani bagwi pohor nango, phiya mwnakma bo nangkukma wngkha.
en: Light is needed for us to see, but darkness is also important.

kok: Mwnakma chwngno lenglana tei thuna bwkhak chubao.
en: Darkness helps us to rest and sleep.

kok: Omo bo kaisa sinai simanwi bisingnikok tei uanamasingsa swnamo.
en: It also creates a sense of mystery and wonder.

kok: Aswkno teiwaisa jora nwng horo phataro phuru, kaisa mukphliksa nadi ah mwnama chajakma bwkhak.
en: So next time you're outside at night, take a moment to appreciate the darkness.

kok: Omo haino pohor nangmaswk nangkukma, tei omo thani omo sakni naithong tongo.
en: It's just as important as light, and it has its own beauty.

kok: Mayachamani abo wngkha borokni bisingo kaisa nangkukmani koboljaknai tongmung kaham.
en: Kindness is one of the most important virtues that a person can possess.

kok: Abono khe bebak borokrokno gosi'ui nao tei uabo uansok rwo, tei abobaino mungsaya mungsle swngcharo swlaimung bo sok phayo.
en: It is the act of being considerate and thoughtful of others, and it is something that can make a real difference in the world.

kok: Mayachama kokthai, mwnwima, eba chubana bagwi yak pholokmani abohrok bai khoroksaswk ni sal chwngsa rwi mano tei bohrokni sak baithang khabacharwi mano.
en: A kind word, a smile, or a helping hand can go a long way to brighten someone's day and make them feel better about themselves.

kok: Nini mayano phunuknani kwbangma dalbidal lama tongo.
en: There are many different ways to show kindness.

kok: Nini kamini nokgantirogo bo jora rwimano eba nok kwrwirokni bagwi bo, nwng poito chamani abotwi ma-pha kwrwirokni tongthayo bo yapharwi mano, eba nwng bui tekto kotor manjaknairokni kokno bo ahaino khwna'ui tongwi mano.
en: You can volunteer your time at a local soup kitchen or homeless shelter, donate to a charity that you believe in, or simply be a good listener to someone who is going through a tough time.

kok: Nini samung kotor eba kotoi phano wngthwng abo mungsa wngya, mayachamani khe jesa phuru phano kaham.
en: No matter how big or small the act, kindness is always appreciated.

kok: Oh swngchar belai kheno maya nango.
en: The world needs more kindness.

kok: Abo samung khe kotoise phiya belai kotor swlaimung tubui mano.
en: It is a simple act that can make a big difference.

kok: Abobaino teisa phuru khe sabono chuba'ui man abono naitukdi, chubana muchungyarok tawngdi tei yak pholokna muchungyarok tawngdi.
en: So next time you see someone who could use a little help, don't hesitate to reach out and lend a hand.

kok: Nwng bohrokni salno kaham phano khwlaiwi mano.
en: You might just make their day.

kok: Kaisa maya chamani phunukmari khe Kaham Samaritan.
en: One classic example of kindness is the story of the Good Samaritan.

kok: O kothoma o, khoroksa borok bujak kha tei thwitwtwi khe lamao yakarwi kwlangjak kha.
en: In this story, a man is beaten and left for dead on the side of the road.

kok: Khoroknwi borok laiwi thangkha, phiya bohrok bono chubaya.
en: Two men pass by, but they do not help him.

kok: Abobaino, waitham o sokphainai borok, bo wng kha Samaritan, a derajak borokno chubana bagwi bathak kha.
en: However, a third man, who is a Samaritan, stops to help the injured man.

kok: Sak bokocho yapharmung wngkha kaisa borok khoroksa sak manwi rwmani thwimani yak ulo.
en: Organ donation is the process of giving organs or tissues to someone else after death.

kok: Obo sak manwi swlaina bagwi muchung tongnairokni bagwi lang thangcharwna tei hamcharwna samung kwlayo.
en: It can save lives and improve the quality of life for people who are waiting for transplants.

kok: Dal bidal ni sakmanwi tongo aro baksa ba yapharwi mano romdi, kidney, liver, bwkha, lungs tei pancrease rok.
en: There are many different types of organs that can be donated, including kidneys, livers, hearts, lungs, and pancreases.

kok: Bokobai rok yapharwi mano romdi, bekreng, bukur, bwkhani valve tei mokolrok.
en: Tissues that can be donated include bone, skin, heart valves, and corneas.

kok: Sak bokocho yapharthani dal bidal hamari manwi mano.
en: There are many benefits to organ donation.

kok: Yachaknaini bagwi sak bokocho manmani langmani kaisa kwtal langma manthai hai.
en: For the recipient, organ donation can mean a new lease on life.

kok: Yapharnaini bagwikhe sak bokocho yapharmani bisingtwi o hayungo khoroksa juda borok tei langma mwthangnai wngwi bachaui mano.
en: For the donor, organ donation can be a way to make a difference in the world and help to save lives.

kok: Kisaswk bwkhao muitu narwkthai tongo tumung nwng sak bokocho yapharna muchungwi tongkhe.
en: There are a few things to keep in mind if you are considering organ donation.

kok: Puila, nwng umor bisi 18 ni swlai kwbang tei sak kaham tongna nangnai.
en: First, you must be over the age of 18 and in good health.

kok: Ulnwio, nini kaisa gosijak driver ID tongna nangnai.
en: Second, you must have a valid driver's license or state ID.

kok: Ulthamo, nwng jesakhebo yasi mari ma rwnai sak bokocho yapharna bagwi.
en: Third, you must sign a consent form to donate your organs.

kok: Nwng tumung teibo swrwngna muchungwi tongkhe sak bokocho yapharmungno twywi, oro kwbang lam tongo nini bagwi.
en: If you are interested in learning more about organ donation, there are many resources available to you.

kok: Nwng o website o habwi mano United Netwrok for Organ Donation eba www.unos.org.
en: You can visit the website of the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) at www.unos.org.

kok: Hayakheba nwng nini amchaini gana ginio Organ Procurement Organization (OPO) o.
en: You can also contact your local organ procurement organization (OPO).

kok: Chathaini sakduk khali kwthwng chamung tei hamya chathai no karma simiya.
en: Healthy food is not just about eating salads and avoiding junk food.

kok: Omo juda-juda chathaino chamasiya nini sakni je bolimung tei bahai khe kahamkwrwngkhe samung khai.
en: It's about eating a variety of foods that give your body the nutrients it needs to function properly.

kok: Oro bwthai, muikwthwng, jotto bwthai bwchwlwi tei hankwrwi protein khobjago.
en: This includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and lean protein.

kok: Aro kwbangma juda juda sadukni chakjaknai lama tongo, tei khoroksa borokni sago samung khaikhe tei khoroksa ni sago samung khaigwlak.
en: There are many different ways to eat healthy, and what works for one person may not work for another.

kok: Surani mannakhe niniro tamkhe samung khainai tei nini tongmung chamung bwkhak swnamdi.
en: The key is to find what works for you and make it a part of your lifestyle.

kok: Kaisa lama sakdukni chajaknai kwlai khainakhe nogo teibo uramuram khe songdi.
en: One way to make healthy eating easier is to cook at home more often.

kok: Oro nono teibo kaswkma rio nini chathai swraimanwi sakao tei nono sadukma saithani gosirio.
en: This gives you more control over the ingredients in your food and allows you to make healthier choices.

kok: Tei kaisa lama sakdukjak chathani swnamna hwnkhe nini chamungo kisasa swlaidi.
en: Another way to eat healthier is to make small changes to your diet.

kok: Phunukamari karwi, nwng jora rwi chengwi mano kaisa bwthai sebugwi eba mwikwthwng nini chathayo salo waisa khobkhe.
en: For example, you could start by adding one serving of fruits or vegetables to your meals each day.

kok: Eba, nwng kulumgwnang chamung simi sakdukmano chongwi swlaimano.
en: Or, you could swap out unhealthy snacks for healthier options.

kok: Nini chamungo kisasa swlai mankhe jora lai thepaimano tei nini sakdukno kotorma pherwimano.
en: Making small changes to your diet can add up over time and make a big difference to your health.

kok: Haini bagwi takiridi nwng amjukthani tei bomo nini ro samung khai.
en: So don't be afraid to experiment and find what works for you.

kok: Sakduk chathani nini chamung tamo simi ya, phiyaba nwng bahai khe chamung cha.
en: Eating healthy is not just about what you eat, but also about how you eat.

kok: Twrwk-twrwk khe chamani tei khakupulungwi nono nini chathayo teibo tongthok chubaimano tei kisa chamabai nono olo khapungrio.
en: Eating slowly and mindfully can help you enjoy your food more and feel satisfied after eating less.

kok: Ah twijlang wngkha kaisa kotor bisingkok gang thai, jotto dal malmatarokni nok.
en: The ocean is a vast and mysterious place, home to all sorts of creatures.

kok: Chikonsa plankton simi kotorma ahyung, ah twijlang langma bai pungjak.
en: From the smallest plankton to the largest whales, the ocean is teeming with life.

kok: Tei kainwi thairok ah twijwlango solai kwrwi.
en: And no two places in the ocean are the same.

kok: Twijlang habarlam thwgwi bini sakni manthokya thepama oro buphang-uaphang tei malmatarok tongo, ah kubui tonghalokrok habar ni omo yakchakjak bwkhak.
en: Each ocean ecosystem has its own unique set of plants and animals, adapted to the specific conditions of its environment.

kok: Kaisa jottoni swlai dalbidal kwthang thairok oh hating ni hwnkhe coral reef.
en: One of the most biodiverse places on Earth is the coral reef.

kok: Coral reefs tunglulu, thene twirok ah hayungni yaksiyagra bising naituk mano, tei bohrok wngkha kuar dalbidal malmatarokni nok.
en: Coral reefs are found in warm, shallow waters around the world, and they are home to a wide variety of creatures.

kok: Coral reefs chikonsa malamatarokbai swnam jago abono Coral polyps hwnwi ringjago.
en: Coral reefs are made up of tiny animals called coral polyps.

kok: Oh polyps kaisa kwrak hwima, calcium carbonate mangkhong, kaisa reef swnamna bwkhak jora rwngwi obo swnamjago.
en: These polyps secrete a hard, calcium carbonate skeleton, which builds up over time to form a reef.

kok: Coral reefs kaisa kuar dalbidal ah rokni baagwi kaisa nok bagwi mano, bekereng kwrwi rok, tei kubun twibomni kok langma.
en: Coral reefs provide a home for a wide variety of fish, invertebrates, and other marine life.

kok: Beraikhiri tei swnamphimani bohrok nangkukma wngwimano.
en: They are also important for tourism and recreation.

kok: Talikhahamya, Coral reefs wngkha uanamung bising kwbangma bwchwlwi rokni simi, nobartwibar swlaijakma khobwinai, ebrumrwmani, tei belai ah rommani.
en: Unfortunately, coral reefs are under threat from a number of factors, including climate change, pollution, and overfishing.

kok: Tumungno chwng Coral reefs no bachirina bagwi tangmung naya hwnkhe, bohrok homanwi kwmai thangnai.
en: If we do not take action to protect coral reefs, they will be lost forever.

kok: Salsa, kaisa bwrwi sikli mung Michelle bini nokganani Coral reef no naituk bera tongmani.
en: One day, a young girl named Michelle was exploring the coral reef near her home.

kok: Bo bokhongrokno nai tongmani bini rungma thayo thepana hwnwi.
en: She was looking for shells to add to her collection.

kok: Ah phiyokjak bulainairok marirok wngkha uramuram nangma amjokmungrok bohrokni soima tei golirwma.
en: The trials of freedom fighters are often major tests of their endurance and resolve.

kok: Ah mwkhang khamunsukmani solyarokni bising, bohrok ah phan choyai bulainani bagwi bohrok poito khaima bising ma naituknai.
en: In the face of overwhelming odds, they must find the strength to continue fighting for what they believe in.

kok: Bohrokni khachongjakrok wngkha uramuram kuchuk, iko bohrok bohrokni borok phiyoknani bagwi bulaimani.
en: Their expectations are often high, as they are fighting for the freedom of their people.

kok: Bohrok jottomanwi yakarna bwkhak nanganw, bohrokni sakni langmarokno khobwinai, bohrokni alongrok manna bwkhak thangkhe.
en: They must be willing to sacrifice everything, including their own lives, in order to achieve their goals.

kok: Kaisa jottoni swlai mungkoto phyokjakma bulainairok laihbuma ni bising wngkha Nelson Mandela.
en: One of the most famous freedom fighters in history is Nelson Mandela.

kok: Madela 27 bisirok along bising katikha bini bulaima kwthaiya apartheid South Africa o.
en: Mandela spent 27 years in prison for his fight against apartheid in South Africa.

kok: Haiphano ah kwrakjakrok bo dadakdidik wngmani, bo jesakhe phano khakamung yakarya.
en: Despite the hardships he faced, he never gave up hope.

kok: Bo along simi kaisa kwrakma bodolokra khe ongkhorkha, tei paithago South Africa no kaisa kwchangthotok kuplung twimung lukuchongraida bwkhak twlangkha.
en: He emerged from prison as a stronger leader, and eventually led South Africa to a peaceful transition to democracy.

kok: Tei kaisa mungkoto phiyokjak bulainai wngkha Mahatma Gandhi.
en: Another famous freedom fighter is Mahatma Gandhi.

kok: Gandhi India ni phiyokjakma ninangrimung twih walaiya kasoma bwkhak twlangkha.
en: Gandhi led India's independence movement through nonviolent resistance.

kok: Bo poito khaijak je walaimani aswkno teibo walaimani bagwkha dagi mano, tei je aswkno ah lama kubui phiyokma manna bwkhak hwnkhe kwchangthotok kupulung kokmarok bisingtwih wngkha.
en: He believed that violence would only lead to more violence, and that the only way to achieve true freedom was through peaceful means.

kok: Bini khlaimunga wngkha tangmanjak, tei India bini yokjakamani 1947 bising mano.
en: His methods were successful, and India gained its independence in 1947.

kok: Ah marirok phiyokjak bulainairok wngkha kasa muitonarwkma ah yakarma je borok bohrokni poitorokni bagwi jeshpahano khainani tiyar wngjak.
en: The trials of freedom fighters are a reminder of the sacrifices that people are willing to make for their beliefs.

kok: Bohrokni kothomarok wngkha kaisa jotto chini bagwi khasrangrwnai, tei bohrok chwng muito khairio je chwng jesakhe phano khajamung tayakardi, jesaphano bahai ah solyarok khakama manma.
en: Their stories are an inspiration to us all, and they remind us that we should never give up hope, no matter how difficult the odds may seem.

kok: Ah borok-hai chengmani wngkha kaisa kokkhak salaikok je bisirraokni bagwi kokchirlaijak wngmani.
en: The beginning of humanity is a topic that has been debated for centuries.

kok: Aro wngkha kwbangma juda juda kokbwkrairok tongo bahai tei buphuru puila borokrok phaima bwkhak bagwi, phiya wngkubui karwi kebo saimanya.
en: There are many different theories about how and when humans first came to be, but no one knows for sure.

kok: Baksa soisikwrwngrok poito khaikha je borokrok mwkhrarokni simi hamkrai wngo chiraisai bisirok sakao, jephuru kubunrok poito khayo je chwng kaisa kuchuk phan bai swnamjakha.
en: Some scientists believe that humans evolved from apes over millions of years, while others believe that we were created by a higher power.

kok: Khauarya bahaikhe chwng phaima tongkha, aro mungsa poito chaya wngya je borokrok tongo kaisa manthokya dahlrok.
