en: Regardless of how we came to be, there is no doubt that humans are a unique species.

kok: Chwng jottoi malmatarok wngkha je ah karon khlaimanmung bwkhak, swnamma, tei kok manjulaima.
en: We are the only animals that have the ability to reason, create, and communicate.

kok: Chwng bo jottoi malmatarok unkha je phanbokma tei khairokmung bagwi ah chakphan tongo.
en: We are also the only animals that have the capacity for empathy and compassion.

kok: Oh tonghamrok chwngno mahmlai swnamo tei ah torwkma malmata bugraha simi chwngo swkagwi thepama.
en: These qualities make us special and set us apart from the rest of the animal kingdom.

kok: Kaisa manwirok je borokno aswk mantholya swnammarok wngkha chini pharimung thansa samung tei logichalukma bwkhak.
en: One of the things that makes humans so unique is our ability to cooperate and work together.

kok: Oh pharimung chwngno kutuk dopharok tisama bwkhak tei unanamani tangseprok swnamma bai gosikha.
en: This ability has allowed us to build complex societies and create amazing technologies.

kok: Omo chwngno bo gosikha baksa bataimarok mechenma bwkhak je chwng kaisa dahl malaima tongma.
en: It has also allowed us to overcome some of the challenges that we face as a species.

kok: Phunukmari karwi, chwng bemarokni bagwi hammungrok hamkrai bwkha mankha, lamarok swnamma kolok chalmungrok beraima bwkhak, tei ahaino ah tal sakao borokrokno tonima.
en: For example, we have been able to develop cures for diseases, create ways to travel long distances, and even put humans on the moon.

kok: Aow, borokrok chasukjakya.
en: Of course, humans are not perfect.

kok: Chwng kotor kuar hamya aboni logi kotor kuar kaham chukjak wngkha.
en: We are capable of great evil as well as great good.

kok: Chini sakni hagiri tei chini saksakrokno baikhrupmung bwkhak chini thani khlaimanma tongo.
en: We have the potential to destroy our own planet and ourselves.

kok: Kanchum ahaino kaisa amtwinoamwtwi tongdal swlaimai bising twi kokswbaikhrupjak khai mano richum, yaklapchu, manwikhwnwirok, naithokrwmung, khwnai, tei bisingni rikmani.
en: Fashion can be defined as a constantly changing style in clothing, footwear, accessories, makeup, hair, and interior design.

kok: Omo wngkha kaisa sak-kok samung tei kaisa borokni saksuar, morji tei hodarwk tongborom yaktwima bwkhak phwnangjak mano.
en: It is a form of self-expression and can be used to convey a person's personality, mood, and social status.

kok: Omo kaisa kubui kebengmung je bolongrok, twiuarrok, tei ahaino borokno chaya khaimani.
en: It's a serious problem that's harming forests, lakes, and even people.

kok: Acid watwi wngmani jephuru chemicals kahai sulfur dioxide pherang thong bai nokbar ni bising twi yakarjakmani, swnamnokrok, tei malkhungrok.
en: Acid rain is caused when chemicals like sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxide are released into the air by power plants, factories, and cars.

kok: Oh chemicals twi bai wngphirok ah nokbarkhung bising acids sakmung wngo, bomo hwnkhe watwi wngwi hao kwlaiyo, kothor, eba syari.
en: These chemicals react with water in the atmosphere to form acids, which then fall to the ground in rain, snow, or fog.

kok: Acid watwi buphangrok piyakmung khaimano bohrokni bwlairokno teibo acidic swnamo.
en: Acid rain can damage trees by making their leaves more acidic.

kok: Omo bwlairokno kormo khlaima bwkhak tei swkraina bagwi wngwi mano, je buphang no phankwrwi khlaimano tei tiebo khanangkrak bemar bwkhak omo swnamo.
en: This can cause the leaves to turn yellow and fall off, which can weaken the tree and make it more susceptible to disease.

kok: Acid watwi ah rokno bwthar mano tei kubun twini langma ah twino belai acidiic swnamawi.
en: Acid rain can also kill fish and other aquatic life by making the water too acidic.

kok: Jora rwmani bising, acid watwi nok kotorrok tei mangthongrok bohrok swnamjakmani ah manwi-khwnai rokno cha'ui khibimani bai.
en: In addition, acid rain can damage buildings and statues by corroding the materials they're made of.

kok: Aro kwbangma manwirok tongo je acid watwi no khaina bagwi khlaijak mano.
en: There are a number of things that can be done to reduce acid rain.

kok: Kaisa hwnkhe sraisrai tangphan mukrok bwkhak swlaijak mano, ahaino solar tei pherang nokbar.
en: One is to switch to cleaner energy sources, such as solar and wind power.

kok: Tei kaisa wngkha ebrumruma kasomarok swnamnokrogo tei pherang thong rogo thepamani.
en: Another is to install pollution controls on factories and power plants.

kok: Tei paithago, chwng jotto chini bokocho twi tamo khaiman hwnkhe kisa chalukani, teibo swnamphimani, tei tangphan noo teibo khatiwui phwnangnani.
en: And finally, we can all do our part by driving less, recycling more, and using energy more efficiently.

kok: Aswkno teiwaisa phuru nwng watwi bankundri nukhe, acid watwini bagwi wansukdi.
en: So the next time you see a rainstorm, think about acid rain.

kok: Klaus wngkha khoroksa belai hoku nwngrak.
en: Klaus was a heavy smoker.

kok: Bo salo kaisa cigarettes bokhok nwngo, tei bo omo aswkno 20 bisirok saka karwi khlai phai tongo.
en: He smoked a pack of cigarettes a day, and he had been doing so for over 20 years.

kok: Bo saimano je hoku nwngmani bini sakduk ni bagwi hamya hwnwi, phiya bo abono khakama bwkhak yakar manya.
en: He knew that smoking was bad for his health, but he couldn't seem to quit.

kok: Salsa, Klaus lahar tola himwi thangphuru bo khoroksa siniya borok no nukha.
en: One day, Klaus was walking down the street when he saw a strange man.

kok: Ah borok kaisa kuphur coat kanjak wngkha tei bini yago kaisa siniya manwi tongo.
en: The man was wearing a long white coat and had a strange device in his hand.

kok: "Khwnagradi, " Klaus sakha. "nwng tamo khai tong?"
en: "Excuse me," Klaus said. "What are you doing?"

kok: "Ang khoroksa soisinai," ah borok sakha. "Ang kaisa kwtal manwi o samung khai tongo je borok rokno hoku nwngmani yakarna chubachu khai manai."
en: "I'm a scientist," the man said. "I'm working on a new device that will help people quit smoking."

kok: "Kubuino?" Klaus sakha "amo kaisa uanamasinsa!"
en: "Really?" Klaus said "That's amazing!"

kok: "In', omo wngma," ah borok sakha.
en: "Yes, it is," the man said.

kok: "Oh manwi nono teikaisa bukcha thayo howui mano boro nwng hoku nwngmani nini sakduk saka ah sago kwlaima nugwi manai."
en: "This device will send you to another space where you will be able to see the effects of smoking on your health."

kok: "Omo kaisa poito chaya wngjago, " Klaus sakha." ang omo chaitok nainai."
en: "That sounds incredible," Klaus said. "I'd like to try it."

kok: Ah borok mwnwikha. "Belai kahamno, " bo sakha. "Haino oh manwini bising yapri rwdi tei ang oh tangsepno chengnai."
en: The man smiled. "Very well," he said. "Just step into this device and I'll start the process."

kok: Klaus yapri amri rwkha ah manwiyo tei ah borok bini ungkulukni duklam sowui rwkha.
en: Klaus stepped into the device and the man closed the door behind him.

kok: Ani kakani malkhung wngkha bumuk-alaida mal.
en: My uncle's car was a resource-intensive beast.

kok: Omo thok chao khoroksa twikangjak mangingong kahai, tei omoni hoku pipe kosom hoku chumuirok ongkharwma.
en: It guzzled petrol like a thirsty camel, and its exhaust belched out clouds of black smoke.

kok: Phiya omo wngkha kaisa kolok malkhung, ani kakani bagwi, bini bihik, tei bini maktham chwrairok bagwi kwbangma khotol bai.
en: But it was also a spacious vehicle, with plenty of room for my uncle, his wife, and their three children.

kok: Salsa, ani kaka bini nukhungni borokno chalugwi twlangmani ah twirwkung bwkhak bojora bo thok paijakha.
en: One day, my uncle was driving his family to the beach when he ran out of petrol.

kok: Bo kaisa digi gurukha ah lamani nar bwkhak tei himna bwkhak chengkha ah ganani thok bathakthai bwkhak.
en: He pulled over to the side of the road and started to walk to the nearest petrol station.

kok: Bo himwi tongphuru, bo kaisa bohrok buthup nukha kaisa malkhung yaksiyagra kitingjak je bai thangkha.
en: As he was walking, he saw a group of people gathered around a car that had broken down.

kok: Ah malkhung wngkha kaisa teibo belai thok-chaya naidal ani kakani slai, tei omo bo belai chikonsa wngkha.
en: The car was a much more fuel-efficient model than my uncle's, and it was also much smaller.

kok: Ani kaka ah baijak malkhung sakao borok samung tangma bwkhak naina bathakkha.
en: My uncle stopped to watch the people work on the broken car.

kok: Bo khuarjak bahai daitono bohrok omo thepama bwkhak chukha, tei bo naisikha je bohrok kaisa kwbang kisa bumukrok bo wngma slai phwnangmani wngkha.
en: He was impressed by how quickly they were able to fix it, and he also noticed that they were using a lot less resources than he was.

kok: Bo saimankha je bo oh borokni simi kwbang swrwng mano.
en: He realized that he could learn a lot from these people.

kok: Jephuru ani kaka nogo sokkha, bo bini bihikno sakha bo tamo nukha.
en: When my uncle got home, he told his wife about what he had seen.

kok: Bo gosikha je bohrok kwbang swrwngmano ah borokni simi je ah malkung baijakno thepakha.
en: She agreed that they could learn a lot from the people who had fixed the broken car.

kok: Bohrok ani kakani malkhung phalna bwkhak tei teibo thok-chaya naidal bwkhak chongkha.
en: They decided to sell my uncle's car and buy a more fuel-efficient model.

kok: 2023 ni tamblangmolo, kutung lilakmung Los Angeles doyungo tokkha.
en: In the summer of 2023, a heat wave hit the city of Los Angeles.

kok: Tungmarirok khwinani chengkha, tei borok rok philik manna chengkha.
en: The temperatures were soaring, and the people were starting to get restless.

kok: Nok kaisa o, kaibwrwi nukhungno kwchangkhe tongna chaitok tongo.
en: In one house, a family of four was trying to stay cool.

kok: Mapha song, John bai Mary, khoroknwino nokni simi samung khayo, tei bohrokni khoroknwi bwsarok, Sarah bai Michael, bohrokni rwngnokni samung khaina chaitok tongo.
en: The parents, John and Mary, were both working from home, and their two children, Sarah and Michael, were trying to do their schoolwork.

kok: Nok bisingni sipjaknairok nobar thapa kupulungkhe cholitongo, Phiya oro tabuk bo oro kutungkho.
en: The fans in the house were running full blast, but it was still hot.

kok: John ol manmwi manma chengkha tabukni tangsep sijaknai bai.
en: John was starting to get interested in the latest fan technology.

kok: Bo aboni bagwi porijak je kwtal sapokthaih sipjaknai je nokno kwchang khaimano sirisiti sipjaknai slai teibo samung khaimano.
en: He had read about a new type of fan that could cool a room more efficiently than traditional fans.

kok: Bo kisa rutukrwkh khaina hwnwi chongwi nakha tumung naina bagwi bo kaisa naituk mankha hwnwi je bini nukhungo samungkhai mannano.
en: He decided to do some research to see if he could find one that would work for his family.

kok: John website kaisa mankha je jadrepod sipjaknai phaljago.
en: John found a website that sold a variety of fans.

kok: Bo ayangtwi browsed khainaikha juda juda sipjaknai sapokthaino twi, tei bo paithago sipjaknai naitukmankha je bo wansukani bini nukhungni bagwi samung khaiyanw hwnwi.
en: He browsed through the different types of fans, and he eventually found a fan that he thought would work for his family.

kok: Oh sipjaknai "oroiporoiwi gundrijak sipjaknai", hwnwi ringjago teibo rwjak gundrijak nokbar hwnwi swnamjakha je nokno kwchango khaikha sirisiti sipjaknai rokni slai teibo samung khaimano.
en: The fan was called the "Disorderly Vortex Fan", and it was designed to create a vortex of air that would cool the room more efficiently than traditional fans.

kok: John sipjaknai dagimungrikha, tei aboni olo sokphaikha.
en: John ordered the fan, and it arrived a few days later.

kok: Bo tongma nogo thepai rwkha, tei bo daktino chajak thangkhe bahai kaham khe abo samung khai.
en: He set it up in the living room, and he was immediately impressed by how well it worked.

kok: Tongmung kahamrok wngkha ah loirok tei yagul samungrok je kubun borok ni bagwi borom phunugo.
en: Good manners are the habits and actions that show respect for other people.

kok: Bohrok tongmungrok swrwngjak wngkha je ah rangchak raida sakao, je samarok kubunrokno bo haikhe no saknangma khaidi je nwng saknangjakna muchungjakma khai.
en: They are learned behaviors that are based on the Golden Rule, which says to treat others the way you want to be treated.

kok: Tongmung kahamrok wngkha nangkukma tamni hinba bohrok ah hayungno kaisa teibo tongna bwkhak tonthok thai.
en: Good manners are important because they make the world a more pleasant place to live.

kok: Bohrok kaisa sinai simana'ui hoda swnamna bwkhak chubao tei borok no teibo kwchagthotok tei boromjak uansukma swnamo.
en: They help to create a sense of community and make people feel more comfortable and respected.

kok: Aro wngkha kwbangma juda juda sapokthaihrok tongmung kahamrok, phiya baksa ah belai nangkukma kaisarok khobma tongkwchang wngdok, boromrwjak wngdok, tongkwthar wngdok, kubunrok larojak wnngdok, tei bojak.
en: There are many different types of good manners, but some of the most important ones include being polite, being respectful, being honest, being considerate of others, and being responsible.

kok: Tangkwchang wnngdok kokmarok wngdok kwchangkhai tei borom rwjak kubunrok bwkhak.
en: Being polite means being courteous and respectful to others.

kok: Omo "khapur" tei "hambai nono," samani khobmarok ah duklam khulukma rommani kubunrokni bagwi, tei jephuru khoroksaswk koksai tongkha khunjukainai khwnamani.
en: This includes saying "please" and "thank you," holding the door open for others, and listening attentively when someone is speaking.

kok: Boromjak wngdok kokmarok kubunrokno saknangmani borom tei borom rwma bai, khauraya bohrokni omor, bosong, sir, tongthar, eba hodarwk tongborom.
en: Being respectful means treating others with dignity and respect, regardless of their age, race, gender, religion, or social status.

kok: Omo kubunrokno chengta khlaimai khobyawui, jephuru bohrok koksai tongphuru bohrokno kasuyawui, tei bohrokni khachongmarokno khwnamani ahaino tumung nwng bohrok bai gosiya phano.
en: This includes not making fun of others, not interrupting them when they are speaking, and listening to their opinions even if you disagree with them.

kok: Tongkwthar wngdok kokmarok kubuikuk tei sakthar wngdok.
en: Being honest means being truthful and sincere.

kok: Omo tala saya eba phemlokmani khobyawui, tei khachongmungrok bagwi sakbwskang wngdok.
en: This includes not lying or cheating, and being upfront about your intentions.

kok: Larokjak wngdok kubunrok kokmarok wngdok wansukmung tei chubamung.
en: Being considerate of others means being thoughtful and helpful.

kok: Omo saimanri wngdok khobmarok ah kubunrokni nangmarok tei nwng tamo bohrokno tongthotok wansukma swnamma bwkha khlaimani.
en: This includes being aware of the needs of others and doing what you can to make them feel comfortable.

kok: Phwrwngnai, ang wansukha bayaprok wngkha kaisa belai nangkukma manwirok langmani bagwi.
en: Teacher, I think friends are one of the most important things in life.

kok: Aro borok tongo je chini bagwi tongo jephuru chwng bohrokno nango, je chwngno mwnwi rio, tei je chwngno borok haikhe tornani chubao.
en: They're the people who are there for us when we need them, who make us laugh, and who help us grow as people.

kok: Jephuru ang chwrai phuru, ang kaisa torsukya hai.
en: When I was younger, I was kind of immature.

kok: Ang kubuino buchiya bayapsong ni nangkukmano.
en: I didn't really understand the importance of friendship.

kok: Ang wansukha omo jotto tongthok tongmani hwnwi tei thansa khai manwirok khailaimani.
en: I thought it was all about having fun and doing things together.

kok: Phiya ang haino torwi thangkha, ang saimankha je bayapsong wngkha aboni slai teibo kwbang.
en: But as I've gotten older, I've realized that friendship is so much more than that.

kok: Omo kaisa khoroksaswk kok sajaknai tongmani bwkhak je nono buchinai, je sabono nwng poito khaimano, tei nwng saboni sakao yakar mano.
en: It's about having someone to talk to who understands you, who you can trust, and who you can count on.

kok: Ani bayaprok ani bagwi rwja tei kepher bisingtwih tongwi tongo.
en: My friends have been there for me through thick and thin.

kok: Borok ano ani kahama tei hamya phuru nukjak, tei borok ano homnino hamjago tei twichurujak khayo ano.
en: They've seen me at my best and my worst, and they've always loved and supported me.

kok: Abo ano ani kutuk jorarogo twih chubakha, tei bohrok ano mwnwi rio jephuru ang omo kwbang nangjak tongphuru.
en: They've helped me through tough times, and they've made me laugh when I've needed it most.

kok: Ang saimano je ang hominino ani bayaprokni sakao yakar mano.
en: I know that I can always count on my friends.

kok: Bohrok mohai borok je ang saksak yaksiyagra tongwi mano, tei je ang saimano ani bagwi homino tongnai.
en: They're the people who I can be myself around, and who I know will always be there for me.

kok: Ang belai khatung khajak bohrokni bayapsongni bagwi, tei ang saimano je ani langma bohrok kwrwi khe kwrwikuk wngkhamu.
en: I'm so grateful for their friendship, and I know that my life would be much poorer without them.

kok: Jephuru ani bwsai bini puila computer mankha, ah technology tabukbo omo chengjora bising siko.
en: When my husband acquired his first computer, the technology was still in its infancy.

kok: Ah computer kotor, hilikma kol je kwbangma thai nakha chini tongmani nokbisingo.
en: The computer was a large, bulky machine that took up a significant amount of space in our living room.

kok: Abo wngkha belai morokjak, tei chwng amono naimanna bwkhak dalbidal talrok romwi khatina nangkha.
en: It was also very expensive, and we had to save up for several months to be able to afford it.

kok: Ani bwsai belai tongthokjak wngkha bini kwtal computer ni bagwi, tei bo damrwirok swrwngmanio jora lairio bahaikhe omo no phwnangna hwnwi.
en: My husband was very excited about his new computer, and he spent hours learning how to use it.

kok: Bo daktino khoroksa kwrwng wngwi thangkha phwnangmani bising twi ah computer rutukrwk khaima bwkhak, laihrok swina, tei thwngmung thwngnarok.
en: He quickly became an expert in using the computer to do research, write papers, and play games.

kok: Ang aswk ol manjakya ah computer no phwnangmani bising, phiya ang ah suvidha ni bagwi chajakma wngjakha amo bo phwnangwi rwthairok rwi manma bwkhak tei kubun samungrok khaima je kaisa bijapnok eba khatinok bwkhak beraitongthok bwkhak phwnangjak.
en: I was not as interested in using the computer, but I did appreciate the convenience of being able to use it to pay bills and do other tasks that used to require a trip to the library or store.

kok: Bisirok thangma bai, computer rok teibo naimanma tei sogwinani wngkha.
en: As the years went by, computers became more and more affordable and accessible.

kok: Borok chikonsa tei teibo phangwnang bo wngkha.
en: They also became smaller and more powerful.

kok: Omo bohrok no teibo jotto omorokni borok bai luku hamjakma swnamkha, bwrwima rokno khobwinai.
en: This made them more popular with people of all ages, including women.

kok: Ang paithago computerrok ni bising phwnangwi manwirok khainani iko samungni bagwi presentationrok swnamnani tei ani rangmairok naikol bwkhak ol manmung.
en: I eventually became interested in using computers to do things like create presentations for work and manage my finances.

kok: Tini, computers tei electronics wngkha kaisa bokcho chini sal thwngwi tongmarok.
en: Today, computers and electronics are a part of our everyday lives.

kok: Chwng bohrokno samung, rwngnok, tongthokmung, tei kwrwnglaimani bagwi phwnango.
en: We use them for work, school, entertainment, and communication.

kok: Borok chini langmarokno kwlaikuk tei teibo suvidha kwbangma lamarokni bising swnamkha.
en: They have made our lives easier and more convenient in many ways.

kok: Ah pohor phlikchati swnamjakmani swkang, borok homchang tei thok chati bohrokni nokrogo pohor rwma bwkhak phwnangkha.
en: Before the invention of the light bulb, people used candles and oil lamps to light their homes.

kok: Oh pohorni yaphangrok belai yaksrai wngya wngkha tei borok uramuram kwbang hoku thaihrwkha.
en: These sources of light were not very efficient and they often produced a lot of smoke.

kok: Ah pohor phlikchati swnamjakmani jottomanwi swlaikhak.
en: The invention of the light bulb changed everything.

kok: Omo borokno yapharma bwkhak horo teibo pohor tongna tei omo samung wngmanma bwkhak swnamkha tei ah mwnak bising thwngkha.
en: It allowed people to have more light at night and it also made it possible to work and play in the dark.

kok: Kaisa lama phereng khatina bwkhak wngkha pohorrokno mwthakma jephuru nwng khotol yakaro.
en: One way to save electricity is to turn off lights when you leave a room.

kok: Teikaisa lama pherang khatima bwkhak wngkha yaksrai-phan pohor phlikchatirok phwnangma bwkhak.
en: Another way to save electricity is to use energy-efficient light bulbs.

kok: Yaksrai-phang pohor phlikchati rok sabrumbrum pohor phlikchatirokni slai kisa pherang phwnangjago tei bohrok kwdwk tikio.
en: Energy-efficient light bulbs use less electricity than regular light bulbs and they last longer.

kok: Chwrairok pherang khati mano pohorrok mwthakmani bai jephuru bohrok kaisa khotol yakaro tei manwirok khakma wngma jephuru borok phwnangjakya.
en: Children can help save electricity by turning off lights when they leave a room and by unplugging appliances when they are not in use.

kok: Bohrok ah thikemung pherang bohrok phwnangma sijak wngjora wngjak bai bo chubai mano.
en: They can also help by being aware of the amount of electricity they use.

kok: Pherang khatimani wngkha nangkukma tamhinba omo chini hangar yaprimari khaina bwkhak chubamarok.
en: Saving electricity is important because it helps to reduce our carbon footprint.

kok: Jephuru chwng kisa pherang phwnango, chwng kisa nokkwkhwrang phap thaihmung.
en: When we use less electricity, we produce less greenhouse gases.

kok: Nokkwkhwrang phaprok wngkha kaisa ah kwchar phermarok nokbartwibar swlaima.
en: Greenhouse gases are one of the main causes of climate change.

kok: Pherang khatimani bai, chwng ah habar mwthangma bwkhak chubai mano tei chwng rang bo khati mano.
en: By saving electricity, we can help to protect the environment and we can also save money.

kok: Horkathi swnamlaima jorao amchayo hiksongnwi thepa laimani samung belai kotor khe nukjago.
en: Matchmakers in traditional societies played a vital role in bringing couples together.

kok: Bohrokni hodao bohrok belai borom rwjago, tei bohrokni khoraimarok bo belai yachakjago.
en: They were often respected members of the community, and their advice was highly valued.

kok: Horkathi swnamnairok bebak phaising twi no yachajago, amchayo boni nukhung bomo hai, hiksongnwi ni ajemung bo, tei bohrok bo tongkwthar no poito khwlai abotwirog.
en: Matchmakers would consider a variety of factors when making a match, including the social status of the families involved, the financial situation of the couple, and their religious beliefs.

kok: Bohrokni baithangni rwngmungno bo naijago, boni tongmung chamungrog, boni rwngrem no twywi bo, tei sakdukrok bo naijago.
en: They would also take into account the personal qualities of each individual, such as their personality, education, and appearance.

kok: Horkathi swnam mani abo talnwi taltham phano nangwi mano eba khe bisi phano nangwi mano.
en: The process of matchmaking could take months or even years.

kok: O jora o, horkathi swnamnairok hiksongnwirok sini layo tei bohrokni nukhung no bo sinijago.
en: During this time, the matchmaker would get to know the couple and their families.

kok: Bohrok hiksongnwi malaijaknai jora bo rwjago jora kahamrogo khe.
en: They would also arrange for the couple to meet each other on several occasions.

kok: Hiksongnwirok bohrok bataijak mahai wngjak khe, horkathi swnamnairok bohrokni nukhung bisingo salaina cheng layo.
en: If the couple felt that they were compatible, the matchmaker would then begin the formal negotiations between the families.

kok: Waisa gosewi na khe, o kokrwlaijak hiksongnwirok kaijagwi mano bohrokni hukumu panda o.
en: Once a deal was reached, the couple would be married in a traditional ceremony.

kok: Horkathi swnam mani samungni bwthai abo amchayo chobo choro tei halog bolaithani swpwngo.
en: Matchmaking in traditional societies resulted in lasting and fulfilling relationships.

kok: O hiksongnwirok bohrok kiching borok belaino gothoklayo, tei bohrokni nukhung tei hodasong bo gose bayo.
en: The couples were often well-suited to each other, and they had the support of their families and community.

kok: Abo baino bohrok gosesogwi mano bohrokni lama o jwngjal phaiwi bo.
en: This helped to ensure that they would be able to weather any challenges that came their way.

kok: Horkathi swnam mani puila phuru ni hai aswk khwlai jakliya, baksa buksu ni amchayo khe tabok bo wngwi tong kho.
en: While matchmaking is no longer as common as it once was, it still plays an important role in some traditional societies.

kok: Jephuru aro tabukbo baitaimarok bwkhak mechenrwma tongo, ah phangwnang manmarirok nuclear phan nangkukmani wngkha.
en: While there are still challenges to be overcome, the potential benefits of nuclear energy are significant.

kok: Kaisa ah kotorma subhidarok nuclear phan wngkha omoni kwrakama.
en: One of the biggest advantages of nuclear energy is its stability.

kok: Nuclear phan phangrok 24 damrok kaisa salo chaluk mano, 7 salrok kaisa hatio, khaurarya ah salbar eba kubun tonghalokrok.
en: Nuclear power plants can operate 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, regardless of the weather or other conditions.

kok: Omo kokmarok je bohrok kaisa pherangni puitgnang yaphang, haino jephuru kubun yaphangrok manthokya wngkhe.
en: This means that they can provide a reliable source of electricity, even when other sources are unavailable.

kok: Nuclear phan kaisa solaima tongo bacher hangar yaprimari.
en: Nuclear energy also has a relatively low carbon footprint.

kok: Jephuru tongrwk mari supungmungrok sujakma bwkhak, nuclear phan duna bwthaihrok belai kisasa nokkwkhwrang phap tikhlaimarok.
en: When compared to fossil fuels, nuclear energy produces much less greenhouse gas emissions.

kok: Omo kaisa teibo habar bayapma saimung pherang achairwmani bagwi omo sanmarok.
en: This makes it a more environmentally friendly option for generating electricity.

kok: Aow, aro bo bataimungrok tongo mecherwma bwkhak nuclear phan bai.
en: Of course, there are also challenges to be overcome with nuclear energy.

kok: Ah jottoni slai nangmani oh wngkha ah nuclear phiyakma swirwma.
en: The most significant of these is the issue of nuclear waste.

kok: Nuclear phiyakma wngkha radioactive tei kwbangma bisirokni bagwi katimung khatijak wngna nango.
en: Nuclear waste is radioactive and must be stored safely for many years.

kok: Haiphano, aro kasa lombor swmaini tanseprok hamkrai wngjak tongo oh swirwma bai lenden bwkhak.
en: However, there are a number of promising technologies being developed to deal with this issue.

kok: Tophano ah bataimungrok, ah phangnang manmarirok nuclear phan nangkukma wngkha.
en: Despite the challenges, the potential benefits of nuclear energy are significant.

kok: Omo wngkha kaisa kwchwng, tei kwrwng phan yaphang je chwngno malaima bwkhak chubai mano chini phan nangmarok tormani.
en: It is a clean, reliable, and efficient source of energy that can help us to meet our growing energy needs.

kok: Ang wansukmakhe haisi "buma" oh kokthai phwnangjakmani khe chini uramuram wansukma ari o buma tamo bahai wngnai hwnwi.
en: I think that the use of the word "mother" is often limited by our expectations of what a mother should be.

kok: Chwng wansugo bumarok belai sakthor, nurturing, tei homnino bohrokni slai swkang bwsarokno tonio.
en: We expect mothers to be selfless, nurturing, and always putting their children first.

kok: Omo thangwi thangnani bagwi tangmung 3 wngwi mano, tei omo bumarokno uansukphan chaya khwlaimano, eba bangthayai bohrok uansuskyai bohrok belai khaitongmani.
en: This can be a very difficult role to live up to, and it can lead to mothers feeling guilty or inadequate if they don't feel like they're doing enough.

kok: Ang wansukha omo muitonarakna nangkukmani je kubuino bumarok bo borokno, tei bohrokbo aswk chasukjakya.
en: I think it's important to remember that mothers are just people, and they're not perfect.

kok: Bohrokbo chayarok khwlai mano, tei bohrokbo thangwi phliksa manwi mano jephuru bohrok wngnaino siyai bohrok tamo khai tong.
en: They're going to make mistakes, and they're going to have moments when they're not sure what they're doing.

kok: Abobo wngo.
en: That's okay.

kok: Chwng jottono chaya khwlayo.
en: We all make mistakes.

kok: Tamo matters khai hwnkhe je chwng bohrokni thani swrwngma bai tei waisa phuru teibo kahamkhe khaina hwnwi.
en: What matters is that we learn from them and try to do better next time.

kok: Ang hai hin wansukha omo muitonarakna nangkukma hwnkhe je aro mungsa juda kubui lama kwrwi buma wngna hwnkhe.
en: I also think it's important to remember that there is no one right way to be a mother.

kok: Jotto buma no pherlayo, tei jotto chwrai rokbo pherlayo.
en: Every mother is different, and every child is different.

kok: Kaisa nukhungo samung khaiphano tei kubuniro khaigwlak.
en: What works for one family might not work for another.

kok: Hwnkhe takiridi experiment khainani tei naitugwi karidi nini bagwi tamo samung cha tei nini nukhungo.
en: So don't be afraid to experiment and find what works for you and your family.

kok: Buma wngwi belai no uanamasingsa tei rwmnani saimanani, phiya omo bataimani bo wngmano.
en: Being a mother is a wonderful and rewarding experience, but it can also be challenging.

kok: Boijakya khorgo rok wngkha muani khlaimung tei uramuram buchimanya dahl.
en: Wild rabbits are a fascinating and often misunderstood species.

kok: Bohrokno hayungni yaksiyagra juda kaisa tongmarok naitukmano, tei bohrokni banagmarok ernai ninangwi thungnukmarok sakboknai chahthai bai twi manthokkhe.
en: They are found in a variety of habitats around the world, and their populations can fluctuate dramatically depending on the availability of food and water.

kok: Kaisa suk khasrangjak manwirok boijakya khorgoni bagwi bohrok khopmani bwkhak bohrok pharimung bwkhak naharmung.
en: One of the most interesting things about wild rabbits is their ability to adapt to their surroundings.

kok: Bohrok wngkha kuar rem nobartwibar rogo thangwi mano, tei bohrok juda chamungrok chai mano.
en: They are able to survive in a wide range of climates, and they can eat a variety of foods.

kok: Oh naharmungrok bohrokno oph hagirini jottoni swlai manjak abuktwi nwngnai mal hwnwi gosikha.
en: This adaptability has allowed them to become one of the most successful mammals on the planet.

kok: Talikhahamya, boijakya khorgorok wngkha sikarirokni bagwi kaichommung luku hamjakjak.
en: Unfortunately, wild rabbits are also a popular target for hunters.

kok: Borok sikar khaijakmani hwnkhe bohrokni bikhumu, muihan, tei haino thwngma rokni bagwi.
en: They are hunted for their fur, meat, and even for sport.

kok: Oh sikhar khaimani boiyjakya khorgoni bangmanirok khairwkha baksa ari bwkhak.
en: This hunting has led to a decline in wild rabbit populations in some areas.

kok: Sikari jora rwmung bai, boijakya khorgorok haino kubun sikrimung bai bwskang malayo, tongmanma kwmamano khobwinai, nobartwibar swlaima, tei bemar.
en: In addition to hunting, wild rabbits also face a number of other threats, including habitat loss, climate change, and disease.

kok: Tongmanma kwmama hwnkhe boijkaya khogorokni bagwi kaisa kotor biyal, tamni hwnkhe bohrok tongna bagwi kwbang thai nango.
en: Habitat loss is a major problem for wild rabbits, as they need a lot of space to live.

kok: Nobartwibar swlaijakma bo kaisa wanamasinja, tamni khe omo boijakya khorgo rokni pherwi tongmani swlaijago.
en: Climate change is also a concern, as it is causing the habitats of wild rabbits to change.

kok: Bemar kaisa boijakya khorgo rokni bagwi kotor biyal wngwi mano, bohrok wngkha khanagkrak juda juda bemarokni lombor bwkhak.
en: Disease can also be a major problem for wild rabbits, as they are susceptible to a number of different diseases.

kok: Tophano jotto sikrimarok tongphano, boijkaya khorgorok tabukb hayungni kwbangma bwkhak nwnwi nukjago.
en: Despite all of these threats, wild rabbits are still a common sight in many parts of the world.

kok: Palaijaknai tei tongthokjaknai jora ni mol phaiwi tongo.
en: The coming season is a time for celebration and joy.

kok: Haiphano, o jora o se kulum-kwsa wngkukmani bo jora.
en: However, it is also a time for increased risk of illness.

kok: Kisisa sak hamkhwrai tei kwchwng khe tongjaknai raida no loi khwlaima bisingtwi, sakno tei sakni nukhungno kaham tei bermar ni phiyogwi mano.
en: By following some simple health and hygiene tips, you can help to keep yourself and your family healthy and safe.

kok: Jotto ni swlai sak kaham tongna bagwi nangkuk mani wngkha yak su mani se.
en: One of the most important things you can do to stay healthy is to wash your hands frequently.

kok: Kuchuk-kongraini virusrok pirjagwi mano, aboni bagwi phainai mol o khe yak suna nangsogo.
en: This is especially important during the coming season, when cold and flu viruses are more likely to spread.

kok: Chakhwi budul tei twi bai yak su phuru Mukpli 20 swk jora nadi, abobo nwng khithai thangmani yagulo, chana swkang, tei kulumrok bai malaiwi phai mani yagulo.
en: Be sure to wash your hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, especially after using the bathroom, before eating, and after being around sick people.

kok: Nini mwkhang o ahai no tatang di yaksuya swkang, abo yong habwi mano.
en: You should also avoid touching your face, as this can spread germs.

kok: Nwng nini mwkhang no tangna khe, swkang yak suwi nagra di.
en: If you do touch your face, be sure to wash your hands immediately.

kok: Mwktrwi kwpulung nana bo belai nango.
en: It is also important to get enough sleep.

kok: Nwng lengwi tongphuru, nini bisingni phan aswk kwrakya, aboni bagwi nono teibo sak dera rw wi mano.
en: When you are tired, your immune system is not as strong, making you more susceptible to illness.

kok: 7-8 dam swk hor burumno thuna chaitok di.
en: Aim for 7-8 hours of sleep per night.

kok: Chamung kaham chamani bo tei kaisa nangkuk mani sak kaham tongna bagwi.
en: Eating a healthy diet is another important part of staying healthy.

kok: Bwthai manwi no kwbang chamani, mwikwthwngrog, tei mairok chamani nini sakno kwrak khwlayo tei omo se jotto ni swlai kahamkugo.
en: Eating plenty of fruits, vegetables, and whole grains can help to boost your immune system and keep you feeling your best.

kok: Kuchuk berem o pore mani abo langma o waisa se jora phayo sakno kwtal hukumu bai gwdalwi tongna bagwi, kwtal kok swrwngwi mano, tei langma kolok ni bagwi kiching swnamwi mano.
en: Studying abroad is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to immerse yourself in a new culture, learn a new language, and make lifelong friends.

kok: Abo wngkha kaisa sakni ni sinimungno kuchugo tisajaknai lamase tei sakno batailaimung ni yakni yogwi mano.
en: It's also a great way to boost your resume and set yourself apart from the competition.

kok: Kwbangma dalbidal lama saiwi najaknai tongo, aroni bisingo je nwng chajakmani tei chukmani abono kaisa rutugwi namano.
en: There are many different programs to choose from, so you can find one that fits your interests and budget.

kok: Nwng dholi kotor o de swrwngna muchung eba dholi bwsa o de muchung, aro nini bagwi lama tongo.
en: Whether you want to study in a major city or a small town, there's a program out there for you.

kok: Kuchuk beremo pore mani kaisa kaham wngkha nwng bebak hayungni borokrok bai malaiwi mano.
en: One of the best things about studying abroad is the chance to meet new people from all over the world.

kok: Nwng dabidal hukumu tei bohrokni naharmungrogno swrwngwi man nai, tei nwng swngcharni borokrok uansoktwi uansogwi man nai.
en: You'll learn about different cultures and perspectives, and you'll develop a global mindset.

kok: Tei kaisa kuchuk beremo swrwngmani kaham wngkhe nwng koksana rwngnai.
en: Another great benefit of studying abroad is the chance to improve your language skills.

kok: Nwng kok kwtal swrwngna thangkhe, nwng salbrum no swrwngnani jora bo mannai.
en: When you're immersed in a new language, you'll have the opportunity to practice it every day.

kok: Omo hai kheno teibo kaham khe tei koroya'ui sa'ui mannai buini kok no.
en: This will help you become more fluent and confident in speaking another language.

kok: Au kwbwino, kuchuk beremo poremani abo jwngjal bo phaiwi mano.
en: Of course, studying abroad can also be challenging.

kok: Nwng kwtal hakotor o ma tongnai, nini nukhungni borok tei kichingrok bai chalwi.
en: You'll be living in a new country, away from your family and friends.

kok: Nwng kwtal hukumu tei tongmung chamungrok bai gwdalna ma swrwngnai.
en: You'll have to adjust to a new culture and way of life.

kok: Phiya abotwi jwngjalrok bo kaisa swrwngjaknai lama se.
en: But these challenges are also part of the learning experience.

kok: Kwdwkma jora romwi, aro Alena mungwi khoroksa bwrwi sikli tongo bolong buchukni chikonsa kamio.
en: Once upon a time, there was a young woman named Alena who lived in a small village on the edge of a forest.

kok: Bo wngkha kaham tei kwchang phola, tei bo bolongo bini sal katina sara tei mungsa hamjakya, naitwimani buphang-uaphang tei malmatarok.
en: She was a kind and gentle soul, and she loved nothing more than spending her days in the forest, tending to the plants and animals.

kok: Salsa, Alena bolong bisingtwi himwi thangphuru bo siniya naijaknai bwskango phaikha.
en: One day, Alena was walking through the forest when she came across a strange sight.

kok: Aro ha o hakor kotorma tongo, tei aro kosom bwtwi ongkhortongo.
en: There was a large hole in the ground, and from it was gushing a black liquid.

kok: Alena omohai agio waisa phano nukya khu, tei bo khatungjak.
en: Alena had never seen anything like it before, and she was curious.

kok: Bo hakor bisingo ongkhorwi thangkha tei yak kuplungkhe bwtwi khurwi tubukha.
en: She reached down into the hole and scooped up a handful of the liquid.

kok: Abo rwja tei swrapung-swrapung, tei abono ni bahai sulfur hai.
en: It was thick and sticky, and it smelled like sulfur.

kok: Alena bini logi a bwtwi no nogo twlangkha tei bini bupha no phunukha.
en: Alena took the liquid home with her and showed it to her father.

kok: Bo wngkha sijak borok, tei bo saimano abo tamo.
en: He was a wise man, and he knew what it was.

kok: Bo Alena no sakha omo thok hwnwi, tei omo belaino morokjak soimanwi.
en: He told Alena that it was oil, and that it was a very valuable substance.

kok: Bo sakha je omo bai kwbangma manwi swnam mano, chati ni thok tei machines kokbwi.
en: He said that it could be used to make many things, including fuel for lamps and machines.

kok: Alena belai tongthokjak thok ni bagwi saimanwi, tei bo chabwi nakha bo bini kami no phwnangwi chubanai hwnwi.
en: Alena was excited to learn about oil, and she decided to use it to help her village.

kok: Bo chati chikonsa swnamkha thok phwnangwi, tei bo bini Ama no rwkha.
en: She built a small lamp using oil, and she gave it to her mother.

kok: Kaisa mukumuno bising, nwng joro dal manwirok naituk mano.
en: In a museum, you can find all sorts of things.

kok: Aro wngkha palirijakmanirok tei takjakmarok, aow, phiya aro kwchang richum tongo, kolrok, tei ahaino engines.
en: There are paintings and sculptures, of course, but there are also old clothes, tools, and even engines.

kok: Nwng kaisa doyungni laihbuma bagwi swrwng mano ah manwirokno naimani bai je borok tongmani bai phwnangjak phaima bwkhak.
en: You can learn about the history of a city by looking at the things that people used to live with.

kok: Nwng nugwi mano bahai borok rok swlaijakha jora thwgwi, tei bahaikhe bohrokni tongma lama swlaijakha.
en: You can see how people have changed over time, and how their way of life has changed.

kok: Salsa, ang kaisa kotor doyungni kaisa mukumunok bwkha thangkha.
en: One day, I went to a museum in a big city.

kok: Ang ah kwcham engines kaisa thumjakma no naitongmani jephuru ang kaisa khorang khwnakha "khulumkha," ah khorang sakha "nwng angbai kok sana chajak hwnwi?"
en: I was looking at a collection of old engines when I heard a voice "Hello," said the voice "Would you like to chat?"

kok: Ang yaksiyakgra philkha tei kaisa chwrai chikonsa ani gana bachajak nukha.
en: I turned around and saw a little girl standing next to me.

kok: Bo kaisa thwngjaknai engine romjak wngkha "akon'," ang sakha "nwng tamoni bagwi kok sana muchung?"
en: She was holding a toy engine "Sure," I said "What do you want to talk about?"

kok: "ang haino uanamasingsa wngkha oh engines bagwi, " bo sakha "bohrok bahaikhe samung khlai?"
en: "I was just wondering about these engines," she said "How do they work?"

kok: Ang bono sakha ah juda juda sapokthaih engines bagwi, tei bahai bohrok phan malkhungrok, relmalkhungrok, tei rungkotorrok bwkhak phwnangjak.
en: I told her about the different types of engines, and how they are used to power cars, trains, and ships.

kok: Bo kubuino ol manjak wngkha, tei bo ano kwbangma swngmungrok swngkha.
en: She was really interested, and she asked me a lot of questions.

kok: Chwng jora kwdwk kok salaikhaa, tei ang bini bagwi kwbang swrwngkha.
en: We chatted for a long time, and I learned a lot about her.

kok: Khachuksa [mung], ang khajamung oh kokdukrok nono kahamkhe mananw hwnwi.
en: Dear [Name], I hope this letter finds you well.

kok: Angbo oh sep no nana muchungmani bwkhak kok sanani ranghalokni kok swikwrwngungni bagwi.
en: I wanted to take this opportunity to talk to you about financial literacy.

kok: Nwng saimano, ranghalokni kok swikwrwngmung wngkha pharimung bwkhak nini rang no naikolnani tei buchinani.
en: As you know, financial literacy is the ability to understand and manage your money.

kok: Ranghalokni kok sqikwrwngmung tongnani bwkhak omo belai nangkukma, nini jesaphano omor wngdi eba ajima mil.
en: It's important to have financial literacy, no matter what your age or income level.

kok: Aro kwbangma manwi tongo nwng nini ranghalokni kok swikwrwngmung bwkhak kaham khai mananw.
en: There are many things you can do to improve your financial literacy.

kok: Kaisa nangkukma manwi wngkha juda juda sapokthaih rok ranghalokni kok thaihmanwi rok tei samungrok.
en: One important thing is to learn about different types of financial products and services.

kok: Nwng swrwngwi nana nangkha bahai khe nini rangpuisa rangchongmung khainai tei bahaikhe nini thinang ni bagwi khatinai.
en: You should also learn about how to budget your money and how to save for the future.

kok: Teikaisa nangkukma manwi hwnkhe kaisa rangchongmung swnamnani tei abo bai kwphai tongnani.
en: Another important thing is to make a budget and stick to it.

kok: Kaisa rangchongmung wngkha kaisa chapmung bahaikhe nwng nini rangpuisa tal thwgwi swbaina bwkhak naitong.
en: A budget is a plan for how you're going to spend your money each month.

kok: Omo nono yaprimari khaithani chubai mano nini swbaimani no tei kahamkhe swnamwi je nwng ajimani slai da teibo swbaimani kwrwi.
en: It can help you to track your spending and make sure that you're not spending more than you earn.

kok: Paithago, omo thinangni bagwi khatinani belai nangkukma.
en: Finally, it's important to save for the future.

kok: Omoni kokmarok wngkha habayakarmung karwi khatimani, kaisa nokni bagwi tola dormai rwmung, eba tei kubuni jesaphano kotor swbaima je nwng nini thinangni bagwi tongwiwi mano.
en: This means saving for retirement, for a down payment on a house, or for any other major expense that you may have in the future.

kok: Hamsuthai wngkha kaisa phangwnang khanangjak.
en: Gratitude is a powerful emotion.

kok: Omoni thani ah pharimung tongo chini langmano swlaina bwkhak tei chwngno tongthokma, sakdukma, tei teibo khlaimanmung swnamo.
en: It has the ability to transform our lives and make us happier, healthier, and more successful.

kok: Jephuru chwng hamsuthai wngkha, chwng chini langmarokni ah kaham manwirok sakao naisikma wngo, tei chini thani tamo tongma bai chwngno chajakma bwkhak omo chubamarok.
en: When we are grateful, we focus on the good things in our lives, and this helps us to appreciate what we have.

kok: Hamsuthai bo chwngno kubunrok bai kwrwngna tei kwrak halokbokmarok tisama bwkhak chubamarok.
en: Gratitude also helps us to connect with others and build strong relationships.

kok: Ang poito khayo je hamsuthai wngkha kaisa ah jottoni slai nangkukma manwirok chwng nini lanmani bagwi swrwng mano.
en: I believe that gratitude is one of the most important things we can learn in life.

kok: Omo wngkha kaisa yaksrai je hamkrai tei chasamarok bai loi khlaimung wngwi mano.
en: It is a skill that can be developed and improved with practice.

kok: Chwng teibo hamsuthai ol khlaimung khayo, ah kwlaikukma omo wngmarok bwkhak nukha ah kaham chini langmarokni bising tei chajakma bwkhak ah borok sabao chini bagwi nankukma wngkha.
en: The more we practice gratitude, the easier it becomes to see the good in our lives and to appreciate the people who are important to us.

kok: Ang kaisa kuthuk hamsuthai buchimani bisingtwih ani sakni saimanjakrok mankha.
en: I have obtained a deep understanding of gratitude through my own experiences.

kok: Ang ani langma bising twih kwbangma 3 barrok khai paikha, phiya ang homino mungsaswk naituk mano ah hamsuthaini bagwi.
en: I have been through many difficult times in my life, but I have always been able to find something to be grateful for.

kok: Ahaino jephuru manwirok bohrokni hamya wngo, ang saimano je ang belai talikhakaham kwthang tongma bwkhak tei ani nukhung tei bayaprokni twichuruma manna bwkhak tongo.
en: Even when things were at their worst, I knew that I was lucky to be alive and to have the support of my family and friends.

kok: Hamsuthai ano kaisa tongthokma tei teibo khongkwlai borok wngma bwkha ano chubakha.
en: Gratitude has helped me to become a happier and more resilient person.

kok: Omo ano jotto tongrem bising kaham nukma bwkhak ano chubakha, tei omo ano bataimarok mechenma bwkha phan rwkha.
en: It has helped me to see the good in every situation, and it has given me the strength to overcome challenges.

kok: Taluang 2023 bising, khoroksa bwrwima sikli Sarah mungwi kaisa kwtal company bai yaknaharjak je ah hayung tungmung kasomani bwkhak saktharjak wngkha.
en: In October of 2023, a young woman named Sarah was hired by a new company that was dedicated to preventing global warming.

kok: Bo tongthojak wngkha kaisa mungsaswk bokcho wngma bwkhak je ah hayung bising kubui pherlaimung swnam mano.
en: She was excited to be a part of something that could make a real difference in the world.

kok: Sarahni puila sal ah samungo wngkha swrwngwi lairwma ah company ni pinnok tei sokthairokni bagwi.
en: Sarah's first day on the job was spent learning about the company's mission and goals.

kok: Bo bini thwngdol bwkhak sinirimung rwjakha, bomo kaisa juda borok bodol jotto hayung sakani simi swnamjakma wngkha.
en: She was also introduced to her team, which was made up of a diverse group of people from all over the world.

kok: Sarah daktino saimankha je bo kaham companyni bisingo wngkha hwnwi.
en: Sarah quickly realized that she was in good company.

kok: Jottono bini thwngdol sakao khamuchungjak wngkha ah samung bohrok khlai tongmani bagwi, tei bohrok jotto swmai tangjak kaisa pherlaimung swnamani bwkhak.
en: Everyone on her team was passionate about the work they were doing, and they were all committed to making a difference.

kok: Sarah kaisa samungbwtang bwkhak samungbokajak wngkha je nokkwkhrang phap ongkhormarok khaina bwkhak kwtak himlarok hamkrai wngkha.
en: Sarah was assigned to a project that was developing new ways to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

kok: Bo kolok darwi samung khaikha, phiya bo ah samungbwtang khlaimanna bagwi tongthokjak wngkha.
en: She worked long hours, but she was excited about the potential of the project.

kok: Thansa samung tangmani bai, chwng jotto hayung tungmani kasogra bwkhak chubaimano tei kaisa tikinai thinang chini hagirini bagwi swnam mano.

kok: Ah bosong kaham korai, kaisa phan tei khairokma mari, bisisai bagwi borok tongphwrwngmani kaisa kwswngthong wngkha.
en: The noble steed, a symbol of strength and grace, has been a mainstay of human civilization for millennia.

kok: Jesaphano yaphang wngthwng aro gosiya wng manya ah kwthama je tongmarok borok tei korairokni kwcharo.

kok: Chwng kisa kok kwdwk salai kha, chini khatungma tei imangrogno twywi, chini nahar mung tei muchungmungrog.

en: We had a small school, a general store, and a post office.

kok: Kaisa saknainok wngkha kaisa sakduknaikani rwngnok rugi saknaimung bakmani kaisa bising rugi tangbwtang bising.
en: A hospital is a healthcare institution providing patient treatment in an inpatient setting.

en: Inpatient care is provided by hospital inpatient departments, emergency departments and outpatient clinics.

kok: Saknainokrok nangnungya kwrwng tei mungtisajak hamya nailkolnairok, saknainairok, tei kubun sakduk kwrwngrok bai tongsong wngkha.
en: Hospitals are usually staffed by professional and registered nurses, physicians, and other health professionals.

en: Specialty hospitals focus on a particular type of care, such as cancer care, cardiac care, or orthopedic care.

kok: Khabemar naijaknai saknainokrok borokni bagwi naikani bago khapang hamya bai.
en: Psychiatric hospitals provide care for people with mental illness.

kok: Saknairokrok wngkha kaisa nangkukma bokcho ah sakduknaikani tangdal o.

kok: Bohrok kaisa dalbidal hamyarok tei dukhu manmarok naikani karwi bago, tei bohrok kaisa mal tangmung thwngo ah kasomung, diagnosis, tei bermar ni saknaimung.

kok: Hasing yarwng bisira rwgwi phwnangjagwi phayo nausea tei kwpamani no saknaima bwkhak.

kok: Kaisa porimung sapukthai kokbwlaihni bising "Phytotherapy rutukwrwk, " rutukwrwkrok mankha je hasing yarwng wngkha amjokthai nausea tei kwpamani khaimani bising rugirok chemotherapy tolathang tongo.
en: In a study published in the journal "Phytotherapy Research," researchers found that ginger root was effective in reducing nausea and vomiting in patients who were undergoing chemotherapy.

kok: Ah porimung manjakanairok hasing yarwng namani saimanrimungrok amswkno kisa nausea tei kwpamani slai manjaknairok je kaisa placebo namani.
en: The study participants who took ginger root reported significantly less nausea and vomiting than the participants who took a placebo.

en: Another study, published in the journal "Alternative Therapies in Health and Medicine," found that ginger root was effective in reducing nausea and vomiting in patients who were undergoing surgery.

en: The study participants who took ginger root reported significantly less nausea and vomiting than the participants who took a placebo.

kok: Sapsutrarok mwtailobanaini ganakuk.

kok: Nwirem, sapsutrarok borok rokni morji chasama khaimano tei langmao nukmungo chubai mano.

kok: Omo tamnihinmale sapsutrarok jotto hodani bagwi nangkukma.

kok: Thamrem, sapsutrarok jotto hodani bagwi nangkukma.

kok: Omo hodano sakdugwi tei jottono katiwui tonina bagwi chubai mano.

kok: Aswkno, hwnkhe tei waisa jora jephuru nwwng sapsutrarokno twi slelema wansuktongkhe muitonarakdi, sapsutrarok hwnkhe mwtailobnaini ganakuk.
en: So, the next time you are feeling lazy about cleaning, remember that cleanliness is next to godliness!

en: She had been to the doctor many times, but they couldn't figure out what was wrong with her.

kok: Ellani ma-pha bohno twywi unama kuthugo tongmani.
en: Ella's parents were very worried about her.

kok: Salsa Ellani buma bohno sakham banigo twlangwi thangkha.
en: One day, Ella's mother took her to a health fair.

kok: Aro kwbangma judajuda booth songchajakmani, bebak bootho kaisa alaidakhe sakhamno twywi kokthum rwjak tongo.
en: There were many different booths set up, each one with information about a different health topic.

kok: Ella tei buma bebak booth berai naikha tei Ella chahmung kaham, sakloi tei katiui tongnano twywi kwbangma manwi swrwngkha.
en: Ella and her mother visited each booth, and Ella learned a lot about healthy eating, exercise, and staying safe.

kok: Banigo Ella, bini tonghalokno nugwi muchungswkjak abohai khoroksa saknaiphang baibo malaikha.
en: Ella also met a doctor at the fair who was very interested in her case.

kok: Boh bohno bini sinimarino twywi kwbangma kok swngkha tei boh kisaswk amjok naikha.
en: He asked her a lot of questions about her symptoms, and he did some tests.

kok: Sal kisaswkni ulo paithago, saknaiphang romwi mankha Ellani tamo wngkha.
en: After a few days, the doctor finally figured out what was wrong with Ella.

kok: Boh bohno sakha je bini Vitamine, ni biyal tongo tei boh bohno Vitamine chahna bagwi kokbiti rwkha.
en: He told her that she had a vitamin deficiency, and he prescribed her some vitamins to take.

kok: Ella Vitamine chahnani chengkha, tei boh logilogino hamwi tongmano khachongwi mankha.
en: Ella started taking the vitamins, and she started to feel better right away.

kok: Boh teibo kwbangkhe chahmung chaui mankha, tei boh teibo phan mankha.
en: She was able to eat more food, and she had more energy.

kok: Boh sakham banigo thang mankha hwnwi boh belai, khatungjak tongmani tei bohno sakhamthani chubanai saknaiphangni thani boh hamsuthai.
en: She was so happy that she had gone to the health fair, and she was grateful to the doctor for helping her get better.

kok: Ellani kothoma wngkha kaisa sakham rwngni nangkukmano muitu khwlairwnai.
en: Ella's story is a reminder of the importance of health education.

kok: Dopha sakbaithang nanglaimani wngkha kaisa kerengtwi langmani babai.
en: Interpersonal conflict is a normal part of life.

kok: Omo bayaprok, nukhungni logisong, baksa samungkhainairok, tei khangnangjak logisongrokni bising wngwi mano.
en: It can happen between friends, family members, coworkers, and romantic partners.

kok: Aro kwbangma juda juda dopha sakbaithang nanglaimung phermarok tong, iko juda juda mourukmarok, poitorok tei alongrok.
en: There are many different causes of interpersonal conflict, such as different values, beliefs, and goals.

kok: Nanglaimung kok manjukmanya bai pherjak mano, sakbaithangni bulaimarok, tei phann biyalrok.
en: Conflict can also be caused by miscommunication, personality clashes, and power struggles.

kok: Jephuru nanglaimung wngo, omo bokcho bai mano.
en: When conflict occurs, it can be difficult to deal with.

kok: Omo nanglaimung sakpharma lupkhlaimani bwkhak mano eba kubun borokno lathadwkhwi kari mano.
en: It can be tempting to avoid the conflict or to lash out at the other person.

kok: Haiphano, omorok sakdukni lamarok bokcho bai nanglaimung bwkhak wngwi manya.
en: However, these are not healthy ways to deal with conflict.

kok: Nanglaimung bai bokcho kahamkuk lama wngkha omo ni bagwi kok salainani.
en: The best way to deal with conflict is to talk about it.

kok: Omoni kusu sraisrai khai saamani nini wansukrokno tei kubun borokni nukmung bo khwnanani.
en: This means expressing your feelings and listening to the other person's perspective.

kok: Omo chubama kuplung bwkhak naitukma bwkhak bo mano kaisa kwcharo nono nanglaimung kokchap chuabai mano.
en: It can also be helpful to find a mediator to help you resolve the conflict.

kok: Dopha sakbathang nanglaimung bataimani wngwi mano, phiya omo kaisa swrwngnani bo sep wngwi mano.
en: Interpersonal conflict can be challenging, but it can also be a learning opportunity.

kok: Nanglaimung chwngno teibo swrwngna bagwi chubai mano chini saksakni bagwi tei kubun borok bai.
en: Conflict can help us to learn more about ourselves and the other person.

kok: Omo chwngno hamkrai bwkhak chubai mano chini manjulaimani tei nanglaimung khathonjak yaksrairok.
en: It can also help us to develop our communication and conflict resolution skills.

kok: Chwng jephuru nanglaimung bokcho kwcharo kaisa sakdukni lama bai swrwngo, chwng kwrakuk khe halok kwrwngmarok tisai mano tei teibo langmarok supungwi manwi mano.
en: When we learn to deal with conflict in a healthy way, we can build stronger relationships and have more fulfilling lives.

kok: "Tongkwthar wngkha kahamkuk chaplam" wngkha kaisa samani je kokmarok abo wngkha homnino kahamma tongkwthar bwkhak, tumungno amo 3 wngkha.
en: "Honesty is the best policy" is a saying that means it is always better to be honest, even if it is difficult.

kok: Tongkwthar wngkha nangkukma tamni hinba omo poito tei borom rwma borokni kwchar tisamarok.
en: Honesty is important because it builds trust and respect between people.

kok: Jephuru borok saimano je nwng wngkha tongkwthar, bohrok wngkha teibo amtwi nwng poito tei nwng khulukma bwkhak.
en: When people know that you are honest, they are more likely to trust you and open up to you.

kok: Omo phangwnang halokbokjakrok tei teibo supungmani saimanmarok bwkha dagi twlang mano.
en: This can lead to stronger relationships and more fulfilling experiences.

kok: Aro wngkha kwbangma manmarirok tongkwthar wngjak bwkhak.
en: There are many benefits to being honest.

kok: Phunukmari karwi, tongkwthar wngjak nono nanglaimung katina bwkhak chubai mano, chongmarok kahamma swnamo, tei halokbokmarok kwrak tisao.
en: For example, being honest can help you to avoid conflict, make better decisions, and build strong relationships.

kok: Nwng jephuru tongkwthar wngkha, nwng teibo ahaino saksak kubui wngna nango tei kaisa langma tongna je nwng kungchukjak wngkha.
en: When you are honest, you are more likely to be true to yourself and live a life that you are proud of.

kok: Aow, tongkwthar wngjak homino wngya.
en: Of course, being honest is not always easy.

kok: Omo kubui sana wngwi mano jephuru omo wngkha kwrak tei jephuru nwng ah bwthaihrok kirima wngkha.
en: It can be difficult to tell the truth when it is hard or when you are afraid of the consequences.

kok: Haiphano, omo wngkha muitu khlaima nangkuma bwkhak je ah kolok-joraari tongkwthar ni manmarirok hakchal hilikma ah bara-joraari sama.
en: However, it is important to remember that the long-term benefits of honesty far outweigh the short-term pain.

kok: Tumungno nwng tongkwthar bwkhak kaphramung wngkha, aro wngkha kisa manwirok chwng saksakno chubana bwkhak khai mano.
en: If you are struggling to be honest, there are a few things you can do to help yourself.

kok: Puila, karonrokno sinina bwkhak chaitokdi tangwi nwng akolsitra wngdok wngkha.
en: First, try to identify the reasons why you are being dishonest.

kok: Waisa nwng saimankha nini tongmung chalukmani tamo wngkha, chwng ah biyal ni yapharwng nikuma bwkhak chengwi mano.
en: Once you know what is driving your behavior, you can start to address the root of the problem.

kok: Nwirem, loi khlaimung tongkwthar wngjak chikonsa lamarokni bising.
en: Second, practice being honest in small ways.

kok: Borok 1: Wansuk khapang mwnwikothokrok wngkha aswkno kubuiya.
en: Person 1: Romantic Comedies are so unrealistic.

kok: Borok 2: Kubuino, ang saimano? Ah hamjakma ol manmung homnino puila nukma bai hamjakma bising kwlaima, tei bohrok waisaphano jesaphano kebengmungrok kwrwi.
en: Person 2: I know, right? The love interests always fall in love at first sight, and they never have any problems.

kok: Borok 1: Tei ah nanglaimungrok homnino aswkno swnamma wngkha.
en: Person 1: And the conflicts are always so contrived.

kok: Haino, kaisa tokeni bising, ah borjro rok kaklaikha tamni hinba ah borokni yaar ah bwrwi bai hamjakma bising wngkha.
en: Like, in one movie, the couple broke up because the guy's best friend was in love with the girl.

kok: Borok 2: Abo aswkno mwnwijaknai. Omo kahaiya je kubui langmani bising wngmarok.
en: Person 2: That's so ridiculous. It's not like that happens in real life.

kok: Borok 1: Kubuino. Tei ahaino jephuru bohrok thansa wngo, omo homnino aswkno chasukjak.
en: Person 1: Exactly. And even when they do get together, it's always so perfect.

kok: Bohrok waisaphano jesaphano bulaimarok eba gosilaiyaungmarok tongma wngkhe.
en: They never have any fights or disagreements.

kok: Borok 2: Omo kahai ah tokerok wngkha chaitokmani chwngno sama bwkhak je hamjakma wngkha homnino tei chasukjak.
en: Person 2: It's like the movies are trying to tell us that love is always easy and perfect.

kok: Phiya abo ah tonghalokya.
en: But that's not the case.

kok: Hamjakma wngkha kwrak samung.
en: Love is hard work.

kok: Omo jora nao tei tisana bwkha chaitogo kasa runghalok chornani bai.
en: It takes time and effort to build a lasting relationship.

kok: Borok 1: Ang saimano. Aboni bagwino ang tei rom-coms nailiya.
en: Person 1: I know. That's why I don't watch rom-coms anymore.

kok: Bohrok hamjakmani bagwi borokno kubuiya khakamanirok rio.
en: They give people unrealistic expectations about love.

kok: Aro kwbangma juda juda lamarok tongo risunok khainani, kaisa sirisiti sumani kol tei phwranjaknai bwkhak teibo eco-friendly khlaimungrok iko yak sumani tei ari phwrangmani simi phwnangmani.
en: There are many different ways to do laundry, from using a traditional washing machine and dryer to more eco-friendly methods like hand washing and line drying.

kok: Kaisa lama risunok khaina bwkhak kaisa kol phwngyawui wngkha nini yak bai rirok sumani kaisa twikhok eba swkwlwkma bisingtwih.
en: One way to do laundry without using a machine is to hand wash your clothes in a basin or sink.

kok: Omo khaina bwkhak, ah twikhok no twi tululu bai supungdi tei kaisa chikonsa bangmari risukno detergent jora rwdi.
en: To do this, fill the basin with warm water and add a small amount of laundry detergent.

kok: Nini rirokno chomdi kisa srapsa ni bagwi, hwnkhe bohrokno hupredi kaisa risuma eba brush bai.
en: Soak your clothes for a few minutes, then scrub them with a washcloth or brush.

kok: Nini rirokno kahamkhai suhdi twi kwchwng bai, hwnkhe bohrokno mwsagwi karidi.
en: Rinse your clothes thoroughly in clean water, then wring them out.

kok: Nini rirokno khachiwui phwrandi kaisa rirokaro eba phwnangmani rack sakao.
en: Hang your clothes to dry on a clothesline or drying rack.

kok: Tei kaisa saimung wngkha kaisa sumani kol phwnangma bwkhak kaisa phwranjaknai karwi.
en: Another option is to use a washing machine without a dryer.

kok: Omo phan tei rang banchirwi mano, phiya omo tei jora tei chaitok bo nango.
en: This can save energy and money, but it does require more time and effort.

kok: Rirok kaisa kol bising suna bising kaisa phwrangjaknai karwi, ah kol no twi bai supungdi tei risuknok detergent jora rwdi.
en: To wash clothes in a machine without a dryer, fill the machine with water and add laundry detergent.

kok: Ah kol no gothokma saikel bwkhak thepadi, hwnkhe omo chengdi.
en: Set the machine to the appropriate cycle, then start it.

kok: Jephuru ah saikel paihyo, nini rirokno ah kol simi karidi tei bohrokno khachiwui phwrandi.
en: When the cycle is complete, remove your clothes from the machine and hang them to dry.

kok: Tumungno nwng kaisa ari bising tongkha kaisa kwbang watwi bai, nwng ah watwini twino phwnangwi nini rirokno phwranna bwkhak chubachu khlaimano.
en: If you live in an area with a lot of rain, you may be able to use the rain to help you dry your clothes.

kok: Nini rirokno kaisa rirokari phatardigi ah watwi bising khachiwui mano.
en: Hang your clothes on a clothesline outside in the rain.

kok: Ah soap opera kaisa chikon aoli tongthairok tongnairokni yaksiyagra kwcharrogo.
en: The soap opera centers around the lives of the residents of a small town.

kok: Ah kwchar tongdal, Constance, wngkha khoroksa bwrwima sikli je khapharmani wngma bwkhak jorarok bwkhak phaima bai bini bwsai thwidrop o.
en: The main character, Constance, is a young woman who is struggling to come to terms with the recent death of her husband.

kok: Bo bini khoronwi bwsarok pusina bagwi yakar kwlangjakma bwkhak bini sakni sakao, tei bo bini dukhu no tangma bwkhak kaisa lama naitukma bwkhak khaharmani.
en: She is left to raise her two young children on her own, and she is struggling to find a way to handle her grief.

kok: Salsa, Constance khoroksa borok Frederick mungwi malaikha kaisa manwi khwnwi khatinogo.
en: One day, Constance meets a man named Frederick at the grocery store.

kok: Frederick wngkha khoroksa kaham tei khairokjaknai borok , tei bo Constance bo bini twichumura yapharkha.
en: Frederick is a kind and compassionate man, and he offers Constance his support.

kok: Constance Frederick ni bagwi uansukmani hamrw bwkhak chengkha, phiya bo kwtal halokbokma sakpharo wngna chengkha tamni hinba bo takbukbo bini bwsai thwimani dukhumanwi tongkhu.
en: Constance begins to develop feelings for Frederick, but she is hesitant to start a new relationship because she is still grieving the loss of her husband.

kok: Paithago, Constance Fredrick no kaisa sujuk rina bwkha chongwi naakha.
en: Eventually, Constance decides to give Frederick a chance.

kok: Bo bobai cholinanai chekha, tei bo daktino bobai hamjagwi thangkha.
en: She starts dating him, and she quickly falls in love with him.

kok: Frederick Constance no bini dukhu ni simi hamnani chubakha, tei bo bo bono phan rwkha bini chwrairokno bini sakni sakao puisnani.
en: Frederick helps Constance to heal from her grief, and he gives her the strength to raise her children on her own.

kok: Constance tei Frederick kaijakha, tei bohrok kaisa tongthok langma thansa khe tongkha.
en: Constance and Frederick get married, and they have a happy life together.

kok: Bohrok thansa khe bohrokni chwrairokno puisikha, tei bohrok khoroksa tei khoroksa no kaham jorarok tei hamya twih twichuruma khayo.
en: They raise their children together, and they support each other through good times and bad.

kok: Constance belai khatung khajak Fredrick's hamjakma tei twichuruma manma bagwi, tei bo saimanao je bo jesakhe phano bono hambai kwbang rwimanya jottomanwwi bo bini bagwi khaimani.
en: Constance is grateful for Frederick's love and support, and she knows that she will never be able to thank him enough for everything he has done for her.

kok: Ah soap opera kaisa khajamung koktun bai phaikha.
en: The soap opera ends with a message of hope.

kok: "Rwngkotor swrwngnairok beer bai saimanjakrok": khoroksa rwngkotor srwngnai wngwi, ani thani tongo ani banik banta saimanjakrok beer bai.
en: "College student's experiences with beer": As a college student, I have had my fair share of experiences with beer.

kok: Baksa oh saimanjakrok kubui wngkha, jephuru kubunrok laisa lem uansukjak wngkha.
en: Some of these experiences have been positive, while others have been less than ideal.

kok: Haiphano, kaisa saimanjak je ang tei pogya ah jora ang manmani "along beer" manma ani dorm khotol bwkhak tunjakha.
en: However, one experience that I will never forget is the time I got "prison beer" delivered to my dorm room.

kok: Omo jotto chengkha jephuru ang horsa ni bagwi ani baksa bayaprok bai phatar beraimani phuru, tei chwng kaisa pizza kwcharna bwkhak chongkha.
en: It all started when I was hanging out with some friends one night, and we decided to order a pizza.

kok: Chwng chini kwcharma online thairikha, tei swrapsarok bisingbai, chwng kaisa saklaijakma mankha je chini pizza tunjakha wngkha wngkha hwnwi.
en: We placed our order online, and within minutes, we received a notification that our pizza was being delivered.

kok: Haiphano, jephuru ah tunmani bohrok nukjak phaikha, bo Pizza twijakya.
en: However, when the delivery guy showed up, he was not carrying a pizza.

kok: Aboni slai, bo kaisa beer case twijak wngkha.
en: Instead, he was carrying a case of beer.

kok: Chwng jottono palmanya wngkha, phiya ah tunnai chwla swbaikhrupbwi sakha je chwng chini kwcharma dalukjak thangkha tei kaisa kwcharma bai.
en: We were all confused, but the delivery guy explained that he had gotten our order mixed up with another order.

kok: Bo sakha je ah kubun borok kaisa beer case khwcharkha hwnwi, tei bo aboni slai chaya khlai omo chwngno tunphaikha.
en: He said that the other person had ordered a case of beer, and he had accidentally delivered it to us instead.

kok: Chwng jottono kisa sakpharoro wngkha puilao, phiya paithago chwng ah beer no narakna hwnwi chongkha.
en: We were all a little hesitant at first, but we eventually decided to keep the beer.

kok: Phaithago, omo wngkha phiyokjak beer.
en: After all, it was free beer.

kok: Chwng ah beer case khulukha tei nwnglainani chengkha.
en: We opened the case of beer and started drinking.

kok: Ah beer kubuino belai kaham wngkha, tei chwng jottono kaisa kotor kuar jora tongkha.
en: The beer was actually pretty good, and we all had a great time.

kok: Yokmung: Kaisa sakbaithang naharmani twi.
en: Freedom: A Personal Perspective

kok: Yokmung wngkha kaisa kokthai je phwnangjak tongo tei asnowk kwbangma borok bai raida swbaijakha, aswkno kwbangma salaithaikok bising, je amo soktwtwi omoni kokmang kwmai tongo.
en: Freedom is a word that has been used and abused by so many people, in so many contexts, that it has almost lost its meaning.

kok: Phiya ani bagwi, yokmung wngkha kaisa belai khakepleng manwi.
en: But for me, freedom is a very simple thing.

kok: Omoni ah khlaimanmung wngkha ani langmano ani sakni jorarok sakao tongna, kubunrok bai satokjakma eba mwthakmung wngjak karwi.
en: It is the ability to live my life on my own terms, without being controlled or oppressed by others.

kok: Ang kaisa jora tei thaini bising achaikha boro bwrwima rokno chwla rokbai sakphan baksa gosijakya wngkha.
en: I was born into a time and place where women were not considered to be fully equal to men.

kok: Chwng ah nogo tongna bwkhak khakajakha, chwrairokno torrwna, tei chini bwsairokno naikani khainani wngkha.
en: We were expected to stay at home, raise children, and take care of our husbands.

kok: Phiya ang waisa phano amtwi langma bwkhak tongma muchungya.
en: But I never wanted to live that kind of life.

kok: Ang yokna muchungkha ani sakni imangrok unsruma, swrwngna tei torna bwkhak, tei ah hayungni bising pherlaimung swnama bwkhak.
en: I wanted to be free to pursue my own dreams, to learn and grow, and to make a difference in the world.

kok: Ang talikha kaham wngkha mapharok tongma bwkhak je ani naimungkotorrok twichuruma khayo.
en: I was fortunate to have parents who supported my ambitions.

kok: Bohrok ano rwngnokkotor thangna bwkhak khatungrimung khayo, kaisa samung nana bwkhak, tei ani langma nai sakni jorarok tongma bwkhak.
en: They encouraged me to go to college, to get a job, and to live my life on my own terms.

kok: Tei ang hamsuthai wngkha oh seprokni bagwi je ang beraina nangp, borok kwtal malaina bwkhak, tei juda juda hukumurok swrwngna bwkhak.
en: And I am grateful for the opportunities that I have had to travel, to meet new people, and to learn about different cultures.

kok: Phiya ang saimano je jottono ang hai talikha kaham wngya.
en: But I know that not everyone is as lucky as I was.

kok: Aro ah hayung bising tabuk bo kwbangma borok tongo je bohrokni yokmung gosijakya, tamhinba haino bohrokni bosong, bohrokni sir, eba bohrokni tongthar.
en: There are still many people in the world who are denied their freedom, simply because of their race, their gender, or their religion.

kok: Jephuru omo thuyam khotol tonikhok tei manwirok bwkhak phayo, aro kwbangma manwirok gosijago.
en: When it comes to bedroom furniture and design accessories, there are many things to consider.

kok: Nwng kaisa bukcha thai swnamna muchungjago je kainwino tongdal tei samungkhainai, tei je nini tongmung chamung bai khoropsa wngo.
en: You want to create a space that is both stylish and functional, and that fits your personality.

kok: Phiya kwbangma pherlaimani saimungrok bai manthogo, omo saimanna kuthuk wngwi mano boroni simi chenjak kha.
en: But with so many different options available, it can be hard to know where to start.

kok: Kaisa nangkukma manwi nini khorogo tonima bwkha hwkhe jottokhobwi vibe nwng nini thuyamkhotol ni bagwi swnamna muchungjakmani.
en: One important thing to keep in mind is the overall vibe you want to create in your bedroom.

kok: Nwng bukcha thai da nang je lenglamani tei kwcharmani, eba mungsaswk teibo kwsrwng tei jolirwmani?
en: Do you want a space that is relaxing and inviting, or something more energetic and stimulating?

kok: Waisa nwng saimankhe nwng tamo naitong, nwng nini chongmarok nini tola beser o chengwi mano.
en: Once you know what you're looking for, you can start to narrow down your choices.

kok: Tumungno nwng kaisa lenglamani tei kwcharmani thuyamkhotol naitongkhe, babaikwrwi palirok tei kwlwi ri rok sainani gosidi.
en: If you're looking for a relaxing and inviting bedroom, consider choosing neutral colors and soft fabrics.

kok: Sakkati jesamanwi belai kwchwng eba khorangkoto hwnkhe, omo kaisa chaya nokbarkhung swnam mano.
en: Avoid anything too bright or loud, as this can create a negative atmosphere.

kok: Nwng kahamkhe swnamna nango aro kwbangma khasrangma achukjaknai tongo, ahaino thuyam, achukphang, yaktwi eba chaise lounge.
en: You should also make sure there is plenty of comfortable seating, such as a bed, armchair, or chaise lounge.

kok: Nwng tumungno teibo kwsrang tei jolirwmani thuyamkhotol naii tongkhe, nwng khakrakjak palirok tei naidalrok saiwi mano.
en: If you're looking for a more energetic and stimulating bedroom, you can choose bolder colors and patterns.

kok: Nwng baksa naithothok rikma bokhrwirok thepai mano, ahaino kaisa swisamung bokcho tonikhok ni eba kaisa manthokya pohor thepamarok.
en: You can also add in some interesting design elements, such as a statement piece of furniture or a unique light fixture.

kok: Haino kisa naikini khai belai takhaidi, belai kwbang jolirwma khamunsukmani wngwi mano.
en: Just be careful not to overdo it, as too much stimulation can be overwhelming.

kok: In', mungsa thuyamkhotol paimanya thuyam tongthothok karwi.
en: Of course, no bedroom is complete without a comfortable bed.

kok: Sakina Aissa kaisa chikonsa kami bising achaikha ah Algeria hapungrokni bising.
en: Sakina Aissa was born in a small village in the mountains of Algeria.

kok: Bini maphasong wngkha Berbers, kaisa bosong bodolrok je ah hakotor swnmao.
en: Her parents were Berbers, one of the many ethnic groups that make up the country.

kok: Sakina kaisa gana-takma hoda bising torw, boro borok juda juda bosongrokni tongo tei kwchangtotok bising thansa samungkhayo.
en: Sakina grew up in a close-knit community, where people of different ethnicities lived and worked together in peace.

kok: Phiya jephuru Sakina bisi omor 10 wngkha, ah luku choba Algeria bising ongkhor kha.
en: But when Sakina was 10 years old, the civil war in Algeria broke out.

kok: Ah nanglaimung wngkha ah kwbangkuk Arab tei ah chikonsa Berber kwcharo.
en: The conflict was between the Arab majority and the Berber minority.

kok: Sakinani kami ah kwcharo manjakha, tei bo yakpuila nukjakha ah bulaimung tei baikhrupmani je ah choba tubumani.
en: Sakina's village was caught in the middle, and she witnessed firsthand the violence and destruction that the war brought.

kok: Kwbangma borokrok bwtharjakha, tei teibo kwbangma bohrokni norokrok yakarna bwkhak sakphanjakha.
en: Many people were killed, and many more were forced to flee their homes.

kok: Sakinani nukhung wngkha omoni bising je thaikwmajak wngkha.
en: Sakina's family was among those who were displaced.

kok: Ah hachingma bising bohrok kharwi bathakthai camp bwkhak bohrok phaikha, boro bohrok naithokya tonghalorol bising tongkha.
en: They fled to a refugee camp in the desert, where they lived in squalid conditions.

kok: Ah choba tikikha kaisa bisichi slai teibo karwi, tei omo kaisa Sakina tei bini nukhungni sakao kaisa swbiamani sekrupma wngkha.
en: The war lasted for more than a decade, and it had a devastating impact on Sakina and her family.

kok: Bohrokni jottomanwi tongmani bohrok kwmajakham tei bohrok kirima bising tongma bwkhak bohrokni langmarok bagwi bohrok sakphanjak wngkha.
en: They lost everything they had, and they were forced to live in fear for their lives.

kok: Phiya haino ah jotto dukhu manmani kwcharni bising, Sakina waisaphano khajamung kwmajakya.
en: But even in the midst of all the suffering, Sakina never lost hope.

kok: Bo saimano je salsa, ah choba painai tei bo bini nok bwkhak phirok mananw.
en: She knew that one day, the war would end and she would be able to return home.

en: If there was one fruit that could be considered the king of fruits, it would be the mango.

en: Some of the most popular varieties include the Alphonso, the Kent, and the Haden.

kok: Thaichukrok hainohai kwthar chajakha, phiya bohrok kaisa dalbidal chahmarok, mwkhwihrok, smoothes, tei muirok bising phwnangjak bo mano.
en: Mangoes are typically eaten fresh, but they can also be used in a variety of dishes, such as salads, smoothies, and curries.

kok: Bohrok kwran, canned, eba bwtwi bising swnam bo mano.
en: They can also be dried, canned, or made into juice.

kok: Thaichukrok kaisa kwbang sinai tei kothok bwthaih wngkha je kwbangma juda juda lamarok bising twih tongthokjak mano.
en: Mangoes are a versatile and delicious fruit that can be enjoyed in many different ways.

kok: Bohrok wngkha kaisa sakdukma tei chahkohlom chahmung eba olo chahmung saima, tei bohrok kaisa dalbidal chahmarok bisingtwih phwnangjak bo mano.
en: They are a healthy and nutritious snack or dessert option, and they can also be used in a variety of dishes.

kok: Tumungno nwng kaisa thaichuk waisa phano chaitok naiyakhukhe, ang nono khaina bwkhak khatungrimung rio.
en: If you have never tried a mango, I encourage you to do so.

kok: Loi wngmani: Kaisa kothoma khajamung tei loi wngmani hamnani wngkha kaisaa kubui kebengmung je chirasairok borok ah hayung yaksiyagra nangrwmarok.
en: Addiction: A Story of Hope and Recovery Addiction is a serious problem that affects millions of people around the world.

kok: Omo kaisa 3 tei judakhai tonmani saimanma, phiya aro hamnami bagwi kajamung tongo.
en: It can be a difficult and isolating experience, but there is hope for recovery.

kok: Oh koksopn bising, chwng khoroksa borokni bagwi kothoma kaisa sanai je loi wngmani bai khapharjak phiya obono mechenma bwkwhak phaimankha.
en: In this article, we will tell the story of a person who struggled with addiction but was able to overcome it.

kok: Chwng kwtal karima ah juda juda bwchwlwirok naiyanw je bohrokni loi wngmani bwkhak khanglaijak, ah bataimungrok bohrok hamani bising dadakdidik wngmani, tei ah manwirok je bohrokno omo bising twih mana chubachu khaimani.
en: We will explore the different factors that contributed to their addiction, the challenges they faced in recovery, and the things that helped them get through it.

kok: Chini kothoma kaisa bwrwima sikli mung Sarah bai chengjago.
en: Our story begins with a young woman named Sarah.

kok: Sarah wngkha kaisa kwchwng tei manphanjak rwngswrwngnai, phiya bo khapharjak khachuk-buchuk tei khakwbaimani bai.
en: Sarah was a bright and talented student, but she struggled with anxiety and depression.

kok: Bo kephekbithirok tei arak sak-bithi rwma bwkhak phwnangnani chengkha, tei daktino bini loi wngmani spiraled kaswkma baira wngthangkha.
en: She began using drugs and alcohol to self-medicate, and soon her addiction spiraled out of control.

kok: Sarah bini samung kwmajakha, bini halokbokmarok, tei bini nok.
