en: Sarah lost her job, her relationships, and her home.

kok: Bo nokthai kwrwi wngkha tei lamarogo ma tongkha jephuru bo paithago kokchapkha bo chubama nanai hwnwi.
en: She was homeless and living on the streets when she finally decided to get help.

kok: Sarah kaisa saknaimung pandarem hapkha, aro bo swrwngkha bini loi wngmani yaphang bagwirok tei bahaikhe bini khanangjak no samung chokrwnai bwkhak kaisa sakduma lama bising.
en: Sarah entered a treatment program, where she learned about the root causes of her addiction and how to cope with her emotions in a healthy way.

kok: Bo kwtal bayaprok bo swnamkha je bini hamnani no twichuruma khayo.
en: She also made new friends who were supportive of her recovery.

kok: Saknaimung dalbidal talrok olo, Sarah bini kwtal langma chengna tiyar wngkha.
en: After several months of treatment, Sarah was ready to start her new life.

kok: Bo kaisa samung mankhaa, kaisa nokthai bisingo lorikha, tei bo bini chomimanirokno teisa tisana bwkhak chengkha.
en: She got a job, moved into an apartment, and began to rebuild her relationships.

kok: Salsa, kaisa malmatarokni motha ah twi hakor kuthumkha, kisa nwngmarok tongthogwi.
en: One day, a group of animals were gathered at the watering hole, enjoying a few drinks.

kok: Iko ah nwngmarok kochokheno, ah malmatarok bataina bwkhak chengkha.
en: As the drinks flowed, the animals began to get competitive.

kok: Bohrok batai kachikmani chengkha kubun thwgwi naina bwkhak sabo jottoni slai arak nwngwi man.
en: They started racing each other to see who could drink the most alcohol.

kok: Ah bataimani wngkha kirimasingsa, tei ah malmatarok teibo tei teibo phekrwjak manwi tongkha.
en: The competition was fierce, and the animals were getting more and more intoxicated.

kok: Paithago, khoroksa malmatarokni bising, kaisa mwnwi, tei nwngwi manliya.
en: Finally, one of the animals, a deer, could drink no more.

kok: Bo goirok thang ah twi hakorni tei lengkha.
en: He stumbled away from the watering hole and collapsed.

kok: Ah kubun malmatarok mwnwikha tei choyawui nwngkha.
en: The other animals laughed and continued to drink.

kok: Phiya hwnkhe, ah mwnwi jangrima bwkha chengkha.
en: But then, the deer started to convulse.

kok: Bo arak thwima bithimani wngkha, tei bo thwina nai tongkha.
en: He had alcohol poisoning, and he was dying.

kok: Ah kubun malmatarok termankha je bohrok tamo khaikha hwnwi, tei borok kirijakha.
en: The other animals realized what they had done, and they were horrified.

kok: Bohrok ah mwswi no chubana bwkha chaithokha, phiya omo belai lerwi thangkha.
en: They tried to help the deer, but it was too late.

kok: Bo kisa swrapsa olo thwikha.
en: He died a few minutes later.

kok: Ah malmatarok jotto belai mokjak wngkha, tei bohrok swmai thangkha bohrok tei arak nwngliya hwnwi.
en: The animals were all very sad, and they vowed never to drink alcohol again.

kok: Chwraiphangsini thwngmungrok wngkha chini langmarokni bagwi kaisa mahmlai bokcho,
en: Childhood games are a special part of our lives.

kok: Bohrok chwngno thongthok tei mwnwimarok damrwirok bai bago, tei bohrok chwngno nangkukma langma poriremrok swrwngna bagwi chubao.
en: They provide us with hours of fun and laughter, and they help us learn important life lessons.

kok: Baksa ah belai lulu hamjajak chwraiphangsini thwngmungrok wngkha huijakma, dwkhwi buchukni budul, dwkhwi barsuma, tei marbels khobwi.
en: Some of the most popular childhood games include hide-and-seek, tag, jump rope, and marbles.

kok: Oh thwngmungrok wngkha khakepleng bwkhak thwngma tei belai kisa manwi-khwnwirok nangma, bohrokno jotto omorrokni bagwi chasukjak swnamani.
en: These games are simple to play and require very few materials, making them perfect for kids of all ages.

kok: Jora rwmung bising tongthok wngjak bwkhak, chwraiphangsini thwngmungrok chwrairokno borokni hodarwk hamkrai tei motor yaksrairok bo chubai mano.
en: In addition to being fun, childhood games can also help children develop their social and motor skills.

kok: Huijakma chwrairokno phwrwngo bahai kubunrok bai chubalaima bwkhak tei bahai bwkhangrogo rwtharma.
en: Hide-and-seek teaches children how to cooperate with others and how to follow directions.

kok: Dwkhwi buchukni budul rok chwrairokno bohrokni raibaisamung tei agility hamkrayo chubamarok.
en: Tag helps children develop their coordination and agility.

kok: Dwkhwi barsuma chwrairokno bohrokni ojon tei kokyapri hamrwma chubamarok.
en: Jump rope helps children improve their balance and rhythm.

kok: Tei marbles chwrairokno bahai khe baitaina bwkhak phwrwngmarok tei bahaikhe jitimani tei harimani bai phaiphalmung bwkhak.
en: And marbles teaches children how to compete and how to deal with winning and losing.

kok: Chwraiphangsini thwngmungrok wngkha kaisa kotorkuar lama chwrairokni bagwi bohrokni bayaprok tei nukhung bai kwrwngma bwkhak.
en: Childhood games are also a great way for kids to connect with their friends and family.

kok: Jephuru nwng khoroksaswk bai kaisa thwngmung thwngo, nwng kaisa saimanjak bakjak swnamani je nono thansa ganarwk khai tubui mano.
en: When you play a game with someone, you're creating a shared experience that can bring you closer together.

kok: Tei jephuru nwng nini nukhung bai kaisa thwngmung thwngo nwng haino tongthok simi ya, nwng twbo swrwngmani bahaikhe thansa samung khainai tei bahai khoroksa tei khoroksa no twichuruma khainai.
en: And when you play a game with your family, you're not only having fun, you're also learning how to work together and how to support each other.

kok: Talikhahamya kwbangma ah hamkuk chwrai phangsini thwngmungrok je chwng torwi thwngwi phaimani bohrok tabuk aswk luluk hamjajak wngya agi waisa wngwi phaima hai.
en: Unfortunately, many of the classic childhood games that we grew up playing are no longer as popular as they once were.

kok: Ang nono tini swihormani bagwi boromjakha.
en: I am honored to be writing to you today.

kok: Ang nini samungni kotor bhokto, tei ang nini kokbwkhal bai khaswrango "kunu lorima bara kwrwi", jerw nwng pherlaimani salaima bisngtwi kwchang nobarhalok eba kwchang raksarima nokbarhalok.
en: I am a huge fan of your work, and I was inspired by your essay "No Extra Movement", where you discuss the difference between cool weather and freezing cold weather.

kok: Ang oh kokbwkhalo ani sak-sak wansukma bwkhak rina muchungo.
en: I would like to share my own thoughts on this topic.

kok: Kwchang nobarholok belai no swrangphirimani tei phanrimani.
en: Cool weather is refreshing and invigorating.

kok: Kutung tungplama simi holirwmung lamsogwi mano tei omo sina simanwi siringsiring tei kwchangthotok swnam mano.
en: It can be a welcome relief from the heat of summer, and it can create a sense of calm and tranquility.

kok: Kwchang raksarima nokbarhalok, tei kubun digi, belaino rakphereh tei nakarmung riya.
en: Freezing cold weather, on the other hand, is harsh and unforgiving.

kok: Omo kirimasingsa wngmano, tei omo 3 takutung tei khasrangwi mano.
en: It can be dangerous, and it can make it difficult to stay warm and comfortable.

kok: Kaisa kotorma pherlaimani bising kwchang nokbarhalok tei kwchang raksarima nokbarhalok wngkha mohai omo chini sakno khoti khayo.
en: One of the biggest differences between cool weather and freezing cold weather is the way it affects our bodies.

kok: Jephuru kwchango, chini sakrok kaham khai tonimano tei bohrokni temparature no kwlaikhe halogwi.
en: When it is cool, our bodies are able to maintain their temperature relatively easily.

kok: Chwng jampar eba jacket kanna nangwi mano, phiya chwng tangrak tei khsrangwi tongwi mano.
en: We may need to wear a sweater or jacket, but we can still stay active and comfortable.

kok: Jephuru kwchang raksario, chini sakrok teibono teibo samung kwrak khaina ango kutung tongna khe.
en: When it is freezing cold, our bodies have to work much harder to stay warm.

kok: Chwng richumung pola thumsa nanganw, tei chwng nokbising ma tonganw.
en: We may need to bundle up in layers of clothing, and we may even need to stay indoors.

kok: Tei kaisa pherlaimani bising twi kwchang nokbarhalok tei kwchang raksarima nokbarhalok lama wngkha chini morji no gwdalrima.
en: Another difference between cool weather and freezing cold weather is the way it affects our mood.

kok: Kokchirmani wngkha kaisa hamya nangmani.
en: Criticism is a necessary evil.

kok: Omo wngkha ah twtamani tansep tei dorbaphangmani ah mungsaswk tongham, tei omo kaisa morokjak kol ah rikmung samung charwmani bagwi, kokrwbai, rwchpmung, eba kubun swnamanma chaitokma.
en: It is the process of evaluating and judging the quality of something, and it can be a valuable tool for improving the work of art, literature, music, or other creative endeavor.

kok: Haiphano, kokchirmani baikhrupmung bo wngmano, mungsa swnamani kokphirokma yapharmani karwi kubunrok tamo swnamkha abo tola swbaimani.
en: However, criticism can also be destructive, tearing down what others have created without offering any constructive feedback.

kok: Ah chasukjak kokchirmani wngkha kaisa je kainwi banik tei chubama wngkha.
en: The perfect criticism is one that is both fair and helpful.

kok: Omo khorang kanrokmani tei yakumu yaphang sakao wngna nango, tei bahai ah samung swngmani bising charwma bwkhak omo nangmani kokberamarok karwi yapharna nango.
en: It should be based on sound reasoning and evidence, and it should offer specific suggestions for how to improve the work in question.

kok: Ah chasukjak kokchirma wngkha khoroksaswk je ah rwngdal manwi bagwi elemgnang wngma tei je bohrokni wansukmarok kwchwngma tei kothumma sraisrai bwkhak chukma wngkha.
en: The perfect critic is someone who is knowledgeable about the subject matter and who is able to articulate their thoughts clearly and concisely.

kok: Kokchirmani wngkha kaisa yaksrai je swrwngma tei charrwma loi khlaimung bai swrwng mano.
en: Criticism is a skill that can be learned and improved with practice.

kok: Tumungno nwng khoroksa kaham kokchir wngmani bising ol manmung wngkha, aro kisa manwirok tongo nwng khlaimano.
en: If you are interested in becoming a better critic, there are a few things you can do.

kok: Puila, kuarmakhe poridi tei ah juda juda sakmang rikmung tei kokrwbai kaisa kwrak buchimani hamkrai khaidi.
en: First, read widely and develop a strong understanding of the different forms of art and literature.

kok: Nwirem, dehrama wansukma bwkhak swrwngdi ah samung naitongmani bagwi.
en: Second, learn to think critically about the work you are consuming.

kok: Nwngsakbaithang swngmarok swngdi ah suinaini naimung bagwi, ah nainaini bagwi ah samung khlaima, tei ah seprok ah rikkwrwng bai phwnangjakma.
en: Ask yourself questions about the author's purpose, the audience for the work, and the techniques used by the artist.

kok: Thamrem, kubunrok bai nini khakamungrok bakna bwkhak muchungmani wngkha, ahaino tumung bohrok luku hmjakjak wngya phano.
en: Third, be willing to share your opinions with others, even if they are not popular.

kok: Ah kahamkuk lama nini dehrama yaksrairok wngkha bohrokno loi khlaimani bwkhak charwma bwkhak.
en: The best way to improve your critical skills is to practice them.

kok: Coffee phalnok tangmungni bai dosidopra wngjak iko borok phaima tei thangma bagwi, atomsa fatsa coffee cup eba cha borokni sal chengma bwkhak.
en: The coffee shop was bustling with activity as people came and went, grabbing a quick cup of coffee or tea to start their day.

kok: Baristas rok kwrak samung khlayo sanmarok saka tonina bagwwi, phiya bohrok koksana baagwwi jora naitongo borok ni painai borokrok bai tei bohrokno kahamkhe sinina bagwi.
en: The baristas were working hard to keep up with the demand, but they were also taking the time to chat with their customers and get to know them.

kok: Khoroksa baristas, bwrwima sikla mung Sarah, wngkha kiching hai tei phatarlamsoknai.
en: One of the baristas, a young woman named Sarah, was particularly friendly and outgoing.

kok: Bo bini painai borokrokno sinina hamjago tei bohrokni langmano twi swrwngo.
en: She loved getting to know her customers and learning about their lives.

kok: Salsa, khoroksa chwla habphaikha nugwi khakamani bini sal hamya thang tongo hwnwi.
en: One day, a man came in who looked like he was having a bad day.

kok: Bo uahrap thong wngjak tei bini mokolrok thwipojak.
en: He was pale and his eyes were bloodshot.

kok: Sarah saimano je bo kulum wngjak hwnwi, haini bagwi bo bono suta cha cup yapharkha.
en: Sarah could tell that he was sick, so she offered him a free cup of tea.

kok: Ah chwla kotorkuarkhai cha no yachakha tei kaisa khukthepama nakha.
en: The man gratefully accepted the tea and took a sip.

kok: Bo logilogi no kaham wansukma chengjakha.
en: He immediately started to feel better.

kok: Bo Sarah no sakha je bo kisa salrok romwi kulum kailajak, phiya bo saknainai ni oro thangwi manyakhu.
en: He told Sarah that he had been feeling sick for a few days, but he hadn't been able to get to the doctor.

kok: Sarah bono sakha bo saknainai ni oro jeswk dakti naijak mankhe chanai, phiya kaisadigi bo bono kaham wansukma khai chubana bagwi bono tei kisa cha swnamwi yapharkha.
en: Sarah told him that he should go see a doctor as soon as possible, but she also offered to make him some more tea to help him feel better in the meantime.

kok: Ah chwla paithago coffee phalnogo tongkha kisa jorani bagwi, cha nwngwi tei Sarah bai kok salai.
en: The man ended up staying at the coffee shop for a while, drinking tea and talking to Sarah.

kok: Bo bono bini samung tei nukhungni bagwi sakha.
en: He told her about his job and his family.

kok: Omo nangmani bisingtwih aborokno chubama bwkhak kaisa sep, tei ah hayung pherlaima bisingtwih kaisa swnamma.
en: It's an opportunity to help those in need and make a difference in the world.

kok: Phiya waisa-wuisu, daan wansukmanya thaihmungrok tongwi mano.
en: But sometimes, charity can have unexpected consequences.

kok: Kaisa jottoni slai daan thaihmungrok muchungjakya manthok wngkha je omo kaisa ah rwinaini sakao sakbokjkama swnam mano.
en: One of the most common unintended consequences of charity is that it can create a dependency on the giver.

kok: Jephuru borokno chubachu rijago omoni bagwi samung khaiya karwi, bohrok khakama bwkhak chengwi mano je choyai chubachu khaina.
en: When people are given help without having to work for it, they can start to expect that help to continue.

kok: Omo kaisa khangra babai tubumani tei sinai simanwi mung rwma.
en: This can lead to a lack of motivation and a sense of entitlement.

kok: Tei kaisa daan thaihmungrok muchungjakya wngkha je omo kaisa khakma ah rwnai tei mannaini kwcharo swnam mano.
en: Another unintended consequence of charity is that it can create a divide between the giver and the receiver.

kok: Ah rwnai mannai ni slai kahamkuk wansuk mano, jephuru ah mannai hamsukya eba lachijak wansuk mano.
en: The giver may feel superior to the receiver, while the receiver may feel inferior or ashamed.

kok: Omo kainwi bodolrokni kwthalai borom rwma yaphang saka kaisa holokrung tangma bwkhak karwi 3 omo swnam mano.
en: This can make it difficult for both parties to build a relationship based on mutual respect.

kok: Paithago, daan waisa-wuisu teibo chaya khlaimano kahamni slai.
en: Finally, charity can sometimes do more harm than good.

kok: Tumungno ah chubachu je rwjak wngkha gothokya wngma eba tumungno omo rwjakya wngkha kaisa lama bising je borom rwjak wngkha, omo kubuino ah tonghalok hamya swnam mano.
en: If the help that is given is not appropriate or if it is not given in a way that is respectful, it can actually make the situation worse.

kok: Phunukmari karwi, haino nokthaikwrwi borokno tongthai eba samung ni swrwngmani rwya karwi chahthaih bakmani bo haino bohrokni nokathaikwrwi tangrak khlaimanma.
en: For example, giving food to a homeless person without also providing them with shelter or job training may only enable their homelessness.

kok: Ao, omo wngkha haino kisa ah daan wansukmanya thaihmungrok.
en: Of course, these are just a few of the unintended consequences of charity.

kok: Aro wngkha kwbanga kubun lamarok je daan ulta nang mano.
en: There are many other ways that charity can backfire.

kok: Kwtal korai nana bagwi hatio thang phuru, ang bo palino nanai sa'ui rohor kha tei aroni mwrwknai nobo swng kha abo hai toda tong hwnwi.
en: When I went shopping for a new horse, I mentioned the colour I was looking for and asked the attendant if they had anything in stock.

kok: Bo ano dalbidal korai phunuk kha, phiya abohrok bebakno ang chajakya.
en: She showed me a few different horses, but none of them were quite right.

kok: Hakhe, bo sakha abotwi palini korai kwtal tabokno sok phaidrop.
en: Then, she mentioned that they had just received a new horse in that colour.

kok: Ang naina thang kha hakhe ang waisabai no chajak kha.
en: I went to take a look and I was immediately smitten.

kok: A korai damri naithokma kwchak kwtha'ui ni pali kolok khe, khitongni bikhumu tei khitong bo.
en: The horse was a beautiful chestnut mare with a long, flowing mane and tail.

kok: Bo belai tongna kwrwng tei kwbo kwrwng.
en: She was also very well-behaved and seemed to be quite intelligent.

kok: Ang bono paina hwnwi khao chong kha tei paiwi na'ui bo belai kha swrwng kha.
en: I decided to buy her and I'm so glad I did.

kok: Bo masa chini nukhungni borok hai wngwi thang kha tei bono ani langma o manwi belai tongthok kha.
en: She's been a wonderful addition to my family and I'm so happy to have her in my life.

kok: Ang puila bono nogo tubu phuru, ang malmata naikwrwngrokni thanio boni sakham nairwna bagwi twlangwi thang kha.
en: When I first brought her home, I took her to the vet for an inspection.

kok: A malmata naikwrwng sakha bo bebak no kaham tongo hwnwi tei bo belai kwchang kwchang korai.
en: The vet said that she was in good health and that she was a very sound horse.

kok: Bo sak kaham tongo hwnwi khwna'ui ani uanama hamkha tei ang korai kanani belai tongthokjak.
en: I was relieved to hear that she was healthy and I was excited to start riding her.

kok: Ang tabuk hatibar kisisa romwi korai kamani tei ang kwbwino tongthoksok kha.
en: I've been riding my horse for a few weeks now and I'm really enjoying it.

kok: Kasana bagwi a korai belai kaham tei bo ani kok bo khwna o.
en: She's a very easy horse to ride and she's very responsive to my commands.

kok: Nini chalokjaknai license mannani kwbangma chaslokjorarokni bagwi tongkthwter lama.
en: Getting your driver's license is a rite of passage for many teenagers.

kok: Omo buchimanikhe kwtal mil yokmani tei phiyokjakmani.
en: It signifies a new level of freedom and independence.

kok: Haiphano, malukung swikni ungkuluk thangmani puila jora sundrumahai wngwi mano.
en: However, getting behind the wheel of a car for the first time can also be daunting.

kok: Aro kwbangma manwino twi wansuk thai, lamani raida simi juda juda malkhungrok sapokthaih.
en: There are so many things to think about, from the rules of the road to the different types of vehicles.

kok: Kaisa kotorma bataimani chalukna swrwngmani hwnkhe juda juda lamani kaurwlaimung bokchono twi.
en: One of the biggest challenges of learning to drive is dealing with the different road conditions.

kok: Nwng puila jephuru chengwi ongkhoro, nwng juda juda bwcwllwino saimana nangkukmani je nini chalukmano gwdalwi, ahaino nobarhalok, salni jora, tei thahnglaiso bangmari.
en: When you're first starting out, it's important to be aware of the different factors that can affect your driving, such as the weather, the time of day, and the amount of traffic.

kok: Phunukamari hwnkhe, watwio chalukmarok sal kutung chalukmani belai juda.
en: For example, driving in the rain is much different than driving on a sunny day.

kok: Lamarok wngkha rimirwk tei nukmani khairio, haini bagwi nwng teibo naikani tei twrwk twrwk wngdi.
en: The roads are slicker and visibility is reduced, so you need to be more careful and slow down.

kok: Teikaisa chalokma swrwngmani bataima hwnkhe gears sehmani.
en: Another challenge of learning to drive is shifting gears.

kok: Omo kahamkhai borokni bagwi wngmano je swkango waisaphano yakbai tangjaknai rohormungno chalukjakyakhe.
en: This can be especially difficult for people who have never driven a manual transmission before.

kok: Omo loi khlaimannakhe khaichiwi nango, phiya jodi waisa khaikhe, omo nwirem tongraida wngwi thango.
en: It takes practice to get the hang of it, but once you do, it will become second nature.

kok: Nwng teibo chaluknani khasrangma manwi mano, nwng nini malkungni ganarwkrwk khao nangma khainani chenganw.
en: As you get more comfortable driving, you'll start to feel closer to your car.

kok: Nwng teibo hamraia kahamkhe buchinai bahaikhe handlekhai tei bahaikhe kaswkma khai.
en: You'll develop a better understanding of how it handles and how to control it.

kok: Ani nokarini kisa siringsiring tei hodani nukhung-bayap hai doyungni bwkhao chongma.
en: My neighborhood is a quiet and family-friendly community located in the heart of the city.

kok: Omo bohrok buthup baksayani nok se, tei aro homnino mungsaswk choli tongo.
en: It's home to a diverse group of people, and there's always something going on.

kok: Aro dalbidal khumbahri tongo, thwngjaknai, tei hoda kwcharw, abo kotorkuar thai hwnwi swnamjakmani nukhung kaisa tisana bwkhak.
en: There are several parks, playgrounds, and community centers, making it a great place to raise a family.

kok: Aro kwbangma chahnok tongo, phalnokrok, tei paiphalnai, nokarini yakarya karwi nwng jottomanwi nangmani nwng aswkno manwi mano.
en: There are also plenty of restaurants, shops, and businesses, so you can find everything you need without having to leave the neighborhood.

kok: Kaisa manwi ang belai hamjakmani ani nokarini bagwi hwnkhe hodani sinai simanwi.
en: One of the things I love most about my neighborhood is the sense of community.

kok: Jottono saimano jottono karwi, tei aro homnino sinai simanwi twichuruma tongo.
en: Everyone knows everyone else, and there's always a sense of support.

kok: Nwng mungsamanwi nangkhe, aro homnino khoroksaswk tongo je muchungwi chubana bagwi.
en: If you need something, there's always someone who is willing to help out.

kok: Ang ani nokarinio bisi 10 saka romwi tongwi phaimani, tei ang kisa langmakolok bayaprok swnamkha oro.
en: I've lived in my neighborhood for over 10 years, and I've made some lifelong friends here.

kok: Ang haiphano ani nokarini manmarino hamjago.
en: I also love the convenience of my neighborhood.

kok: Omo jottomanwi ang nangmani bai gana, tei ang kwlaikhai himwi mano eba jotto thaini bawkha saikel khaimano.
en: It's close to everything I need, and I can easily walk or bike to most places.

kok: Ani laharni pathai yagra digi aro kaisa lukuni laisunani bathakjaknai tongo, aswkno obo 1 bwkhak kaisa malkhung karwi yaksiyagra mano.
en: There's a public transportation stop right at the end of my street, so it's easy to get around without a car.

kok: Kaisa ani nokarini kebengjakma hwkhe nokni biyalwi naimanya.
en: One of the drawbacks of my neighborhood is the lack of affordable housing.

kok: Jotto nokrok kwcham wngkha tei swnamphina nangphiro, tei belai kuchuk morokuk.
en: Many of the homes are older and in need of repair, and the prices are very high.

kok: Scott wngkha sikla soisikwrwng bo homnino habarni bagwi belai khamuchungjago.
en: Scott was a young scientist who had always been passionate about nature.

kok: Bo chikonsa aoli hapung gana torwi phayo, tei bo bini jora yokphuru bolongo tei hauarrok naitukberayo.
en: He grew up in a small town near the mountains, and he spent his free time exploring the woods and fields.

kok: Bo aro tongnairok juda juda buphang-uaphang tei malmatarokni bagwi swrwngnani hamjakago, tei bo bohrokni tongwimanthai no bachirina bagwi homnino muchungjak.
en: He loved learning about the different plants and animals that lived there, and he was always eager to protect their habitats.

kok: Jephuru Scott rwnwgkotoro wngkha, bo soisimung tongkhorno porijak.
en: When Scott was in college, he studied environmental science.

kok: Bo habarni hayungo bwskango kwbangma kirima bagwi swrwngkha, tei bo jephano kaisa chubachu khainani bwkhak khathonjak.
en: He learned about the many threats facing the natural world, and he became determined to do something to help.

kok: Rwngthekani olo, bo kaisa khatimani motha o samung mankha, boro bo samungbwtango samung khayo komornai dahl no bachirinani tei rwphima piyakmung ecosystems.
en: After graduating, he got a job with a conservation organization, where he worked on projects to protect endangered species and restore damaged ecosystems.

kok: Salsa, Scott kaisa samungbwtango samungkhai tongmani bolong rwphima bwkhak je sraisrai-tanjak mani.
en: One day, Scott was working on a project to restore a forest that had been clear-cut.

kok: Jephururu bo ario naikolwi tongphuru bo ayang naro thumsa borokbai malaikha je lamchaya khai buphangrok chirphangmani.
en: He was surveying the area when he came across a group of people who were illegally logging the trees.

kok: Scott buthupno swkangbaiswkang malaikha tei bohrok bono choprona hwnwi sikrikha.
en: Scott confronted the group, and they threatened to attack him.

kok: Haiphano, Scott hawo bachai tongkha, tei bo daktino bohrokno yakarna bagwi gosirikha.
en: However, Scott stood his ground, and he eventually convinced them to leave.

kok: Scott's ni tangmung ah salo kubuno samungbwtang khatinairokno khaswrang rwkha.
en: Scott's actions that day inspired the other conservationists working on the project.

kok: Borok jotto bini khakrakno nugwi khaswrangjak tei khathonmani habarno bachirina bagwi.
en: They were all inspired by his courage and determination to protect nature.

kok: Bohrok bolongno rwphima khaina abwi thansakhe samung khlaikha, tei bohrok kaisa tongwimanai hamsama swnamkha buphang-uaphang tei malmatarok je aro tongnairok.
en: They worked together to restore the forest, and they created a thriving habitat for the plants and animals that lived there.

kok: Ah doyung wngkha samung-humung bai gundrijak wngkha.
en: The city was abuzz with activity.

kok: Borokrok ayang uyang tei domani bwkhak wngkha, jottono bohrokni sakni sogwina thairok khorok bising chongwi.
en: People were rushing to and fro, all with their own destinations in mind.

kok: Ah nokbar rwja wngkha ah malkhungni hoku dummarok bahai bai tei ah horns tammani khorang.
en: The air was thick with the smell of exhaust fumes and the sound of honking horns.

kok: Phiya ahaino jotto oh ubrumjabrum ah kwcharni bising, aro kaisa sinai simanwi naituk manna bwkhak wngkha.
en: But even in the midst of all this chaos, there was a sense of humor to be found.

kok: Salsa, ang ah lama tola himwi thangphuru ang ohjora kaisa chwlano achukthai sakao achukmani nukha, kaisa koktunlaih porimani.
en: One day, I was walking down the street when I saw a man sitting on a bench, reading a newspaper.

kok: Bo kaisa tuxedo tei thupi kolok kanajak, tei bini mokol bising kaisa monocle tongo.
en: He was wearing a tuxedo and a top hat, and he had a monocle in his eye.

kok: Bo mohai nukjak tongkha je bo suja no kaisa tokeni ongkhor phai hai.
en: He looked like he was straight out of a movie.

kok: Ang ahaino ganarwk thangkha, ang nukha je ang chwla kubuio kaisa mwnwikothok bijap pori tongo.
en: As I got closer, I saw that the man was actually reading a comic book.

kok: Bo chirikhogwi mwnwi tongkha, tei ang mwnwiya karwi tongwi manliya.
en: He was laughing out loud, and I couldn't help but smile.

kok: Omo aswkno mwnwikothok ah chwla no nukhe, je raidatwi aswkno richumjak, kaisa mwnwi kothok bijap porimani.
en: It was so funny to see this man, who was dressed so formally, reading a comic book.

kok: Omo wngkha bo bini sakni hayungo tongwi tongo, boro jesaphano wngmano.
en: It was like he was living in his own world, where anything was possible.

kok: Ang choyawui ano lama thangkha, tei ang ah tuxedo chwlani bagwi wansuknani mwthak se manliya.
en: I continued on my way, and I couldn't stop thinking about the man in the tuxedo.

kok: Bo ano kaisa muitomanrikha je ahaino jotto oh ubrumjabrum ah kwcharni bising, aro homnino mwnwikothokni bagwi khotol tongo.
en: He was a reminder that even in the midst of all the chaos of city life, there is always room for humor.

kok: Ah bwrwima ah podium o bachakha, bini khorang sraisrai tei phangnang.
en: The woman stood at the podium, her voice clear and strong.

kok: "Chwng kaisa hayungrwgwi biyal malaimani wngkha, " bo sakha.
en: "We are facing a global crisis," she said.

kok: "Khoranrok wngkha teibo kwthajak tei kwrak, bohrok kaisa chini hagri sakao swabaimani sekrupma tongmani wngkha.
en: "Droughts are becoming more frequent and severe, and they are having a devastating impact on our planet.

kok: Ah wngthahng bisi saichung bising, chwng Africa, Asia, tei Americas bising khoranrok nukha.
en: In the past year alone, we have seen droughts in Africa, Asia, and the Americas.

kok: Oh khoran kuarpisarjak okkhwi, bigra, tei norjakmung pherjak tongo.
en: These droughts have caused widespread hunger, poverty, and displacement.

kok: Chwng tabukno samung ma khainai oh biyal nikuma bwkhak."
en: We must act now to address this crisis."

kok: Ah bwrwimani kokthairok kaisa yapha khoropma bai malaima wngkha.
en: The woman's words were met with a round of applause.

kok: Bo nokbartwibar swlaima sakao kaisa koklam pandao sana bwkhak kwcharjakha, tei bo ah swbaimani sekrupma khoranrok saimanrimani tisama bwkhak bini char phwnangkha.
en: She had been invited to speak at a conference on climate change, and she had used her platform to raise awareness of the devastating impact of droughts.

kok: Bo haphangrok tei beparirokno ringkha samung nana bwkhak nokkwkhwrang phab emissions lonma bwkhak tei ah nokbartwibar swlaima sekrupmarok holirwma wngkha.
en: She called on governments and businesses to take action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate the effects of climate change.

kok: Bo saksakrokno bo koikha bohrokni sakni langrok biisng swlaimarok swnamna bwkhak, ahaino bohrokni baimani tei teiwaisa gurimani lonmani.
en: She also urged individuals to make changes in their own lives, such as reducing their energy consumption and recycling.

kok: Ah bwrwimani koklam wngkha kaisa phangnang muitunarakna nokbartwibar nikuma bwkhak ah matangthai nangma.
en: The woman's speech was a powerful reminder of the urgent need to address climate change.

kok: Khoranrok wngkha haino kaisa ah kwbangm kekrupmrok nokbartwibar swlaima je chwng swkango nukmani, tei bohrok aswkno hamya wngna bwkhak thangmani tumungno chwng samung nayakhe.
en: Droughts are just one of the many impacts of climate change that we are already seeing, and they are only going to get worse if we do not take action.

kok: Chwng jotto thansa samung makhaina teibo kaisa tikimannai thinang swnamna bwkhak chini hatingni bagwi.
en: We must all work together to create a more sustainable future for our planet.

kok: Ani ama markhe songkrwng.
en: My mother is a fantastic cook.

kok: Ang je muito manmani bo kwdwkma jora romwmi chini nukhungni bagwi songwi phaimani, tei bini muirok homnino kothok.
en: She has been cooking for our family for as long as I can remember, and her food is always delicious.

kok: Bo homnini no kwtal recipes tei sep bai amjokmung khayo, tei bo homnino bini elem bo kubunrokbai bakna gosio.
en: She is always experimenting with new recipes and techniques, and she is always willing to share her knowledge with others.

kok: Kaisa manwirok je ani ama songmani no belai mahmlai kubui khaimani khe bo kwthar, kuchuk-tongham sarimanwirokno phwnangwi.
en: One of the things that makes my mother's cooking so special is the fact that she uses fresh, high-quality ingredients.

kok: Bo waisa phano swnamjak eba swkang-chujak chathairok phwnangya, tei bo homnino jora nawui bini chathaino kahamkhe songo.
en: She never uses processed or pre-packaged foods, and she always takes the time to cook her food properly.

kok: Oh saktongmani bwkhak sukhrubwi bwthaihrokni bising thokmung tei chahkohlom bai kupulung muirok.
en: This attention to detail results in dishes that are full of flavor and nutrients.

kok: Tei kaisa manwi je ani ama songmani bade khaima hwnkhe bini muirokno swnamwi manmani je jottono koima bwkhak twi.
en: Another thing that sets my mother's cooking apart is her ability to create dishes that appeal to everyone.

kok: Bo homnino muchungjago kokrwnglaimung bai juda juda chahmungrok ujono toninani, tei bo homnino kwtal thokmungrok amjokmung bai muchungjago.
en: She is always willing to accommodate different dietary restrictions, and she is always willing to experiment with new flavors.

kok: Omo bono kaisa kotor songkwrwng swnamo kotor nukhungo eba borok bodolo juda juda chaihnaima bai.
en: This makes her a great cook for large families or groups of people with different tastes.

kok: Ani amani songmani wngkha kaisa kotor lama borok rokno thansa tubunani.
en: My mother's cooking is also a great way to bring people together.

kok: Jephuru bo chini bagwi songo, aphuru chwng lenglawui tei khoroksa tei khoroksa ni logisong bai jora katilayo.
en: When she cooks for us, it is a time for us to relax and enjoy each other's company.

kok: Chwng chini sal bagwi kok salayo, mwnwilayo, tei kothomarok banta khayo.
en: We talk about our day, laugh, and share stories.

kok: Aro baksa ani chajakmani muitorok tongo, tei ang ani ama no belai hambai bohrokno swnamma bagwi.
en: These are some of my fondest memories, and I am grateful to my mother for creating them.

kok: Ah sal damrwirok karwi kwchwng khai jilik jalak wng tongo, tei ah tokrok ah buphango tongthokjakkhe rwchapmani.
en: The sun had been shining brightly for hours, and the birds were singing merrily in the trees.

kok: Omo wngkha kaisa chasukjak sal Eid ni bagwi, tei kamini jottono tongthokjak wngkha.
en: It was a perfect day for Eid, and everyone in the village was excited.

kok: Ah chwrairok dakti phaijak, bohrokni kwtal richumrok kanjak manmani bising tei kaisa kotor phungbaili chamani.
en: The children had been up early, getting dressed in their new clothes and eating a big breakfast.

kok: Hwnkhe bohrok jotto mosque bwkhak surina thangkha, tei tabuk borok jotto aoli thekabwrwi bising kuthumkha, ah Eid palaijakmarok bwkhak chengma bagwi naisingmani.
en: Then they had gone to the mosque to pray, and now they were all gathered in the town square, waiting for the Eid celebrations to begin.

kok: Ah kamini aolipha yakpri sehma bwkhak ah khorangkoktokol tei jottono lamsukha.
en: The mayor of the village stepped up to the microphone and welcomed everyone.

kok: Bo sakha ah Eid ni nangkukma bagwi, tei bahai amo wngkha kaisa jora nukhung tei bayaprokni bagwi thansa phai tei palaima bwkhak.
en: He spoke about the importance of Eid, and how it was a time for family and friends to come together and celebrate.

kok: Hwnkhe bo ah kuthumjak no twlangkha kaisa surimung hambairokni bising.
en: Then he led the crowd in a prayer of thanks.

kok: Ah surimani olo, ah terrok chengkha.
en: After the prayer, the festivities began.

kok: Aro chwrairokni bagwi thwngmungrok tongo, rwchapmung tei mwsamani jottoni bagwi, tei kwbangma chathaih tei nwngwi tongthokna bwkhak.
en: There were games for the children, music and dancing for everyone, and plenty of food and drink to enjoy.

kok: Ah kamini borok mwnwikha tei kok sakha tei chakha tei nwngkha, tei bohrok jottono kaisa uanamasingsa jora mankha.
en: The people of the village laughed and talked and ate and drank, and they all had a wonderful time.

kok: Ah sal hapna bwkhak chengkheno, ah kamino borokrok nogo thangna bwkhak chengkha.
en: As the sun began to set, the people of the village started to drift home.

kok: Bohrok lengjak wngkha, phiya bohrok tongthokjak bo wngkha.
en: They were tired, but they were also happy.

kok: Bohrok kaisa chasukjak sal katikha Eid palaimani bohrokni hamjakma borokrok bai, tei bohrok saimano je bohrok omono bisirok phaima bwkhak muito khlaimano.
en: They had spent a perfect day celebrating Eid with their loved ones, and they knew that they would remember it for years to come.

kok: Bolong swnamma wngkha mohai tangsep halogwi hao buphangrok kaijakmani je swkango bolong khajakya.
en: Afforestation is the process of planting trees on land that was previously not forested.

kok: Omo podrepod karonrok paijakhe khai mano, ahaino timber manthogo, haisingni hammung chasama, eba bolongni langma tongthai kaisa swnamwi mano.
en: It can be done for a variety of reasons, such as to provide timber, to improve soil quality, or to create a habitat for wildlife.

kok: Aro kwbangma manmarirok tongo bolong swnammani bwkhak.
en: There are many benefits to afforestation.

kok: Buphangrok twi bai nokbar no kwchwng khaima bwkhak chubao borok saklom tei lenglama swnamtonima rio, tei bohrok haising kochokmani kasogra o chubai mano.
en: Trees help to clean the air and water, they provide shade and shelter, and they can help to prevent soil erosion.

kok: Bohrok carbon dioxide no monogwi nokbartwibar chasama khai thani chaubai mano.
en: They can also help to improve the climate by absorbing carbon dioxide.

kok: Kaisa manmari bolong swnamthani hwnkhe je ang manjakphaimani puilayak wngkhe khorang ebrumrwma khairimani.
en: One of the benefits of afforestation that I have experienced firsthand is the reduction in noise pollution.

kok: Jephuru ang buphang ari twi himphuru, ang tokrok rwchapmani khwnai mano tei bwlairok bai nokbar sibramwi phayo.
en: When I walk through a wooded area, I can hear the birds singing and the wind rustling through the leaves.

kok: Omo kaisa belai siringsiring tei kwchangthotok manjakma, tei omo kaisamanwi je aro buphangrok jodi kwrwi hwnkhe ang tongthogwi mangwlak khamu.
en: This is a very calming and peaceful experience, and it is something that I would not be able to enjoy if there were no trees.

kok: Manmari bising jora rwmungrok je ang kok khurmani, bolong swnamani rangthong chasama bwkhak chubai mano.
en: In addition to the benefits that I have mentioned, afforestation can also help to improve the economy.

kok: Buphangrok forestry swnammung samungrok swnam mano, tei bohrok berainai rokno khasotongwi ari bwkhak tubuthani chubai mano.
en: Trees can create jobs in the forestry industry, and they can also help to attract tourists to an area.

kok: Bebagwi, bolong swnamani wngkha belai hamkraini loi khlaimung.
en: Overall, afforestation is a very beneficial practice.

kok: Oro kwbangma habar, rangthong, tei hodarwi manmarirok tongo.
en: It has many environmental, economic, and social benefits.

kok: Nwng jodi teibo bolong swnamani bagwi swrwngnani muchungjak tongkhe, ang nono khatungrimung rwi kokkhak salaikok go kisa rutukrwk khaidi.
en: If you are interested in learning more about afforestation, I encourage you to do some research on the topic.

kok: Phola gwdaljak swngchar wngkha kwbangma pali tei goron ni haphar se.
en: The spirit world is a place of many colors and shapes.

kok: O hapharo bebakno khwlaiwi mano.
en: It is a place where anything is possible.

kok: Aro raida bo kwrwi, thakmung bo kwrwi, tei ari bo kwrwi.
en: There are no rules, no limits, and no boundaries.

kok: O swngcharo, je nwng muchung mani abono wngwi mano.
en: In the spirit world, you can be anything you want to be.

kok: Nwng birwi mano, twiwi bisingo bo hama sosa'ui mano, tei nwng malmatarok bai bo kok sa'ui mano.
en: You can fly, you can breathe underwater, and you can even talk to animals.

kok: Sala, khoroksa sikli mung Abigail bolong bisingtwi himwi tong phuru bo siniya-nukya abotwi manwi nukha.
en: One day, a young woman named Abigail was walking through the forest when she came across a strange sight.

kok: Abo wngkha sola lama kwcharo bachajak, tei a sola kubun solrok hai wngya abono waisa bo nukya kho.
en: There was a coach standing in the middle of the path, and it was unlike any coach she had ever seen before.

kok: O sola dalbidal malmatarokni bukur bai swnamjak, tei abo kwchwng pali phuljak.
en: The coach was made of different parts of animals, and it was painted in bright colors.

kok: Abigail a sola no nugwi belai sina muchungjak kha, hake bo teisa gana khe nainai hwnwi khao chong kha.
en: Abigail was curious about the coach, so she decided to take a closer look.

kok: Bo aro gana sogwi ba, nukha a sola bisingo khoroksa tongo.
en: As she got closer, she saw that there was someone inside the coach.

kok: Abo wngkha khoroksa bura, tei bo singhason o achukjak.
en: It was an old man, and he was sitting on a throne.

kok: A bura ni kuphur tei kolok khosai tongo, tei bo bwlaini lolang chumjak.
en: The old man had a long white beard, and he was wearing a robe that was made of leaves.

kok: Abigail bo hai borokno waisa phano nukya kho "Hoi" a bura sakha "Ani mung Oden, tei ang o swngcharni pholano mwrwknai se".
en: Abigail had never seen anyone like him before "Hello," said the old man "My name is Oden, and I am the guardian of the spirit world.

kok: Ang ani chwraiphangni bagwi koksanani hamjago.
en: I love talking about childhood.

kok: Abo kaisa langmani yakbahra jora, uanamasingsa tei naitukberaimani kuplung.
en: It's such a special time of life, full of wonder and exploration.

kok: Ang muitomano ang chwrai phuru, ang damrwi romwi phataro thwngwi katio, thwngmani swnamo ani bayap songbai.
en: I remember when I was a child, I would spend hours playing outside, making up games with my friends.

kok: Chwng buphango sengkrakrok swnam tisao, huijak-tei-naitukma thwngo, tei sapung sal logwi chini saikelrok chalugo.
en: We would build forts in the woods, play hide-and-seek, and ride our bikes all day long.

kok: Chini thani unamani eba uanamarok kwrwi, tei chwng haino kisisajorao thangwi tonglayo.
en: We didn't have any worries or concerns, and we just lived in the moment.

kok: Ang khakamani chwraiphang belai nangkukmani tamni hinba obo kaisa jora jephuru chwng chinisaksakni bagwi swrwngma tei hayungo yaksiyagra naisikgwi.
en: I think childhood is so important because it's a time when we learn about ourselves and the world around us.

kok: Chwng kubunbai bahaikhe koksalai swrwngmano, bahai khe chini biyalno kokpairinai, tei chini khanangjakma bai bahaikhe bokcho khainai.
en: We learn how to interact with others, how to solve problems, and how to deal with our emotions.

kok: Chwng chini wansukmung rokno bo hamkrai tei tagwimano.
en: We also develop our imaginations and creativity.

kok: Chwraiphang wngkha torwnani tei hamkrai ni jora, tei omo kaisamanwi je chwng jottono naikolnai.
en: Childhood is a time of growth and development, and it's something that we should all cherish.

kok: Nini chwrairok tongkhe, ang khasrangrwma rio nono nwng jeswk jora mansak bohrokbai jora kwbang swbaidi.
en: If you have children, I encourage you to spend as much time with them as possible.

kok: Bohrokno bohrokni swngcharno naitukberaidi tei bohrokni chayani simi swrwngdi.
en: Let them explore their world and learn from their mistakes.

kok: Bohrokni bagwi tongdi jephuru bohrok nono nango, tei bohrokno tongthokna bagwi tisaridi, siklarokni sakdukma bai.
en: Be there for them when they need you, and help them to grow into happy, healthy adults.

kok: Chwraiphang belai nangmani jora, tei omo mohaimanwi je chini bagwi bebak rangmai.
en: Childhood is a precious time, and it's something that we should all treasure.

kok: Jephuru omo chwrairokno pusinani phayo, aro wngkha tei mungsa kaisa-uarma-khropsarok-jotto gana thangma kwrwi.
en: When it comes to raising children, there is no one-size-fits-all approach.

kok: Jotto chwrai no pherlayo, tei tamo kaisa nukhungni bagwi samungrok khaiphano tei kaisa ni bagwi khaigwlak.
en: Every child is different, and what works for one family may not work for another.

kok: Haiphano, aro baksa sosol raidarok je mapharokno tongthok, sakdukma, tei khlaimanma chwrairokno pusinani chubaimano.
en: However, there are some general principles that can help parents raise happy, healthy, and successful children.

kok: Kaisa ah jotto nangkukma manwirok mapharok khai manma wngkha kaisa kwrak halokbokma bohrokni chwrairokbai songchama bwkhak.
en: One of the most important things parents can do is to establish a strong relationship with their children.

kok: Omo wngkha thansa khe jora katilaimani, bohrokbai koksamani, tei bohrok bai khwnamani.
en: This means spending time together, talking to them, and listening to them.

kok: Omoni kokmangrok tangbwtang arirok tei ari bomanirok, tei bohrokno kwthajak uwngrwmani.
en: It also means setting limits and boundaries, and enforcing them consistently.

kok: Jephuru chwrairok saimano borokni thani tamo khakajak, bohrok teibo ahaino tongraida gothokjak bwkhak wngkha.
en: When children know what is expected of them, they are more likely to behave appropriately.

kok: Tei kaisa nangkukma bwchwlwi wngkhaa chwrairokni pusinani wngkha bohrokno khathansa kahai phwrwngma bagwi.
en: Another important factor in raising children is to teach them about consent.

kok: Omo kokmanagrok bohrokno phwrwngnanai je bohrokni thani manthai tongo jesano phano ehe hinnani je bohrok nana muchungya no, tei bohrok ah kubunrokni manthairokno borom rina nango haino kaham khai ehe hwnwi sana bwkhak.
en: This means teaching them that they have the right to say no to anything they don't want to do, and that they should respect the rights of others to say no as well.

kok: Omo wngkha khaisa nangkukma porirem je chwrairokno bohrok saksakno katirwna satokma tei samung phwnangmani simi.
en: This is an important lesson that will help children protect themselves from abuse and exploitation.

kok: Paithago, mapharok bohrokni chwrairokni bagwi tangmung naidalrok wngna nango.
en: Finally, parents need to be role models for their children.

kok: Chwrairok siklarokno naimani swrwngo bohrokni langmarokni bising, aswkno omo wngkha nangkukma je mapharok tongraida kaisa lama bising je bohrok bohrokni chwrairokni bataima bwkha nango.
en: Children learn by watching the adults in their lives, so it is important that parents behave in a way that they want their children to emulate.

kok: Omo kokmangrok tongham, boromjak, tei bokjak wngjak .
en: This means being honest, respectful, and responsible.

kok: Mwsamung wngkha kaisa sakmang rikmung je ninangrimung twih swbaikhrubwi sama wngkha.
en: Dance is a form of art that is expressed through movement.

kok: Omo saichung eba bodolrokni bising khlai phaijak bo mano, tei omo kothomarok sana bwkha phwnangjak mano, khanangmarok swbaikhrubwi sama, eba khakepleng bwkhak kaisa naithok saimanma ah nainaini bagwi swnamo.
en: It can be performed solo or in groups, and it can be used to tell stories, express emotions, or simply to create a beautiful experience for the audience.

kok: Mwsamung sai bisrok karwi yaksiyagra tongwi tongo, tei omo hating sakao jotto hukumu bising loi khalajak phaikha.
en: Dance has been around for thousands of years, and it has been practiced in every culture on Earth.

kok: Aro kwbangma juda juda mwsamung sapokthaihrok tongo, omoni sak solya laihbuma tei tongdal bai thwgwi.
en: There are many different types of dance, each with its own unique history and style.

kok: Baksa ha jottoni slai luku hamjakjak sapokthaihrok mwsama khobjakha ballet, kwtal mwsamung, hip hop, tei tap mwsamung.
en: Some of the most popular types of dance include ballet, modern dance, hip hop, and tap dance.

kok: Mwsamung kaisa sakno twywi tangmung wngwi mano, phiya omo kaisa khaphang tei khanangjakma bo wngwi manu.
en: Dance can be a physical activity, but it is also a mental and emotional one.

kok: Jephuru nwng mwsao, nwng nini sak no sakbaithang swbaikhrubwi sama kaisa lama bising je kokthairok manya bwkha phwnangmani wngkha.
en: When you dance, you are using your body to express yourself in a way that words cannot.

kok: Nwng ah rwchapmung tei kubun mwsanairok bai manjumani bo wngkha kaisa lama bising je belai phangwnang wngwi mano.
en: You are also connecting with the music and the other dancers in a way that can be very powerful.

kok: Mwsama kwbangma manmarirok manwi mano khorok tei sak kanwini bagwi.
en: Dance can have many benefits for both the mind and the body.

kok: Omo nini cardiovascular sakdukma, mothok khairina, tei nini sak-khaberamung bangrwimano.
en: It can improve your cardiovascular health, reduce stress, and increase your self-confidence.

kok: Omo kaisa kotorkuar lama bwkhak kwtal borok tei bayaprok swnamma bwkhak bo mano.
en: It can also be a great way to meet new people and make friends.

kok: Tumungno nwng mwsama chaitokmani bising ol manjak wngkha, aro wngkha kwbangma bumukrok manthokma bwkhak nono chubana chengjak mano.
en: If you are interested in trying dance, there are many resources available to help you get started.

kok: Aro wngkha rwngremrok jotto homanrok saimanjak bagwi, tei aro wngkha kwbangma bijaprok tei DVDs je nwng sakbaithang phwrwngma bwkhak phwnang mano.
en: There are classes for all levels of experience, and there are also many books and DVDs that you can use to teach yourself.

kok: Loi hamya wngkha kaisa kutuk tongmung, abo khoroksa borokni langmao swbaithotok swlaimung tubuimanw.
en: Addiction is a complex condition that can have a devastating impact on a person's life.

kok: Oboni wngmung chaya haiphano kaisa tongraida eba manuio kubulnani nangsuknai aboni nangmabai yasi kaijago.
en: It is characterized by a compulsive need to engage in a behavior or substance despite negative consequences.

kok: Kephek manuini loihamya, chuarakni loihamya, yapha bumani loihamya, tei sakmotokni loihamyano khobwi kwbangma dalni loi hamya tongo.
en: There are many different types of addiction, including drug addiction, alcohol addiction, gambling addiction, and sex addiction.

kok: Loi hamya jeba borokni bisingo nukjagwimanw, boh jesa umor, bosong, sir eba hoda ranghalok tongmungni phano wngthun.
en: Addiction can develop in anyone, regardless of age, race, gender, or socioeconomic status.

kok: Haikhe, obohai kisaswk pher tongo jebo khoroksa borokni loi hamyani kiringmung bangrwimanw, romdi bosong rwgwi, khapangni bemar, tei tongkhorni pher.
en: However, there are certain factors that can increase a person's risk of addiction, such as genetics, mental health problems, and environmental factors.

kok: Loi hamya wngkha kaisa kuduk bemar, tei oboni mungsa hammung kwrwi.
en: Addiction is a chronic disease, and there is no cure.

kok: Haikhe, borokrokno bohrokni loi hamyani yokthani tei sakhalok kaham, kaham kwrwngkhe thangwi tongthani chubaui mannnai abohai saknaimungni chajak lambo tongo.
en: However, there are effective treatments available that can help people to overcome their addiction and live healthy, productive lives.

kok: Loi hamyani bagwi saknaimungni jottonisai chajak lam wngkha bithi tei therapy-ni dalokjak lam.
en: The most effective treatment for addiction is a combination of medication and therapy.

kok: Bithi, muchungma tei karmungni sinimarino holirwthani simi chubauimanw, yang therapy hinkhe borokrokno loi hamya phaising twlangnai abohai jwngjalrokno paiswkmungo chubauimanw.
en: Medication can help to reduce cravings and symptoms of withdrawal, while therapy can help people to address the underlying issues that led to their addiction.

kok: Loi hamyani simi hamwi phaimung wngkha langma kwrwngwini samung, tei obohai jorabo phayo jephuru borokrok choba khwlainani nang thango.
en: Recovery from addiction is a lifelong process, and there will be times when people struggle.

kok: Haikhe, kaham chubachuni bisingtwi, loi hamyano mechenwi, kaham kwrwng, tongthok chahthokni langma ajiuimanw.
en: However, with the right support, it is possible to overcome addiction and achieve a healthy, happy life.

kok: Tumung nwng eba nini sinijak kebo loi hamyabai choba khwlai tongkhe, chubachu manthogo.
en: If you or someone you know is struggling with addiction, there is help available.

kok: Chubachuni bagwi khoroksa tangdal kwrwngbai gwdaldi.
en: Please reach out to a professional for help.

kok: Tongthokmungungka kaisa tongrem kaham-wngjak tei khapungmung.
en: Happiness is a state of well-being and contentment.

kok: Omo uramuram kubui khanangjakrok bai gwdaljak wngkha ahaino hamjakma, tongthok, tei hansuthai.
en: It is often associated with positive emotions such as love, joy, and gratitude.

kok: Aro kwbangma manwirok tongo je tongthokmung, hamjakma borokrok bai runghalokrok khobmani, kokmang samung, tei kaisa sinai simanwi naimung bwkhak rwui mano.
en: There are many things that can contribute to happiness, including relationships with loved ones, meaningful work, and a sense of purpose.

kok: Haiphano, omo mari bwkhak nangkukma wngkha je tongthokmung homnino kaisa tongphinai tongremya.
en: However, it is important to note that happiness is not always a constant state.

kok: Omo ninangjakmano chini tonghalokrok tei simarirok sakbokmani sakao.
en: It can fluctuate depending on our circumstances and experiences.

kok: Haini bagwi chini langmarokni bising tongthokmung chuaima bwkhak lamaarok naitukna bwkhak omo nangkukma wngkha, ahaino jephuru manwirok kuthuk wngo.
en: That is why it is important to find ways to cultivate happiness in our lives, even when things are tough.

kok: Kaisa lama omo khaina bwkhak wngkha manwirok sakao naisikma bwkhak je chini bagwi nangkukma tei chwng kaham wansukma swnamna bwkhak.
en: One way to do this is to focus on the things that are important to us and that make us feel good.

kok: Tei kaisa lama wngkha hamsuthai wngma bwkhak chini thani tamo tongma tei chini langmarok bising borok chajakma karwi.
en: Another way is to be grateful for what we have and to appreciate the people in our lives.

kok: Paithago, oh hayung bising kaisa pherlaimung swnamma bwkhak lama naitukna bwkhak omo nangkukma wngkha, ahaino tumung omo mungsaswk chikon wngkha.
en: Finally, it is important to find ways to make a difference in the world, even if it is something small.

kok: Jephuru chwng wansukma kahai kaisa pherlaimung swnammani wngkha, omo chwngno kaisa sinai simanwi naimung tei kokmang rwimano, bomo chini jottoi tongthokmung bwkhak bagwi mano.
en: When we feel like we are making a difference, it can give us a sense of purpose and meaning, which can contribute to our overall happiness.

kok: Kaisa samung habar bising ah kokmwkhang wngkha, khoroksa daginai kaisa nangkukma tanmung tangwimano sebukrokno tongthokmung rwnani bwkhak.
en: In the context of a work environment, a boss can play a significant role in contributing to employee happiness.

kok: Kaisa nangmani tei buchinai daginai kaisa kubui samung habar swnammano borok sebuk thinang morokma tei borom rwjak wansukmano.
en: A supportive and understanding boss can create a positive work environment where employees feel valued and respected.

kok: Omo thaihmung bahngrwma tei samung khapungmung bwkhak dagimano, amo sebuk tongthokmug bwkhak samung tangwimano.
en: This can lead to increased productivity and job satisfaction, which can in turn contribute to employee happiness.

kok: "Khoroksa isri wngmani kokmung tamo?" ah bwrwima sikli swngkha.
en: "What is the meaning of becoming a queen?" asked the young woman.

kok: "omo wngkha kokrwnglaimung bwkhak swrwngma wngkha abo jotto wngkha, " ah bwrwichwk sakha.
en: "It is to learn to accommodate all that is," said the old woman.

kok: "Nini khani bising romchrepma bwkhak Naithok tei ah sakdukhu nini bwkhak bising romchrepma, ah tongthok tei khanangma, ah pohor tei ah mwnakma. Ah hayungno amo haikhe naisikma bwkhak, tei omono haiphano hamjakma bwkhak."
en: "To hold in your heart the beauty and the pain, the joy and the sorrow, the light and the darkness.To see the world as it is, and to love it nonetheless."

kok: "Phiya ang abo bahaikhe khai mannai?" ah bwrwima sikli swngkha. "Ah hayung wngkha aswkno dukhumanmani kuplung."
en: "But how can I do that?" asked the young woman. "The world is so full of suffering."

kok: "In', omo wngkha, " ah bwrwichwk sakha.
en: "Yes, it is," said the old woman.

kok: "Phiya omo bo naithok kuplung wngkha. Tei omo ah dukhu manma bising ah naithok naitukma bwkhak chini samung wngkha, tei omo chwngno swlaina rwkha.
en: "But it is also full of beauty. And it is our task to find the beauty in the suffering, and to let it transform us.

kok: "Jephuru nwng khoroksa isri wngo, nini thani phan tongnai.
en: "When you become a queen, you will have power.

kok: Phiya phan kaisa manwiya je nini sakni manna bagwi phwnangjakma wngo.
en: But power is not a thing to be used for your own gain.

kok: Omo wngkha kaisa bokjakmung ah kaham kubunrokni bagwi phwnangjakma wngo.
en: It is a responsibility to be used for the good of others.

kok: Nwng nini phanno phwnangna bwkhak swrwngna nango ah hayung hamrwna bwkhak, amono chaya khaiya bwkhak.
en: You must learn to use your power to heal the world, not to harm it.

kok: Nwng kwchangtoktok wngna bwkhak bo ma swrwngnai.
en: You must also learn to be humble.

kok: Khoroksa isri kubunrokni sakao boya, phiya bo bohrokni tolao boya."
en: A queen is not above others, but she is also not below them."

kok: Ah sengkrak sikla ah chobaha sakao kwlaijak, bini babai bising kaisa kwsani simi thwi kurukmani.
en: The young soldier lay on the battlefield, bleeding from a wound in his side.

kok: Bo ah nokha sakha naisikha tei ah chumuirok buprai laima, tei bini sakao sal chwngmani.
en: He looked up at the sky and saw the clouds scudding past, and the sun shining down on him.

kok: Bo bini aoli bagwi wansukkha, tei ah chahthai bo pogwi phano teisa chaliya, tei ah borok bo teisa nukliya.
en: He thought of his home town, and the food he would never eat again, and the people he would never see again.

kok: Bo bini mokolrok kholobakha tei kaisa surimung sakha.
en: He closed his eyes and said a prayer.

kok: Kaisa swrapsa olo, bo kaisa khorang khwnakha "nwng kaham da" ah sengkrak bini mokol khulukha tei khoroksa bwrai bini sakao bachamani nukha.
en: A moment later, he heard a voice "Are you all right" The soldier opened his eyes and saw a woman standing over him.

kok: Bo kuchuk tei steni kolok wngkha, khwnai kosom kolok tei kwkhwrang mokolrok bai.
en: She was tall and slender, with long black hair and green eyes.

kok: Bo kaisa bukur chumri tei leggings kanjak wngkha, tei bini babai digi kaisa bini seng tongo "ang ang theekno, " ah sengrak sakha "nwng dukhu manjak, " ah bwrwima sakha "ano nono chubana rwdi" ah bwrwima ah sengrakno bini yethek bwkhak chubakha.
en: She was wearing a leather tunic and leggings, and she had a sword at her side "I'mI'm okay," the soldier said "You're hurt," the woman said "Let me help you" The woman helped the soldier to his feet.

kok: Bo bini dulai karikha tei bini yaksiyagra amo khlopma ah thwih kurukma mwthakna bwkhak.
en: She took off her cloak and wrapped it around him to stop the bleeding.

kok: Hwnkhe bo bono kaisa aoli ganabai bwkhak twlangkha.
en: Then she led him to a nearby town.

kok: Ah aoil chikon tei siring wngkha.
en: The town was small and quiet.

kok: Ah borokrok bayapjakma wngkha, tei bohrok ah sengkrakno chahthai tei tongna bwkhak kaisa thaih rwkha.
en: The people were friendly, and they gave the soldier food and a place to stay.

kok: Ah bwrwima bobai tongkha, tei bo bono hamrwna bwkha chubakha.
en: The woman stayed with him, and she helped him to heal.

kok: Rangchakni bolongo, kubuisimungni samung kwrwngrok tongbayo.
en: In the forests of gold, there lived a people who were skilled in the ways of science.

kok: Bohrok sal tei nobarni phan no yachagwi narwkna rwngo, bohrok bohrokni ukti no elements no phanpainai abotwi samungo chuknai manwi swnamlayo.
en: They had learned to harness the power of the sun and the wind, and they used their knowledge to build reliable structures that would withstand the elements.

kok: Salsa, bwrwi sikli mung Lawita bolongo himwi thang tongphuru bo siniya-nukya manwi kaisa nukha.
en: One day, a young woman named Lawita was walking in the forest when she came across a strange object.

kok: Abo rangchakni swnamjak, tei abo kubun manwirogbai kisa phano solya.
en: It was made of gold, and it was unlike anything she had ever seen before.

kok: Bo nogo twlangwi thangkha, hakhe bo boni okrarogno phunugwi kha.
en: She took it home with her, and she showed it to her elders.

kok: O manwi no nugwi bohrok pal manjak liya, phiya bohrok gosewi nalai kha abo belai samungo chuknai manwi se hwnwi.
en: They were puzzled by the object, but they agreed that it was something of great importance.

kok: Bohrok Lawita no dholi o rohor kha o manwino twywi saiman nai abotwi borokno rutukna bagwi.
en: They decided to send Lawita to the city to find someone who could tell them more about it.

kok: Lawita dholi o thang kha, hakhe bo khoroksa elem gwngang borok bai malai kha mung khe Thoth
en: Lawita traveled to the city, and she met with a wise man named Thoth.

kok: Abo wng kha athukirini phan no yachagwi man nai abotwi manwqise hwnwi Thoth sa'ui khwna rw kha.
en: Thoth was able to tell her that the object was a tool that could be used to harness the power of the stars.

kok: Abo wngkha kaisa mwtaini hiyali se hwnwi Thoth bono sakha, tei samung kaham o thepajaknai manwi se hwnwi.
en: He told her that it was a gift from the gods, and that it was meant to be used for good.

kok: Lawita belai tonthokjak kha amohai hiyali no manwi, tei bo swmai tang kha abobai hus khe samung tangnani.
en: Lawita was honored to receive such a gift, and she vowed to use it wisely.

kok: Bo boni borokrokni thani khiphilwi thang phi kha, hakhe bo bohrokno phwrwng kha bahai khe o manwi bai samung tangnai.
en: She returned to her people, and she taught them how to use the tool.

kok: Nelson Mandela wngkha khoroksa South African anti-apartheid pekhrupnai wngkha, thwngrwngrwk ojama, tei bohrok hamajaknai je puila South Africa kosom kasku naikani khainai wngkha 1994 simi 1999 jora.
en: Nelson Mandela is a South African anti-apartheid revolutionary, political leader, and philanthropist who served as the first black president of South Africa from 1994 to 1999.

kok: Bo kaisa jottoni slai nangkukma sakdukrok hayung laihbuma bising kotorma nahartongjakma wngkha.
en: He is widely regarded as one of the most significant figures in world history.

kok: Madela 1918 o Mvezo, South Africa bising achaikha.
en: Mandela was born in 1918 in Mvezo, South Africa.

kok: Bo kaisa kamini bising torkha tei bo kaisa tongkhthar raida pinnok rwngnok bwkhak rwngjak wngkha.
en: He grew up in a rural village and was educated at a Methodist mission school.

kok: Kuchuk rwngnokni olom bo ah Rwngnokyung Fort Hare bwkhak kerong porikha.
en: After high school, he studied law at the University of Fort Hare.

kok: 1994 o, bo ah African National Congress(ANC) manjukha, kaisa thwngrwngrwk motharok je apartheid kebengwi bulaimani chobakhaimani wngkha.
en: In 1944, he joined the African National Congress (ANC), a political organization that was fighting against apartheid.

kok: Mandela bini thwngrwngrwk samung-humung bagwi 1962 o romjakha tei along bising langma paithak jora chopjakha.
en: Mandela was arrested for his political activities in 1962 and sentenced to life in prison.

kok: Bo alongni bising 27 bisirok katikha, bobo wngjora bo kaisa mari wngkha ah anti-apartheid ninangrimung babai.
en: He spent 27 years in prison, during which time he became a symbol of the anti-apartheid movement.

kok: 1990 o, Mandela alongni simi phiyokjakha tei 1994 o South Africa ni kasku chongjakha.
en: In 1990, Mandela was released from prison and elected president of South Africa in 1994.

kok: iko kasku, Mandela South Africa no thansa khaina bwkhak samung tangkha tei kosomrok tei kuphurokni kwcharo millirwphinani remtisamung wngkha.
en: As president, Mandela worked to unite South Africa and promote reconciliation between blacks and whites.

kok: Bo ah paithak apartheid bo naikolkha tei kaisa lukuchongraidarwk haphang bwkha swlaijakmani tongo.
en: He also oversaw the end of apartheid and the transition to a democratic government.

kok: Mandela khoroksa borokkoto kwchangtotok yakpai boromgnang koklopnai wngkha tei gilama kubun boromrok sokat rwjakha.
en: Mandela is a Nobel Peace Prize laureate and has been awarded numerous other honors.

kok: Doyung wngkha belai kuar, sahorjak rajakhor, langma bai tangphan kupulung.
en: The city was a vast, sprawling metropolis, full of life and energy.

kok: Abo mohai thai wngkha aro jesaphano wngmano, tei jotto imang mukthang khaimano.
en: It was a place where anything was possible, and where dreams could come true.

kok: Haiphano jotto borokni bagwi je doyungo khwlaimanjak hai naituk manmani, aro teibo kwbangma tongo je biyalwi swnamjagwi paithago malaimani.
en: But for every person who found success in the city, there were many more who struggled to make ends meet.

kok: Mohai borokrok bosti o tongo, chikon nokbwsao je uramuram belai keseplai tei swnam manya thayo tongjao.
en: These people lived in the slums, in tiny apartments that were often overcrowded and in disrepair.

kok: Bohrok kwdwkma tamwi samung khwlayo hacher rwmabai, tei bohrok yaphang nangmani bade chamung tei sakham naikini khainai karwi uramuram khe ma thango.
en: They worked long hours for low pay, and they often had to go without basic necessities like food and healthcare.

kok: Sikli bwrwi borok khoroksa mung Amelia hwnwi tong.
en: One such person was a young woman named Amelia.

kok: Bo imango kotor nugwi doyungo ma phaikha, haiphano bo daktino saimankha je bo wansukmani abo kubuio belai juda.
en: She had come to the city with big dreams, but she quickly found that reality was much different than she had imagined.

kok: Bo kaisa chikonsa diner o waitressni samung khwlayo, tei bo bini nokchorai suna bagwi bebabagwi nangmaswk rang ajio.
en: She worked as a waitress in a small diner, and she could barely make enough money to pay her rent.

kok: Bo uramuram khe oakhui bisna thangjao, tei bo homnino bini thinangno twi wanachinta wngjak.
en: She often went to bed hungry, and she was always worried about her future.

kok: Salsa, Amelia bini samungni nogo himwi thangphuru bo khoroksa chwla no achuthayo achujak nukha.
en: One day, Amelia was walking home from work when she saw a man sitting on a bench.

kok: Bo tongthai sara, tei bo kaisa mari romjak je sao, "Chwng chamung ni bagwi samung khwlayo." Amelia ah chwla ni bagwi markhe khairokjak, tei bo bono sandwich pairinai hwnwi chongwi nakha.
en: He was homeless, and he was holding a sign that said, "Will work for food." Amelia felt sorry for the man, and she decided to buy him a sandwich.

kok: Bo ah chwla bai kok sai tongphuru, bo bini mung Charlie hwnwi saimankha.
en: As she was talking to the man, she learned that his name was Charlie.

kok: Kokpaihjakya bisingkokrok ah lukuni wansukmani bisirarokni bagwi romjak tongkha.
en: Unsolved mysteries have captured the public's imagination for centuries.

kok: Amelai Earhart kwmamani simi ah Jack the Ripper sinirwma bwkhak, oh dorbakamungrok chwngno uanamasingsa bai yakarkha kubuio tamo wngkha.
en: From the disappearance of Amelia Earhart to the identity of Jack the Ripper, these cases have left us wondering what really happened.

kok: Jephuru baksa oh bisingnikokrok ulo phano kokpaihjakya wngmano, bohrok choyai chwngno muani khlaima bwkhak tamnihinba bohrok kaisa philiksa yapharo ah siniyani bising.
en: While some of these mysteries may never be solved, they continue to fascinate us because they offer a glimpse into the unknown.

kok: Kaisa jottoni slai mungkoto kokpaihjakya bisingkorok wngkha ah Amelia Earhart kwmamani.
en: One of the most famous unsolved mysteries is the disappearance of Amelia Earhart.

kok: Earhart wngkha khoroksa American aviator je puila bwrwima saichung birinai wngkha ah Atlantic twijlang naro.
en: Earhart was an American aviator who became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean.

kok: 1937 o, bo khaisa ah-hayung-yaksiyagra birmung saka phatar kaihma phunuknai Fred Noonan bai.
en: In 1937, she set out on an around-the-world flight with navigator Fred Noonan.

kok: July 2, 1937o ah Pacific twijlang sakao mangnwi kwmakha, tei bohrokni talika tongmarok saimanyakhu.
en: The pair disappeared over the Pacific Ocean on July 2, 1937, and their fate remains unknown.

kok: Earhart tei Noonanni logi tamo wngkha aboni bagwi kwbangma kokbwkrairok tongo.
en: There are many theories about what happened to Earhart and Noonan.

kok: Baksa poito khayo je bohrok ah twijlang bising baikhrubkha, jephuru kubunrok poito khayo je bohrok ah Japanese rokbai romjakha hwnwi.
en: Some believe that they crashed into the ocean, while others believe that they were captured by the Japanese.

kok: Tabukbo kubunrok poito khayo je bohrok uansuksukma kwmakha lukuni mokolni bising yokna bwkhak.
en: Still others believe that they deliberately disappeared in order to escape the public eye.

kok: Oh Earthart ni kwmamani bisingkok ah yaktoljak bijaprok, koksoprok, tei swijakphunukmarok wngkha.
en: The mystery of Earhart's disappearance has been the subject of books, articles, and documentaries.

kok: 2017 o, khoroksa rutukrwk thwngdolrok sakhlaikha je bohrok yakumu mankha je Earhartni plane baikhrubkha kaisa hachal twihathaih ah Pacific twijlang bising.
en: In 2017, a team of researchers announced that they had found evidence that Earhart's plane crashed on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean.

kok: Vimes khorok mihimjagwi tongmani wngkha.
en: Vimes was having a headache.

kok: Omo wngkha ah khorok mihimma kahai je nono nini khwnai chirna bwkhka muchungma swnamop, eba mukhuisa kaisa sakkrwrakma kokthaima koktun ah swnamarok bwkhak jesaphano omo wngkha je nono khorokmihima rwkha ah puila thaini bising.
en: It was the kind of headache that made you want to tear your hair out, or at least write a strongly worded letter to the makers of whatever it was that had given you the headache in the first place.

kok: Oh tonghalok bising, ah khorok mihima kaisa chongjakma samung bwkak chaitokmani sal thaihmung wngkha.
en: In this case, the headache was the result of a particularly trying day at work.

kok: Vimes kaisa bwtang kwbang khokmungni bagwi naitukmung khlaitongmani, tei bo matongkha boh mungsathayo sowgwiliya hwnwi.
en: Vimes had been investigating a series of robberies, and he was starting to feel like he was getting nowhere.

kok: Boh lengjakha, bo khabaihjakha, tei boh haino nogo thangna tei hatibarsa ni bagwi thuna muchungjakha.
en: He was tired, he was frustrated, and he just wanted to go home and sleep for a week.

kok: iko bo bini tangkhor bwkhak phirogwi himwi thangkheno, Vimes kaisa chikonsa switwi akorok phalnok laikha.
en: As he was walking back to his office, Vimes passed a small stationery shop.

kok: Ah tailamni bising, bo kaisa mari nukha ha sakha "kahamkuk koktunrok ah doyungni bising".
en: In the window, he saw a sign that said "Best Letters in the City".

kok: Vimes bathakkha tei kaisa mukphliksani bagwi mari bai chengkha.
en: Vimes stopped and stared at the sign for a moment.

kok: Bo bini khorok mihimma bagwi wansukha, tei bo jotto ah koktunrok bo swina bwkhak nangma bagwi wansukkha.
en: He thought about his headache, and he thought about all the letters he had to write.

kok: Bo hamakolo nakha tei ah phalno bising thangkha.
en: He sighed and went into the shop.

kok: Ah phalnok wngkha jotto rwngremrok switwi akorok yaktummarok bai kuplung wngkha.
en: The shop was full of all sorts of stationery supplies.

kok: Aro swikongrok, phangswikongrok, tei swilaih, kholopnairok, stamprok, tei ahaino kisa taipni kolrok tongjak.
en: There were pens, pencils, paper, envelopes, stamps, and even a few typewriters.

kok: Obobo Kubui kok o hayungni tonghalok kwthang tongkho je jottonino chermung bata'ui sana nayo, wngmungrokbo aswkse kirimasingsa tei wanamasingsa abohrok imang hamya rogo nukjakphayo.
en: It is true that there exist in this world situations that defy all explanation, events so strange and wondrous that they seem to be the stuff of dreams or nightmares.

kok: Obohaino kaisa kothoma ang norokno sanani nayo, kaisa wanaphan tei kaisa siniya-nukya wngma abo khulukjak sinai jephuru bohrok hayungni bwskango pehel rwjaganw.
en: Such is the case with the story I am about to tell you, a tale of supernatural forces and the strange events that unfolded when they were unleashed upon the world.

kok: Obo jottono horsani bisingono chengkha, jephuru kaisa kiching bodol kuthumlayo kaisa tongthokmungni bagwi.
en: It all began one night, when a group of friends were gathered together for a party.

kok: Bohrok aphuru nwnglaiwi tei mwnwilaiwi, thongthoklaiwi kaisa tei kaisa tongmani atomsa chati thwi paikha.
en: They were drinking and laughing, enjoying each other's company, when suddenly the lights went out.

kok: Ah nok khotol mwnakbai koboljak wngwi thangkha, tei kaisa khorang hama nalaima simino khwnaui tongsio.
en: The room was plunged into darkness, and the only sound was the sound of their own breathing.

kok: Hwnkhe, mwnak bisingo, bohrok kaisa wanamasingsa pohor chwngsaui tongma nukha.
en: Then, in the darkness, they saw it: a strange, glowing light.

kok: Obo ganaginino phaikhwna hwnwi tongkha, tei obo chwngma teibo se chwngprabwi phayo.
en: It seemed to be coming from nowhere, and it was growing brighter and brighter.

kok: Kichingsong kirijaklaikha, phiya bohrok sinanibo muchungjago.
en: The friends were terrified, but they were also curious.

kok: Bohrok sinani muchungjagkha o pohorle tamo tei obo boroni phai hwnwi.
en: They wanted to know what this light was, and where it was coming from.

kok: Twrwk twrwk, bohrok pohorni ganao thanglaikha.
en: Slowly, they approached the light.

kok: Jephuru bohrok ganao sogwio, bohrok nukha obo kaisa chikonsa holong kwchwngni se pohor phayo.
en: As they got closer, they could see that it was coming from a small, glowing sphere.

kok: Ah holong nobaro uriui tongo, tei obo chwnamung bai kitingjak.
en: The sphere was hovering in the air, and it was surrounded by a faint aura.

kok: Mwnwi kothok mangpilirok tei videos wngkha kaisa dime chwnwi oh salrogo, phiya baksa haino bohrok kubunrokni slai juda khai nukjago.
en: Funny pictures and videos are a dime a dozen these days, but some of them stand out from the rest.

kok: Omo wngkha kaisarok je aswkno solaijak eba khapchaya je bohrok chwng chirikgwi mwnwi rio.
en: These are the ones that are so relatable or absurd that they make us laugh out loud.

kok: Kaisa phunukmari thangnai video je viral thangmani kaisa aming bakso chikonsa wo habna chaitok tongmani.
en: One example is a recent video that went viral of a cat trying to fit into a small box.

kok: Ah aming sraisrai khai kaphramung wngwi tongo, phiya omo chaitogwi tongo, tei jotto manwi wngkha haino aswkno mwnwi kothok.
en: The cat is clearly struggling, but it keeps trying, and the whole thing is just so funny.

kok: Tei kaissa phunukmari wngkha kaisa mangpili kaisa swi thupi kanmani je omoni bagwi belai kotorma.
en: Another example is a picture of a dog wearing a hat that is way too big for it.

kok: Ah swi aswkno mwnwijaknaai nukjak tongo je omono mwnwina bwkhak wngmaya.
en: The dog looks so ridiculous that it's impossible not to laugh.

kok: Omtwi sapukthaih mwnwi kothok mangpilirok tei videos wngkha uramuram hodarwk pinlam bakjago, tei bohrok daktino kaisa "meme" wngwi mano meme wngkha kaisa mwnwikothok mangpili, video, eba soibijap ni lapsa je solaijak tei online o bakjakmani.
en: These types of funny pictures and videos are often shared on social media, and they can quickly become a "meme" A meme is a humorous image, video, or piece of text that is copied and shared online.

kok: Memes uramuram sinijak mangpilirok eba kokthaihthuprok phwnangjakma, tei bohrok swbaikhrubwi sama bai kuar bwtrang khanangjakrokni bwkhak phwnangjak mano.
en: Memes often use familiar images or phrases, and they can be used to express a wide range of emotions.

kok: Kaisa manwwi je ma wngnai jephuru kaisa mwnwi kothok mangpili eba video viral wngo je amo kubunrokbai bakjakmani.
en: One thing that must happen when a funny picture or video goes viral is that it is shared with others.

kok: Omo ni bagwi memes belai luku hamjakma swnamjago.
en: This is what makes memes so popular.

kok: Bohrok nugo kaisa mwnwi kothok mangpili eba vidio, tei bohrok abono bohrokni bayaprok bai bakna muchungjago aswkno je bohrok bo mwnwi manai hwnwi.
en: People see a funny picture or video, and they want to share it with their friends so that they can laugh too.

kok: Haini bagwi memes daktino internet ayang naro auaima wngmano.
en: This is why memes can spread so quickly across the internet.

kok: Kaisa jora kolok wngthahng bising, aro kaisa mokolnukya bikha birnai tongo je ah haching takmani rikmung kubui phunukmani bai bini tongmani swnamo.
en: In a time long past, there lived a blind beggar who made his living by demonstrating the art of soil sculpting.

kok: Bo ah lahar kuna o achugo, bini kolrok tei manwi-khwnwirok bai kitingjak, tei laithangnai rokno kwcharo bono samung khaima naima bwkhak.
en: He would sit on the street corner, surrounded by his tools and materials, and invite passersby to watch him work.

kok: Bini kwrwng yasirok bai, bo ah hachingsa no supungma bisingo kubuljak banokmarok, malmatarok swnammani, buphang uaphangrok, tei haino jotto hakungmanirok.
en: With his deft fingers, he would mold the soil into intricate shapes, creating animals, plants, and even entire landscapes.

kok: Bini samung aswk naithok wngkha je omo haikhe sajakha haino ah jottoni slai kwrakkuk ninda khainai ni mokolo phano mwktwrwi tubui mano.
en: His work was so beautiful that it was said to bring tears to the eyes of even the most hardened cynic.

kok: Salsa, khoroksa bwrwima sikli mung Amara ah hati twih himwi thangmani bojora bo ah mokol nukya bikha birnaino nukha.
en: One day, a young woman named Amara was walking through the market when she saw the blind beggar.

kok: Bo daktino bini samung bai kwlwkkhaa, tei bo kaisa kwdwkma jora karwi bono naina bwkhak bathakkha.
en: She was immediately captivated by his work, and she stopped to watch him for a long time.

kok: Jephuru bo paikha, bo bini thani agukkha tei swngkha tumungno bo bahaikhe hachingsa takma swrwng mano.
en: When he was finished, she approached him and asked if she could learn how to sculpt soil.

kok: Ah bikha birnai mwnwikha tei bono sakah je bo bono phwrwngma bwkhak tongthoknai.
en: The beggar smiled and told her that he would be happy to teach her.

kok: Amara ah tei kisa hatibarok ah bikha birnai ni thani swrwngmani simi katikha.
en: Amara spent the next few weeks learning from the beggar.

kok: Bo bono ah yaphang hachingsa takmani phwrwngkham tei bo bono phunukha bahaikhe juda juda banokmarok tei taknairok swnamkha.
en: He taught her the basics of soil sculpting, and he showed her how to create different shapes and textures.

kok: Amara wngkha khoroksa dakti swrwngnai, tei bo daktino ah rikmung belai yaksrai wngkha.
en: Amara was a quick learner, and she soon became very skilled at the art.

kok: Salsa, ah bikha birnai Amara no sakhaa je amo bini yaksrairok kubui phunukma bwkhak bini bagwi jora wngkha.
en: One day, the beggar told Amara that it was time for her to demonstrate her skills.

kok: Teiwaisa swnamphimani kaisa mal tangraida je tongkhor no katirwui chubanarok tei habar khatima bumukrok.
en: Recycling is a vital process that helps to protect the environment and conserve natural resources.

kok: Teiwaisa swnamphimani bai, chwng khibijak rangmari khairiwui mano je hakorsupungmarok bwkhak thangmani tei soknanini rok, phan khatima, tei rang khatirwma.
en: By recycling, we can reduce the amount of waste that goes to landfills and incinerators, conserve energy, and save money.

kok: Teiwaisa swnamphimani tongraida chengmarok wngkha teiwaisa swnamanaijat manwi-khwnwi rok thummani bai.
